issues.title: Single-executable self-hosting: compiling the Node prod server with bun build --compile (umbrella + one design question)
issues.body:
### What I'm trying to do

Ship a vinext app as one relocatable binary for scale-to-zero hosting (Knative), where cold start is
the metric that matters. The approach that needs the fewest moving parts is to compile vinext's own
Node prod server:

```
vinext build
bun build --compile --bytecode --format=esm --minify --compile-autoload-package-json \
  server-entry.mjs dist/server/index.js
```

where `server-entry.mjs` is ~40 lines that call `startProdServer({ outDir, rscEntryPath })` with
paths derived from `process.execPath`, and the app's server bundle is passed as a second entrypoint
so it is embedded (bytecode) rather than loaded from disk.

### What works today (1.0.0-beta.12, Bun 1.4.2)

- The compile succeeds with no plugins or patches (121 vinext runtime modules; with the second
  entrypoint, the app's server JS is served from the binary: deleting all 159 `dist/server/*.js` files
  changes nothing on 10 probed routes).
- The binary serves App and Pages routes, public files, rewrites, `/_next/data`, not-found, and
  prerendered output, because it is the same `startProdServer` path your nightly deploy suite runs.
- On our run of vinext's own `scripts/e2e-deploy.sh` corpus (778 Next.js e2e cases) this shape passes
  746, versus 717 for the same app compiled through the Nitro bun preset. 32 files flip to green, 3 to
  red (all three are the externals caveat below).
- `startProdServer` already accepts `rscEntryPath` / `serverEntryPath`, and `$bunfs` paths work for
  both. So no new API is needed for embedding; documenting those options as stable (#3445's second
  suggestion) is enough.

### The small things that had to be worked around (already filed, listed here so the set is visible)

| | issue |
|---|---|
| generated `server.js` hard-codes `import.meta.dirname` → binary is not relocatable | #3445 |
| generated `server.js` does not default `NODE_ENV=production` → dev React bundle at runtime | #3444 |
| `output: "standalone"` exits before the prerender phase | #3442 |
| standalone dep copier dedupes by name, first come → wrong `react` in a monorepo | #3443 |
| Node prod server ignores `setImageOptimizer()` (serves originals) | #3446 |

None of them needs a design decision; each is a few lines.

### The one design question: opt-in inlining of server externals (this issue)

The remaining failures come from what is NOT in the vite server bundle. vite leaves server
dependencies external (`react`, `react-dom`, `@opentelemetry/*`, `pg`, …) and resolves them from
`node_modules` at runtime. When Bun compiles the binary it re-bundles those externals itself, with
Bun's export conditions, not vite's:

- `react-version` (e2e) fails because `serverFavoringBrowser` / `serverFavoringEdge` resolve to `node`.
- Passing them as `--external` instead breaks boot: an ESM bare import from a `$bunfs` module cannot
  resolve to `node_modules` on disk (`Cannot find package 'react' from '/$bunfs/root/…'`; `NODE_PATH`
  does not help). That part is a Bun limitation, which I'll take to Bun separately.

Proposal: an **opt-in** build option (say `vinext build --inline-server-externals`, or a config key
under the standalone options) that makes vite bundle the server-side externals into
`dist/server/*` with vite's own resolution and conditions. The output would then be self-contained:
no `node_modules` needed at runtime, no second resolver involved, and the compiled binary carries
everything except static client assets. Off by default, so the normal `vinext start` path is
untouched.

Questions for you:
1. Is a single-executable self-hosting shape something you'd accept in the Node prod server path at
   all, or should it wait for the deployment-adapter API (#80) and live as an adapter?
2. If the former, is an opt-in externals-inlining build option acceptable in principle? I'm happy to
   do the PR; I'd rather ask before writing it since it touches the build config.

### Measurements, for context (not the ask)

Local darwin arm64, noisy host, time-to-first-200 over 12 rounds: compiled prod server with the
embedded app bundle 183 ms (health) / 193 ms (SSR), vs 241 / 237 ms for the Nitro-bun binary of the
same app, vs 296 / 434 ms for `bun server.js` uncompiled. On a Kubernetes scale-from-zero A/B
(n=10 each) the two binaries were not separable (p = 0.16), so I'm not claiming a cold-start win
yet; the compat delta above is the solid part.

issues.title: Dev: client optimizeDeps excludes serverExternalPackages, which breaks optional requires in client deps (linkedom → canvas)
issues.body:
vinext 1.0.0-beta.12 (also on main at c4b705e), App Router, Vite 8.3.1.

The client environment's `optimizeDeps.exclude` includes the whole default `serverExternalPackages` list (packages/vinext/src/index.ts, the `client` environment in the App Router config). `canvas` is on that list. A client dependency that requires `canvas` optionally, inside a try/catch, then breaks in `vinext dev`:

linkedom's `commonjs/canvas.cjs`:

```js
try { module.exports = require('canvas'); } catch (fallback) { module.exports = require('./canvas-shim.cjs'); }
```

With `canvas` excluded, the dep optimizer treats it as external and hoists the require into a top-level `import * as m from "canvas"` in `.vite/deps/linkedom.js`. Vite resolves that import to `__vite-optional-peer-dep:canvas:linkedom`, which throws on evaluation, outside the try. Any client module that imports linkedom fails to load:

    Error: Could not resolve "canvas" imported by "linkedom".
        at http://localhost:5174/@id/__vite-optional-peer-dep:canvas:linkedom:2:7

Plain Vite (no exclusion) bundles the optional peer dep inside the try, and the shim is used. `vinext build` is not affected.

Repro: an App Router client component that does `import("linkedom")` in the browser, `canvas` not installed, `vinext dev`.

Workaround: a plugin whose `configEnvironment` hook removes `canvas` from the client environment's `optimizeDeps.exclude`.

Suggested fix: exclude server-external packages from the client optimizer only when they are imported directly from app code, or do not apply the list to packages that are reached only through a dependency's `require`.

issues.title: build: optimize-imports resolveId re-resolution loop on cross-package barrels (radix-ui) under pnpm — [1/5] analyze client references never finishes
issues.body:
## Summary

`vinext build` hangs indefinitely in phase `[1/5] analyze client references` when the app imports the `radix-ui` barrel (standard shadcn/ui code) under a pnpm node_modules layout. `lucide-react` rewrites are fine; the loop is specific to packages whose barrel re-exports **sibling packages** (`radix-ui` → `@radix-ui/*`).

## Reproduction

- Next.js 16.3.3 app, pnpm 11, `vinext@1.0.0-beta.12`, `@vinext/cloudflare@1.0.0-beta.10`, `vite@8.3.1`, `@vitejs/plugin-rsc@0.5.35`
- shadcn components with `import { Slot } from "radix-ui"` (~30 files, standard shadcn/ui pattern)
- `vinext build` → phase 1 never completes (45+ min, ~100% CPU, hundreds of thousands of `resolve_id` calls)

## Instrumented evidence

I patched `dist/plugins/optimize-imports.js` with counters:

```
[OI-STATS] transforms=2714 (plateaued) resolveIds=11928 (climbing ~600/15s)
  src 11648x @radix-ui/react-slot
  src 32x @opentelemetry/api
```

All modules transform exactly once; `resolveId` for `@radix-ui/react-slot` alone fires 11k+ times and grows without bound.

## Suspected mechanism

`transform` rewrites `import { Slot } from "radix-ui"` to `import { Slot } from "@radix-ui/react-slot"` and registers that source in `subpkgOrigin` → `resolveId` then re-resolves `@radix-ui/react-slot` relative to the `radix-ui` barrel entry via `this.resolve(source, barrelEntry, { skipSelf: true })`. Under pnpm, resolution from inside `radix-ui`'s package dir lands in a different peer-dependency context (`node_modules/.pnpm/radix-ui@x/node_modules/@radix-ui/react-slot`) than app-level imports (`@radix-ui+react-slot@x_react@19/...`), which forks the module graph and keeps generating fresh (importer, specifier) pairs — the scan never converges.

For same-package barrels like `lucide-react` the export-map entries are absolute file paths, so the re-resolve is idempotent — no loop.

## Workaround

Removing `radix-ui` from `DEFAULT_OPTIMIZE_PACKAGES` (via `pnpm.patchedDependencies`) makes the whole build complete in ~20s:

```
[1/5] analyze client references... ✓ 3166 modules transformed. built in 3.43s
[2/5] analyze server references...  ✓ 5986 modules transformed. built in 4.81s
[3/5] build rsc environment...      ✓ 3190 modules transformed. built in 2.63s
[4/5] build client environment...   ✓ 5974 modules transformed. built in 5.02s
[5/5] build ssr environment...      ✓ 6006 modules transformed. built in 3.83s
```

## Suggested fix directions

- Memoize `resolveId` results per `(envName, source)` — bounds the hook to one re-resolve per source.
- Skip re-resolution when `source` resolves to the same id the default pipeline would produce (compare with the natural resolution before overriding), or only register `subpkgOrigin` entries for same-package absolute paths — cross-package bare specifiers arguably shouldn't be re-resolved through the barrel at all.
- Alternatively expose an opt-out for individual `DEFAULT_OPTIMIZE_PACKAGES` entries via `nextConfig.experimental.optimizePackageImports` semantics.

issues.title: Nitro build: when the server bundle is split, the second RSC/SSR chunk exports rsc_exports / ssr_exports that no module declares (500 on every route; bun build --compile refuses the output)
issues.body:
### Summary

With `vinext()` + `nitro()` and code splitting left at Nitro's default, an app large enough to split the server environment into two chunks produces `.output/server/_ssr/rsc2.mjs` and `ssr2.mjs` whose `export { … }` clauses list `rsc_exports` and `ssr_exports`, symbols that are declared in no emitted file. The bundle fails on any runtime: `bun .output/server/index.mjs` answers every route with Nitro's `{ "error": true, "status": 500, "unhandled": true }` and logs `error: "ssr_exports" is not declared in this file`; `bun build --compile` refuses the output with the same two errors. Turning code splitting off for the server bundle makes the same app build, serve and compile.

Tested on `main` (1.0.0-beta.12) with `nitro@3.0.260610-beta`, `vite@8.2.2` (rolldown 1.2.6), Bun 1.4.2, React 19.2.5, on darwin arm64. I first hit this on 1.0.0-beta.4 and beta.8; it is unchanged on beta.12.

### Repro

The app is the reference app in a public repo (App Router, ~25 pages, route handlers, ISR, OpenTelemetry instrumentation, a data-cache adapter). A small app does not cross the split threshold, so I could not shrink it to a fixture yet.

```
git clone https://github.com/getknext-dev/knext && cd knext && git checkout aea1a4c0
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bunx turbo run build --filter=@getknext/core --filter=@getknext/lib --filter=@getknext/db
cd apps/file-manager
# vite.config.ts: nitro({ preset: 'bun', entry: './knext-bun-entry.mjs', rollupConfig: { output: { inlineDynamicImports: true } } })
# 1. as-is (splitting off):
bun run build && PORT=3111 bun .output/server/index.mjs     # GET / → 200, /api/health → 200
# 2. remove the `rollupConfig` line (splitting on), rebuild:
bun run build                                              # exit 0, .output/server/_ssr/{rsc,rsc2,ssr,ssr2}.mjs + 90 chunks
PORT=3112 bun .output/server/index.mjs                     # GET / → 500 {"error":true,"status":500,"unhandled":true}
bun build --compile --format=esm .output/server/index.mjs --outfile app   # exit 1
```

Output of step 2:

```
error: "ssr_exports" is not declared in this file
    at .output/server/_ssr/ssr2.mjs:1
error: "rsc_exports" is not declared in this file
    at .output/server/_ssr/rsc2.mjs:18
```

What the chunks look like (minified, trimmed):

```
// _ssr/rsc2.mjs — imports only node:url, then:
export { …, rsc_exports as S, … }
// _ssr/ssr2.mjs — imports only ../_runtime.mjs, then:
export { …, ssr_exports as j, … }
```

`rsc.mjs` imports from `rsc2.mjs`, `ssr.mjs` imports from `ssr2.mjs`, and `grep -rE '(const|let|var|function|class) (rsc_exports|ssr_exports)|import \* as (rsc_exports|ssr_exports)' .output/server` finds nothing. The names look like rolldown's synthetic namespace bindings for the `rsc` and `ssr` entries, which the secondary chunk re-exports without ever receiving.

### What I checked

- Not the compiler: the uncompiled output fails identically, and all `--compile` / `--minify` / `--bytecode` combinations fail the same way.
- Not app-configurable through rollup options: `build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks` (top level and `environments.rsc.*`) does not reach these chunks. Nitro on rolldown keys off `output.codeSplitting`; setting `rollupConfig: { output: { inlineDynamicImports: true } }` on the `nitro()` plugin makes Nitro set `codeSplitting = false` (`nitro/dist/vite.mjs`), and the same app then builds, serves 200 and compiles.
- Not present in the `vinext start` / standalone path, where the server is one bundle.

### Ask

Either of these would remove the failure for Nitro users:

1. Treat the server environment as non-splittable under the Nitro adapter (set `codeSplitting: false` / `inlineDynamicImports` for it from vinext's side), the way the standalone path already produces one bundle. I'm happy to send that PR if you point me at where you'd want it.
2. If splitting the RSC/SSR environments is meant to work, this is probably a rolldown chunking issue (an entry's namespace object exported from a secondary chunk without a declaration). I can help reduce it for a rolldown report, but I could not yet get a small app over the split threshold.

Until then, the workaround for anyone hitting this is Nitro's own `inlineDynamicImports: true` option (or the equivalent `rollupConfig: { output: { inlineDynamicImports: true } }` above), which Nitro translates into `codeSplitting: false` for the server bundle.

issues.title: nitro/bun preset: `_next/static` client manifests not emitted + `_next/static` misses return HTML 404 instead of plain-text
issues.body:
_Found running the official Next.js e2e test suite against vinext (vinext 1.0.0-beta.8, `nitro({ preset: 'bun' })`, Next.js 16.2 corpus, ESM app). Two related `_next/static` gaps on the nitro-bun adapter path._

## Bug 1 — client runtime manifests are never emitted by the build

`emitNextClientRuntimeManifests` (`dist/build/next-client-runtime-manifests.js`) writes `_buildManifest.js` (`self.__BUILD_MANIFEST = …`) and `_ssgManifest.js`, but it is **exported and never invoked** anywhere in the build pipeline — `grep -rn "next-client-runtime-manifests\|emitNextClientRuntimeManifests\|__BUILD_MANIFEST" dist/` returns only the module's own definition (checked in beta.8 and beta.4). So `vite build` never writes `_next/static/<buildId>/_buildManifest.js` / `_ssgManifest.js`.

- **Repro:** build any app-router or pages-router app; `GET /_next/static/<buildId>/_buildManifest.js`.
- **Expected (Next.js):** `200`, body `self.__BUILD_MANIFEST = {…}`.
- **Actual (vinext):** `404`.

## Bug 2 — nitro/bun adapter doesn't short-circuit `_next/static` misses to a plain-text 404

vinext has the correct handler — `notFoundStaticAssetResponse()` (`dist/server/http-error-responses.js`, returns `text/plain` `"Not Found"`) — and wires it into `startProdServer` (`dist/server/prod-server.js`) and the Cloudflare worker entries (`app-router-entry.js`, `pages-router-entry.js` via `isNextStaticPath`). But the **nitro bun preset** request path is neither, so an unmatched `_next/static` path falls through to the app's rendered custom-not-found **HTML**.

- **Repro:** `GET /_next/static/<buildId>/<nonexistent>.js` on a bun-preset build of an app with a custom `not-found`.
- **Expected (Next.js, and vinext's own standalone/worker paths):** `404`, `Content-Type: text/plain`, body `Not Found`.
- **Actual (vinext bun preset):** `404` with the app's custom-not-found HTML.

## Affected official e2e fixtures (8)

`invalid-static-asset-404-app` (+`-asset-prefix`, +`-base-path`), `invalid-static-asset-404-pages` (+`-asset-prefix`, +`-base-path`), `middleware-custom-matchers-i18n` (only failing case is the `_buildManifest.js` 200-check), `app-dir/asset-prefix-absolute`.

issues.title: App Router: match percent-containing prerendered dynamic paths without double decoding
issues.body:
## Next.js Change

**Commit:** [`b9be068`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/commit/b9be068538492837d2851f2900e1829bb16361c1)
**PR:** [#99121](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/99121)

## What Changed

Next.js no longer decodes dynamic route captures while selecting prerender metadata. The pathname has already been normalized for manifest lookup at that point, so decoding captures again rejects valid literal percent characters and returns a 500. Matching now checks only the route regular expression.

This fixes both closed paths generated by `generateStaticParams()` with `dynamicParams = false` and open dynamic-route fallbacks. Encoded slashes remain encoded within a catch-all parameter, while percent-containing values continue through to the server parameter representation.

## Impact on vinext

vinext should keep prerendered App Router route matching structural once request paths have been normalized for manifest or generated-route lookup. It must not decode an already-decoded pathname a second time while determining whether a dynamic route matches.

Otherwise valid requests such as `/open/docs/space%20here/fallback%25` can throw during matching rather than render, and closed catch-all paths containing `%` or `%2F` may be rejected despite appearing in `generateStaticParams()`.

## Suggested Coverage

- A closed `dynamicParams = false` catch-all route generated with a literal percent-containing parameter returns 200.
- An open catch-all fallback containing a literal percent renders successfully on its initial request and on a subsequent cached request.
- Encoded spaces and `%2F` survive matching without a 500 or an extra decode.
- Assert the `params` value retains vinext’s existing encoded-parameter semantics.

## Related

- [Next.js commit b9be068](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/commit/b9be068538492837d2851f2900e1829bb16361c1)

issues.title: build --prerender-all crashes on cloudflare:* imports (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME)
issues.body:
## Summary

`vinext build --prerender-all` (equiv. `vinext({ prerender: true })`) crashes before rendering anything on a Cloudflare-targeted app, because the prerunner executes the server graph under plain Node.js and the graph contains `cloudflare:*` imports.

```
Error [ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME]: Only URLs with a scheme in: file, data, and node are supported by the default ESM loader. Received protocol 'cloudflare:'
    at prerenderApp (vinext/dist/build/prerender.js:564:22)
    at runPrerender (vinext/dist/build/run-prerender.js:145:25)
```

Observed on `vinext@1.0.0-beta.10`.

## Repro

Any Cloudflare-targeted vinext app where the server graph imports `cloudflare:workers` — e.g. API routes reading bindings (`import { env } from "cloudflare:workers"`), middleware-side helpers using `env`/`waitUntil`, or vinext's own Cloudflare adapter runtime/shims. Plain `vinext build` succeeds (bundling never executes); only the prerender execution phase fails.

Related to #3318 (same caching story: prerender-all is the natural way to give routes static cache policies for the Cloudflare CDN adapter to enforce, so this crash blocks the documented path to edge-cached pages).

## Expected

The prerunner should tolerate workerd-native imports — either by executing the prerender graph inside workerd/miniflare, or by stubbing/externalizing `cloudflare:*` specifiers during prerender (they are irrelevant to rendering HTML). Per-route static generation (`force-static` + `generateStaticParams`) works fine today; only the all-discovery runner is affected.

### Summary

On the Node production server (`vinext start` / standalone), `/_next/image` returns the original file unresized, even when an optimizer is registered with `setImageOptimizer()`. Optimization only runs on the Worker path, where the request handler requires `env.ASSETS && getImageOptimizer()`.

An app with a large local image rendered through `next/image`, and an optimizer registered via `setImageOptimizer()`. `vinext build && vinext start`: `GET /_next/image?url=%2Fphoto.jpg&w=640&q=75` returns the original image (181 KB in our case) with the security headers, and the optimizer is never called. The same optimizer, invoked from a custom Nitro entry, returns a 2.4 KB resized image.

### Question

Would you accept having `prod-server.ts` call the registered optimizer, when one is set, for `/_next/image` (reading the source from `dist/client` / `public`), and fall back to serving the original as today? This also relates to #3427, where the Worker entries rely on `env.ASSETS` for filesystem access that other hosts lack.

issues.title: Standalone server.js hard-codes the output path, so a compiled binary cannot be relocated
issues.body:
### Summary

The generated `dist/standalone/server.js` resolves its build output with `join(import.meta.dirname, "dist")`. When the standalone server is compiled into a single executable (for example with `bun build --compile --bytecode dist/standalone/server.js`), `import.meta.dirname` is fixed at compile time to the build machine's path. The binary works in place, but after it's moved or copied into an image it prints:

```
[vinext] No build output found in <build-machine path>/dist/standalone/dist
```

Tested on `main` (1.0.0-beta.12) with Bun 1.4.2. The build and the compile both succeed, and the compiled binary serves App and Pages routes when left in place.

### Suggestion

- Let `server.js` take the output directory from an environment variable (e.g. `VINEXT_OUT_DIR`) or a CLI flag, falling back to the current `import.meta.dirname` join.
- Document `startProdServer`'s options (`outDir`, and the entry-path options) as a supported API, so custom entries don't depend on internals.

issues.title: Publish checksums and/or artifact attestations for release binaries
issues.body:
## Request

Please publish SHA-256 checksums and/or [GitHub artifact attestations](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/using-artifact-attestations/using-artifact-attestations-to-establish-provenance-for-builds) alongside release binaries.

## Why

Currently the release assets include only bare binaries with no mechanism for downstream consumers to verify integrity or provenance. Projects that install cloudflared from GitHub releases have to either:

- Hardcode SHA-256 checksums and manually update them every release (brittle)
- Skip verification entirely (insecure)

A checksums file (e.g., `cloudflared-checksums-sha256.txt`) in the release assets would be a quick win. Artifact attestations would be even better, enabling cryptographic provenance verification with:

```bash
gh attestation verify cloudflared-linux-amd64 --repo cloudflare/cloudflared
```

## Context

We ran into this while adding supply-chain hardening to [NVIDIA/NemoClaw](https://github.com/NVIDIA/NemoClaw), which downloads cloudflared in its install scripts. We're currently hardcoding checksums as a workaround.

issues.title: 2026.9.0 segfaults in quic-go QueueProbePacket (nil receiver) when running in a Docker bridge network — 2026.8.2 unaffected
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`cloudflared` 2026.9.0 crashes with SIGSEGV roughly every 75 seconds when running
in a Docker container on a bridge network. The panic is a nil-receiver dereference
inside the bundled quic-go fork, on the probe-timeout path.

The same container on 2026.8.2 is completely stable. Notably, a **second tunnel
running the same 2026.9.0 binary on the same machine**, as a host systemd service,
has **zero** crashes — the only meaningful difference is that it uses the host
network directly instead of the Docker bridge/NAT.

Since `QueueProbePacket` is only reached on a PTO (probe timeout), the NAT path
seems to make packet loss / timeouts frequent enough to hit a latent race that the
direct path rarely triggers.

**To Reproduce**

1. Run `cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.9.0` in a Docker container on a user-defined
   bridge network (container IP `172.20.0.2`, NAT via iptables MASQUERADE).
2. Command: `tunnel --no-autoupdate --loglevel info run --token <token>`
   (remotely-managed tunnel, 3 ingress rules pointing at an internal service).
3. Let it run. It starts cleanly every time — all connectivity pre-checks PASS,
   4 connections register (tpe01 / khh01, quic) — then panics after roughly a
   minute and is restarted by `restart: unless-stopped`.
   Observed: **145 crashes in ~6 hours**.

4. Tunnel ID: <填入或留空>
5. cloudflared config: token-based (remotely managed), no local config file.

**Expected behavior**

The tunnel stays connected without crashing, as it does on 2026.8.2.

**Environment and versions**

 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-139-generic (Docker container)
 - Architecture: AMD64 — Intel Core 2 Duo P8800, 2 cores (old hardware, no AES-NI;
   noting it in case goroutine timing is relevant to the race)
 - Version: 2026.9.0 (built 2026-09-09-18:43 UTC), GoVersion go1.26.8
 - Last known good: 2026.8.2 (built 2026-08-14-12:28 UTC)

**Logs and errors**

[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x4c pc=0xdae18d]

goroutine 128 [running]:
github.com/quic-go/quic-go/internal/ackhandler.(*sentPacketHandler).getPacketNumberSpace(...)
        /go/pkg/mod/github.com/chungthuang/quic-go@v0.45.1-0.20260529212404-a9fddf436fc4/internal/ackhandler/sent_packet_handler.go:374
github.com/quic-go/quic-go/internal/ackhandler.(*sentPacketHandler).QueueProbePacket(0x0?, 0xfc?)
        /go/pkg/mod/github.com/chungthuang/quic-go@v0.45.1-0.20260529212404-a9fddf436fc4/internal/ackhandler/sent_packet_handler.go:1042 +0x12d
github.com/quic-go/quic-go.(*Conn).sendProbePacket(0x1524c553b208, 0xd8?, 0x35a126441a6)
        /go/pkg/mod/github.com/chungthuang/quic-go@v0.45.1-0.20260529212404-a9fddf436fc4/connection.go:2722 +0x104
github.com/quic-go/quic-go.(*Conn).triggerSending(0x1524c553b208, 0x35a126441a6)
        /go/pkg/mod/github.com/chungthuang/quic-go@v0.45.1-0.20260529212404-a9fddf436fc4/connection.go:2486 +0x16a
github.com/quic-go/quic-go.(*Conn).run(0x1524c553b208)
        /go/pkg/mod/github.com/chungthuang/quic-go@v0.45.1-0.20260529212404-a9fddf436fc4/connection.go:741 +0x705
github.com/quic-go/quic-go.(*Transport).doDial.func1()
        /go/pkg/mod/github.com/chungthuang/quic-go@v0.45.1-0.20260529212404-a9fddf436fc4/transport.go:326 +0x3a
created by github.com/quic-go/quic-go.(*Transport).doDial in goroutine 107
        /go/pkg/mod/github.com/chungthuang/quic-go@v0.45.1-0.20260529212404-a9fddf436fc4/transport.go:325 +0x737

The `pc` is identical on every crash (`pc=0xdae18d`), with `addr` varying only
between 0x4b–0x4d — a deterministic nil dereference, not memory corruption.

**Additional context**

- **Not OOM:** `OOMKilled=false`, memory usage 17.4 MiB against a 128 MiB limit.
- **Same binary, same host, no crash:** the host-side systemd tunnel runs the same
  2026.9.0 with **0** SIGSEGV over 8+ hours.
- Differences between the two processes on this machine:
  - container: Docker bridge NAT (172.20.0.2), ICMP proxy **enabled**
  - host: direct on the physical NIC, ICMP proxy **disabled** (ping_group_range)
- `net.core.rmem_max` / `wmem_max` are raised to 7500000 on this host, so both
  processes get the full 7 MiB UDP receive buffer they ask for. The stable host
  process runs with the same setting, so this does not appear to be the trigger.
- **Rolling the container back to 2026.8.2 resolves it completely:** 0 crashes in
  over an hour, where the observed rate would have predicted ~48.

issues.title: 🐛 --protocol auto does not fall back to HTTP/2 when the QUIC handshake is rejected with CRYPTO_ERROR 0x178 (tls: no application protocol), and the UDP precheck reports it as healthy
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

On a network where the QUIC handshake to the tunnel edge is **rejected during the TLS handshake** (rather than blackholed), `--protocol auto` never falls back to HTTP/2. It retries QUIC indefinitely with exponential backoff, registers no connections, and the tunnel stays down.

Two distinct observations, in the same run and the same second:

1. **No fallback.** Every dial fails with `CRYPTO_ERROR 0x178 (remote): tls: no application protocol` — TLS alert 120, `no_application_protocol` — and `auto` keeps retrying QUIC instead of switching transports.
2. **The startup precheck reports the opposite of reality.** At the very moment those dials are failing, `UDP Connectivity` is reported `status=pass` with `details="QUIC connection successful"` for both regions, and the run concludes `suggested_protocol=quic`.

This looks like the second causes the first: the precheck's UDP component appears to test reachability rather than a real tunnel handshake, so the transport-selection logic is told QUIC is usable while it demonstrably is not.

## Log

`--protocol auto`, cloudflared 2026.7.2. `run_id` elided, timestamps verbatim:

```
15:51:33Z INF Version 2026.7.2 (Checksum 809407c3d6e78787e2b14863ea6a1d4f31712186b5fd056815d093e29e8bff26)
15:51:33Z INF GOOS: darwin, GOVersion: go1.26.5, GoArch: amd64
15:51:34Z ERR Failed to dial a quic connection error="failed to dial to edge with quic: CRYPTO_ERROR 0x178 (remote): tls: no application protocol" connIndex=0 ip=198.41.200.33
15:51:34Z INF Retrying connection in up to 2s  connIndex=0 ip=198.41.200.33
15:51:35Z ERR Failed to dial a quic connection error="... tls: no application protocol" connIndex=0 ip=198.41.200.193
15:51:35Z INF Retrying connection in up to 4s  connIndex=0 ip=198.41.200.193
15:51:36Z ERR Failed to dial a quic connection error="... tls: no application protocol" connIndex=0 ip=198.41.200.23
15:51:36Z INF Retrying connection in up to 8s  connIndex=0 ip=198.41.200.23
15:51:40Z ERR Failed to dial a quic connection error="... tls: no application protocol" connIndex=0 ip=198.41.192.67
15:51:40Z INF Retrying connection in up to 16s connIndex=0 ip=198.41.192.67
15:51:40Z INF precheck component="DNS Resolution"  details="DNS Resolved successfully"   status=pass target=region1.v2.argotunnel.com
15:51:40Z INF precheck component="UDP Connectivity" details="QUIC connection successful" status=pass target=region1.v2.argotunnel.com
15:51:40Z INF precheck component="UDP Connectivity" details="QUIC connection successful" status=pass target=region2.v2.argotunnel.com
15:51:40Z INF precheck component="TCP Connectivity" details="HTTP/2 connection successful" status=pass target=region1.v2.argotunnel.com
15:51:40Z INF precheck complete hard_fail=false suggested_protocol=quic
```

The backoff kept growing (observed up to `1m4s`). No `Registered tunnel connection` line ever appeared, over more than fifteen minutes, until the protocol was pinned to `http2` by hand — after which all four connections registered within two seconds.

## Expected behavior

After repeated QUIC dial failures, `--protocol auto` should fall back to HTTP/2, as documented in [Run parameters](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/configure-tunnels/cloudflared-parameters/run-parameters/). A TLS-level rejection of the QUIC handshake seems not to be classified as "QUIC is unusable" the way a timeout is.

Secondarily: `UDP Connectivity` should not report `pass` / `QUIC connection successful` on a path where the tunnel's own QUIC handshake is being rejected. As it stands the precheck is actively misleading — it was the reason we believed QUIC was viable here.

## To Reproduce

1. Be on a network that rejects the QUIC handshake to the edge rather than dropping the packets. Ours is a mobile carrier (see below) where UDP to `198.41.192.0/24` / `198.41.200.0/24` on 7844 is reachable but the handshake is refused.
2. `cloudflared tunnel --protocol auto run --token-file ...`
3. Observe repeated `CRYPTO_ERROR 0x178`, growing backoff, no fallback, no registered connections.

`--protocol http2` on the same host and network works perfectly and has done for months.

## How this differs from #749

[#749](https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/issues/749) (closed, 2022) is the same expectation but a different trigger: there UDP was *blocked* and the symptom was `i/o timeout`. Here UDP reaches the edge and the failure happens inside the TLS handshake, which is presumably why it is classified differently — and why the precheck passes.

## Environment and versions

- OS: macOS 15.7.7
- Architecture: x86_64
- Version: **2026.7.2**, reproduced on that build.
- Also on **2026.8.3**: `--protocol quic` produces the identical `CRYPTO_ERROR 0x178`. `--protocol auto` was **not** retested on 2026.8.3 — this is a production tunnel and each attempt takes the service down, so I did not want to run it again blind. Worth noting that on 2026.8.3 the precheck did, in a later run, correctly report `UDP Connectivity ... QUIC connection failed` with `suggested_protocol=http2`, so the precheck behaviour may already differ between the two builds.

## Additional context

The network-side cause is almost certainly upstream of cloudflared and I am not asking you to fix it — QUIC from this uplink reaches Google, Facebook, Akamai and Vultr over HTTP/3 fine, but times out to Cloudflare (`104.18.0.0/16`, `1.1.1.0/24`) and Fastly (`151.101.0.0/16`). Path MTU is 1500 to all of them.

The report is only about the two client-side behaviours: the missing fallback, and a precheck that reports a path as healthy while that same path is failing in the same second.

issues.title: 🐛 Cloudflare Tunnel QUIC connections intermittently terminate with "timeout: no recent network activity" in Azure Container Apps
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

We are running `cloudflared` as a container in an Azure Container App.

The container itself remains healthy and running, but established Cloudflare Tunnel QUIC connections intermittently terminate with:

`timeout: no recent network activity`

When this happens, `cloudflared` retries the connection and successfully registers a new QUIC connection shortly afterwards.

This causes intermittent connectivity interruptions through the tunnel.

The issue appears to affect individual QUIC connections rather than the Azure Container App/container itself. We do not see the container restarting when these connection failures occur.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Run `cloudflared` inside an Azure Container App.
2. Configure a Cloudflare Tunnel using the default/automatic protocol selection.
3. Allow the tunnel to establish multiple QUIC connections.
4. Keep the container running and monitor the `cloudflared` logs.
5. After some time, one or more established QUIC connections intermittently terminate with `timeout: no recent network activity`.
6. `cloudflared` retries the connection and establishes a new QUIC connection.

Example log sequence:

    INF Registered tunnel connection connIndex=0 protocol=quic
    INF Registered tunnel connection connIndex=1 protocol=quic
    INF Registered tunnel connection connIndex=2 protocol=quic

    ERR failed to accept incoming stream requests error="failed to accept QUIC stream: timeout: no recent network activity"
    ERR failed to run the datagram handler error="timeout: no recent network activity"
    WRN failed to serve tunnel connection error="accept stream listener encountered a failure while serving"
    WRN Serve tunnel error error="accept stream listener encountered a failure while serving"
    INF Retrying connection in up to 1s
    WRN Connection terminated error="accept stream listener encountered a failure while serving"

    INF Tunnel connection curve preferences: [X25519MLKEM768 CurveID(65074) CurveP256]
    INF Registered tunnel connection connIndex=0 protocol=quic

Another observed occurrence:

    ERR failed to accept incoming stream requests error="failed to accept QUIC stream: timeout: no recent network activity"
    ERR failed to run the datagram handler error="timeout: no recent network activity"
    WRN failed to serve tunnel connection error="datagram manager encountered a failure while serving"
    INF Retrying connection in up to 1s
    INF Registered tunnel connection connIndex=1 protocol=quic

If it's an issue with Cloudflare Tunnel:

4. Tunnel ID: `[REDACTED]`
5. `cloudflared` config:

        tunnel: [REDACTED]
        credentials-file: [REDACTED]

        # Other configuration omitted because it contains internal/private information.

The tunnel is running inside Azure Container Apps and uses the default/automatic protocol selection.

**Expected behavior**

Established QUIC tunnel connections should remain stable while the container remains healthy and network connectivity is available.

If a QUIC connection does encounter a network interruption, the tunnel should recover without noticeable interruption where possible.

We would also like to understand whether `timeout: no recent network activity` is expected behavior for QUIC connections running inside Azure Container Apps.

**Environment and versions**

- OS: Linux (container)
- Architecture: AMD64
- Version: latest .2026.8.2
- Platform: Azure Container Apps
- Protocol: QUIC
- Protocol selection: Default/automatic
- Base image: `gcr.io/distroless/base-debian13:nonroot-amd64`

The container remains running during the QUIC connection failures.

Multiple tunnel connections are established concurrently.

After rebuilding/redeploying the container, the built-in `cloudflared` connectivity checks reported:

        +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
        |  COMPONENT         TARGET                     STATUS  DETAILS                       |
        +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
        |  DNS Resolution    region1.v2.argotunnel.com  PASS    DNS Resolved successfully     |
        |  DNS Resolution    region2.v2.argotunnel.com  PASS    DNS Resolved successfully     |
        |  UDP Connectivity  region1.v2.argotunnel.com  PASS    QUIC connection successful   |
        |  UDP Connectivity  region2.v2.argotunnel.com  PASS    QUIC connection successful   |
        |  TCP Connectivity  region1.v2.argotunnel.com  PASS    HTTP/2 connection successful |
        |  TCP Connectivity  region2.v2.argotunnel.com  PASS    HTTP/2 connection successful |
        |  Cloudflare API    api.cloudflare.com:443     PASS    API is reachable              |
        +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

        SUMMARY: Environment is healthy. cloudflared will use 'quic' as primary protocol.

Therefore, DNS, UDP/QUIC, TCP/HTTP/2, and Cloudflare API connectivity are successful when the connectivity check is performed.

However, established QUIC connections can subsequently terminate with:

`timeout: no recent network activity`

**Logs and errors**

Additional examples:

    WRN Serve tunnel error error="accept stream listener encountered a failure while serving"
    ERR failed to accept incoming stream requests error="failed to accept QUIC stream: timeout: no recent network activity"
    ERR failed to run the datagram handler error="timeout: no recent network activity"
    WRN failed to serve tunnel connection error="accept stream listener encountered a failure while serving"
    INF Retrying connection in up to 1s
    WRN Connection terminated error="accept stream listener encountered a failure while serving"

The connection is then successfully recreated:

    INF Tunnel connection curve preferences: [X25519MLKEM768 CurveID(65074) CurveP256]
    INF Registered tunnel connection connIndex=0 protocol=quic

Another observed sequence:

    ERR failed to accept incoming stream requests error="failed to accept QUIC stream: timeout: no recent network activity"
    ERR failed to run the datagram handler error="timeout: no recent network activity"
    WRN failed to serve tunnel connection error="datagram manager encountered a failure while serving"
    WRN Serve tunnel error error="datagram manager encountered a failure while serving"
    INF Retrying connection in up to 1s
    INF Registered tunnel connection connIndex=1 protocol=quic

The same behavior has been observed on multiple connection indexes.

**Additional context**

The Azure Container App remains healthy during the failures and we do not observe a container restart associated with the QUIC disconnects.

The tunnel generally continues operating because `cloudflared` automatically reconnects, but the connection termination can cause intermittent interruptions.

The issue does not appear to be caused by an inability to establish QUIC connectivity initially. The connectivity checks successfully report QUIC connectivity to both test endpoints.

We would like to determine whether this is:

- Expected QUIC behavior
- An Azure Container Apps UDP/NAT/idle-timeout interaction
- A `cloudflared` issue
- Or a configuration issue specific to running Cloudflare Tunnel inside Azure Container Apps

We would particularly appreciate guidance on:

1. Is `timeout: no recent network activity` expected for established QUIC connections in this environment?
2. Are there known QUIC/UDP idle-timeout issues when running `cloudflared` inside Azure Container Apps?
3. Could Azure Container Apps networking, NAT, UDP idle timeouts, or another networking component cause an established QUIC connection to become inactive from `cloudflared`'s perspective?
4. Are there recommended `cloudflared` settings, keepalive settings, or timeout settings for this environment?
5. Would switching from QUIC to HTTP/2 be a recommended workaround?
6. Would running multiple `cloudflared` replicas improve availability for this type of failure?
7. Are there additional diagnostics or debug logs we should collect to identify why the QUIC connection becomes inactive?

issues.title: Worker Preview URLs return Cloudflare 1042 before Worker execution while production workers.dev is disabled
issues.body:
### What versions & operating system are you using?

- Wrangler: 4.141.0
- Node: v24.12.0
- npm: 11.6.2
- OS: macOS 12.7.6 (x86_64)
- Worker compatibility date: 2026-09-26
- Worker Previews open beta

The Preview deployment itself is created successfully by Cloudflare. The failure below happens at the remote `workers.dev` edge before application code executes.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction

Source-neutral reproduction project at the exact tested commit:

https://github.com/andrewandrewandryukov-boop/toyota-telegram-bot/tree/fa00abe5b02eefd3701a79d49ce1c48e7b21aae2/fitment/mcp-v2753

No secret values are committed. `/mcp` without the application Bearer token intentionally returns 401 before the read-model asset is loaded, which makes it easy to tell whether traffic reached application code.

### Describe the Bug

A Worker Preview is created successfully and Cloudflare returns both a Preview alias URL and an immutable deployment URL. Preview URLs are enabled while the production `workers.dev` endpoint remains disabled.

State:
- `workers_dev: false`
- `preview_urls: true`
- Worker subdomain state: `enabled: false`, `previews_enabled: true`
- zero production deployments
- Preview deployment succeeds and is reported as latest
- Worker code + Assets + one secret-text binding + one Rate Limiting binding
- `run_worker_first: true`
- no Cloudflare Access app protecting the Preview

Expected: `/mcp` without application auth reaches the Preview Worker and returns Worker-generated HTTP 401.

Actual: Cloudflare returns before Worker execution:

```text
HTTP/2 404
content-type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
server: cloudflare

error code: 1042
```

The same result reproduces on three targets: the Preview alias, the immutable deployment URL, and a deliberately random/nonexistent Preview prefix under the same suffix. Each gets a distinct Ray ID but the same 404/1042 result. A fresh second Preview created after enabling Preview URLs reproduced the same failure and was then deleted.

Sanitized fingerprint from a run:

```json
{
  "fingerprint": "wildcard-preview-router-1042",
  "results": [
    {"kind":"preview-alias","status":404,"errorCode":1042,"cfRay":"a4129dc76a8a9cae-ARN"},
    {"kind":"immutable-deployment","status":404,"errorCode":1042,"cfRay":"a4129dc8abbb0a40-ARN"},
    {"kind":"random-prefix-control","status":404,"errorCode":1042,"cfRay":"a4129dc9dec270da-ARN"}
  ]
}
```

Cloudflare docs define 1042 as a same-zone Worker-to-Worker fetch restriction. The client here is a direct external curl/Node request and the application auth gate should return 401 before any `ASSETS.fetch()`. So 1042 is occurring before application invocation. Whether the Preview router itself is making such a same-zone fetch is only a hypothesis, not a claimed root cause.

Production `wrangler deploy` was intentionally not used as a workaround because this reproduction is specifically about Preview routing and production exposure is not desired.

### Please provide any relevant error logs

```text
Preview deployment: successful
Preview startup time reported by Cloudflare: 47 ms
Production deployments: 0
Preview URLs configured: true
Production workers.dev enabled: false
Expected unauthenticated /mcp: 401 from Worker
Actual: 404 / Cloudflare 1042 before Worker invocation
```

Project diagnostics (they redact the full host and do not print application secrets):

```bash
npm run check:preview-host -- https://<preview-host>
npm run diagnose:preview-routing -- https://<preview-host>
npm run support:preview-routing -- https://<preview-host>
```

Could you confirm whether Worker Previews need additional routing/subdomain configuration when production `workers.dev` is intentionally disabled, or whether this 1042 path is a Preview routing bug?

issues.title: Dependency cleanup/syntax modernisation
issues.body:
Fairly low priority I imagine, but there are various dependency clean ups and code modernisations we can do in this repo.

I already opened a couple of PRs but want a tracking issue to add some context/discussion.

Here are my suggestions:

## Dependencies

| Dependency | Used by | Replace with | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| chalk | wrangler, create-cloudflare, cli | `styleText` (native) or `picocolors` | miniflare uses kleur, so could make sense to settle on that or move miniflare to also use styleText/picocolors |
| execa | wrangler, create-cloudflare | `tinyexec` | #12369  |
| strip-ansi | wrangler, vite-plugin-cloudflare | `stripVTControlCharacters` (native) | #11853 |
| find-up | tools, workers-utils, wrangler | `empathic` | #12601 |
| glob | tools, pages-shared, create-cloudflare | `tinyglobby` | vite-plugin-cloudflare already uses tinyglobby |
| rimraf | workflows-shared, miniflare, wrangler, pages-shared, workers-shared | `premove` | #11913  |
| `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin` | _various_ | Remove | #11906  |

These replacements are what the e18e community recommend (see [here](https://e18e.dev/docs/replacements/)). The modules being replaced are generally much larger, slower, and/or outdated.

I can explain each one if needed, just let me know 👍 

## Syntax (modernisation/perf)

FYI I used the [e18e ESLint plugin](https://github.com/e18e/eslint-plugin) to find a bunch of these (in case you want a way to reproduce the findings etc).

| Old syntax | New syntax | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `arr[arr.length - 1]` | `arr.at(-1)` | |
| `[...arr].map(mapper)` | `Array.from(arr, mapper)` | Avoids an intermediate array being allocated |
| `str.match(regex)` | `regex.test(str)` | In conditional logic, to avoid an unused match array |

For these, we could run `eslint --fix` with the e18e plugin enabled to auto-fix them. There's various occurrences but not a huge amount so it'd be easily reviewable.

---

Let me know if there's any interest in any of these. I and others would be happy to contribute the changes if you give the go-ahead.

issues.title: deploy: config-file routes silently ignored for Workers declaring [assets] (no zone-routes API call; --routes CLI flag works)
issues.body:
## Summary

`wrangler deploy` silently ignores config-file `routes` (no zone-routes API call at all, no warning, no error) for a Worker that declares an `[assets]` directory. The same account/zone attaches routes correctly for a Worker **without** `[assets]`. Passing the identical routes via the `--routes` CLI flag works, which isolates the failure to the config-file path combined with assets.

## Environment

- wrangler: 4.107.0 (also reproduced with the `opennextjs-cloudflare` deploy wrapper on @opennextjs/cloudflare 1.20.1, which delegates to wrangler)
- platform: macOS arm64, Node 22
- Workers config (TOML), abridged:

```toml
name = "example-shop"
main = ".open-next/worker.js"
compatibility_date = "2026-07-12"
compatibility_flags = ["nodejs_compat", "global_fetch_strictly_public"]
workers_dev = true
preview_urls = true

[assets]
directory = ".open-next/assets"
binding = "ASSETS"

routes = [
  { pattern = "example.com/*", zone_name = "example.com" },
  { pattern = "www.example.com/*", zone_name = "example.com" }
]

[[services]]
binding = "WORKER_SELF_REFERENCE"
service = "example-shop"
```

## Actual behavior

```
$ wrangler deploy --config wrangler.example.toml
Uploaded example-shop
Deployed example-shop triggers
  https://example-shop.<acct>.workers.dev
Current Version ID: ...
```

- Only the workers.dev URL is printed; the two custom routes are neither attached nor mentioned.
- `WRANGLER_LOG=debug` shows only `subdomain` API calls — **zero** `/zones/{zone}/workers/routes` requests.
- `wrangler triggers deploy` (also tried `triggers deploy --dry-run`): same, subdomain-only.
- No error, no warning — completely silent.

## Expected behavior

Config-declared `routes` should attach the same way the CLI-flag path attaches them (and the way the same zone succeeds for a no-assets Worker), or the deploy should fail loudly if it cannot.

## Controls that DO work (isolating the bug)

1. Same account, same zone, a second Worker **without** `[assets]` whose config declares `routes = [{ pattern = "api.example.com/*", zone_name = "example.com" }]` → `wrangler deploy` prints and attaches `api.example.com/* (zone name: example.com)` correctly.
2. For the assets Worker, passing the same routes as CLI flags works immediately:
```
$ wrangler deploy --config wrangler.example.toml --routes "example.com/*" --routes "www.example.com/*"
Deployed example-shop triggers
  https://example-shop.<acct>.workers.dev
  example.com/*
  www.example.com/*
```
Both patterns then appear in the trigger output and the zone routes API reflects them.

The only difference between the working and broken cases is (a) `[assets]` present and/or (b) routes declared in the config file instead of CLI flags.

## Impact

Any OpenNext/`[assets]` Worker migrated to custom domain routes via config silently keeps only workers.dev; we lost time debugging the deploy wrapper before narrowing it to wrangler. Workaround in use: the CLI `--routes` flag path.

issues.title: Vitest run stalls indefinitely mid-suite after a workerd pool test file finishes, with no error output
issues.body:
### Summary

A Vitest run using `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` can hang indefinitely partway through a multi-file run: a workerd-backed test file's assertions and `console.*` output all print successfully, and then the run produces zero further output — no next test file starting, no completion summary, no error, no stack trace — until an external watchdog/timeout kills the process. This looks distinct from #15085 (fixed in 0.22.0) and #14180 (fixed): those hangs happen at *final* process teardown; this one happens *mid-run*, before the suite has even finished running all test files.

### Versions

- `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers`: 0.22.0 (already includes the #15085 dispose-ordering fix)
- `vitest`: 4.1.10
- `miniflare`: 5.20260815.0-alpha
- Node.js: 22.x
- Linux (containerized CI runner)

### Observed behavior

1. A Vitest run includes several test files; at least one exercises a Worker via `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` (e.g. calling `fetch()` against the Worker's default export handler).
2. That file's tests pass and log their output normally, including `console.*`/stdout emitted from inside the Worker.
3. After that file's output, the process produces no further logs of any kind — no next file starting, no error.
4. The process never exits on its own. Only an external timeout (CI job timeout, watchdog, etc.) kills it, many minutes later.
5. Reproduced twice in a row under the same conditions (same file, same batch of files run together), so it doesn't look like a one-off flake.

This is easiest to hit when several test files run together in one long-lived process (either Vitest's normal multi-file run, or a sharding/batching tool that groups files into one process) — the hang isn't necessarily tied to being the *last* file in the run, just to a workerd-backed file's pool being torn down for one file while other files are still pending in the same run.

### Suspected root cause

This matches the failure mode described in #15097 ("Miniflare#dispose() rejects with ERR_SERVER_NOT_RUNNING when called twice, skipping the rest of its cleanup"), which was closed `not_planned` but still describes a real defect: if `dispose()` is invoked more than once for the same `Miniflare` instance, the second call rejects early on an already-closed server and **skips the remaining cleanup steps** — including steps that stop things keeping the Node event loop alive (e.g. the dev registry file watcher, per that issue's own description). A leaked handle from a skipped cleanup step would explain a process that just sits there indefinitely with no output and no error, rather than crashing or exiting cleanly — which is exactly what's observed here.

#15085 fixed the *ordering* within a single `dispose()` call, so `workerd` termination isn't blocked behind other independent cleanup. It doesn't address a *second* `dispose()` call short-circuiting and skipping steps entirely. If anything in the pool's per-file or per-run teardown sequence can end up calling `dispose()` twice for the same instance, #15097's bug would still produce a silent hang even on 0.22.0.

### Ask

- Could #15097 be reconsidered? Making `dispose()` idempotent (treat "already stopped" as success and continue the remaining cleanup, rather than throwing and skipping the rest) looks like it closes a real gap regardless of how contrived that issue's specific repro was.
- If there's a known code path in `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` where `dispose()` could be called twice for the same `Miniflare` instance (e.g. a per-file teardown racing a later run-level teardown), a pointer there would help narrow this down. I don't have an isolated minimal repro yet — this was observed under real multi-file CI runs, not a synthetic minimal case — but the shape matches #15097 closely enough that I suspect it's the same underlying issue resurfacing as a mid-run hang instead of a final-exit hang.

### Related

- #15085 (fixed, included in 0.22.0) — different phase of teardown (final exit ordering)
- #14180 (fixed) — different trigger (DO `blockConcurrencyWhile` + console + throw)
- #15097 (closed not_planned) — likely root cause of this issue

issues.title: 🐛 BUG: a network failure while refreshing the OAuth token is reported as an expired login (and starts a new login)
issues.body:
### What versions & operating system are you using?

wrangler 4.126.0 (the same code path is unchanged on `main`), Node.js 22, macOS. The platform does not matter; the bug is in `@cloudflare/workers-auth`.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction

No repository needed. With fake, already-expired OAuth credentials and a token URL that never answers:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/repro/.wrangler/config
cat > /tmp/repro/.wrangler/config/default.toml <<'TOML'
oauth_token = "fake-expired-access-token"
expiration_time = "2020-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
refresh_token = "fake-refresh-token"
scopes = ["account:read"]
TOML
cd /tmp/repro
HOME=/tmp/repro WRANGLER_TOKEN_URL=https://10.255.255.1/oauth2/token npx wrangler whoami < /dev/null
```

### Describe the Bug

When the access token has expired and the refresh request to the OAuth token endpoint fails at the network level (DNS failure, connection timeout, TLS error), Wrangler reports that the login itself is invalid:

```
✘ [ERROR] Not logged in. Your auth token has expired and could not be refreshed, and the environment is non-interactive. Run `wrangler login` in an interactive terminal or set a CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN.
```

In an interactive terminal it goes further and starts a new browser login, which needs the same unreachable server.

The stored refresh token may be perfectly valid: once the network works again, the same refresh succeeds without any login. The real cause only appears in the debug log:

```
Failed to fetch auth token: TypeError: fetch failed
  [cause]: AggregateError [ETIMEDOUT]
Token refresh failed: fetch failed
```

A common real-world trigger is a network where IPv6 is advertised but not routable and IPv4 latency to the token endpoint exceeds Node's default happy-eyeballs attempt timeout (250 ms): every connection attempt times out. Running with `NODE_OPTIONS="--no-network-family-autoselection --dns-result-order=ipv4first"` makes the same refresh succeed, which confirms the credentials were fine all along.

**Cause:** `refreshToken()` in `packages/workers-auth/src/flow.ts` catches every error and returns `false`, so "the server rejected the refresh token" and "no HTTP response arrived at all" become the same result. `loginOrRefreshIfRequired()` then reports `token-expired-*` and, when interactive, starts a login.

**Expected:** a network failure during refresh should say that the Cloudflare auth server could not be reached, leave the stored credentials alone, and not start a login.

### Please provide any relevant error logs

See above (`WRANGLER_LOG=debug`).

issues.title: [Workflows] Bulk introspection and cleanup open resources for every instance at once
issues.body:
### What versions & operating system are you using?

Collected on 2026-09-24 with `envinfo` 7.14.0 using the requested flags (`--system --npmPackages '{wrangler,create-cloudflare,miniflare,@cloudflare/*}' --binaries`). Binary installation paths are omitted:

```text
  System:
    OS: macOS 27.0
    CPU: (10) arm64 Apple M1 Pro
    Memory: 219.08 MB / 16.00 GB
    Shell: 5.9
  Binaries:
    Node: 26.9.0
    Yarn: 1.22.22
    npm: 12.1.0
    pnpm: 12.6.0
    bun: 1.4.2
```

No `npmPackages` section was emitted in the isolated directory. Installed package manifests confirm `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin` 1.2.5, Miniflare 5.20260921.1-alpha, workerd 1.20260921.1, Wrangler 4.138.0 and Vitest 4.1.11. `create-cloudflare` is not installed. The reproduction uses these unmodified packages; no dependency patch is required.

The host meets the [Wrangler system requirements](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/install-and-update/): macOS 13.5+ and a supported Node.js release. No host limits were changed.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction

https://gist.github.com/alexminza/46c544c5f8ddb85d4d1e448a17e6eeab

### Describe the Bug

Workflow-wide introspection creates mutation resources for every recorded instance, even when the caller only lists handles or reads completed status. Disposing an unused workflow introspector also acquires every modifier and starts cleanup for every instance concurrently. This makes local test inspection and cleanup scale with total instance count rather than bounded in-flight work.

**Expected:** listing handles or reading status should not acquire unused mutation resources. Cleanup should avoid constructing unused modifiers and should bound concurrent per-instance operations while still cleaning every recorded instance. No specific concurrency value or public API change is prescribed.

**Actual:** with 1,000 recorded IDs, `introspector.get()` acquires 1,000 modifiers without any `modify()` call. Calling `dispose()` without first calling `get()`, `modify()` or `modifyAll()` also acquires 1,000 modifiers and starts 1,000 concurrent abort operations.

#### Reproduction

1. Save `workflow-introspection-fanout.mjs` from the linked reproduction into an empty directory.
2. Follow its header's pinned dependency installation command, then run `node workflow-introspection-fanout.mjs`.
3. Observe the two diagnostic records and failing regression assertions below. The process exits with code 1 normally, without a runtime crash.

The single file generates a Vitest config and test in a new local directory. It calls the actual published `cloudflare:test` introspector with a counting binding double. The double supplies 1,000 synthetic IDs and makes abort completion asynchronous so overlap is observable. It does not replace the introspector implementation. This is a deterministic helper-call reproduction, **not** a file-descriptor measurement or an end-to-end Workflow execution test. No credentials, remote bindings or file-limit changes are needed.

#### Source path

In the [pinned introspector implementation](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/blob/miniflare%405.20260921.1-alpha/packages/workflows-shared/src/introspection.ts):

- `WorkflowInstanceIntrospectorHandle` starts `unsafeGetInstanceModifier()` in its constructor and retains the result.
- `WorkflowIntrospectorHandle.get()` constructs one such handle for every recorded ID.
- `stopIntrospectionSession()` synchronizes those handles during disposal even if `get()` was never called.
- `disposeInstanceIntrospectors()` starts every disposal through `Promise.all()` with no concurrency bound.

#### Separate native-runtime evidence

A prior local experiment used 1,000 real one-step Workflows, created in batches of 100 and checked complete before the next batch. That experiment used `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin` 1.1.13 with Miniflare 5.20260918.0-alpha / workerd 1.20260918.1 and the **experimental engine cleanup described in [#15809](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/issues/15809)**. The introspector itself was unchanged. The engine patch allowed completed instances to become idle, isolating the additional effect of reopening them for inspection.

| Operation | Native open-file handles |
| --- | ---: |
| Complete all instances, then idle | 37 |
| Read every native status/output, then idle | 37 |
| Call `introspector.get()` without modifications | 3,037, retained through 40 seconds of inspection/status-read idle periods |
| Dispose after inspection | Returns to 37 |
| Separate run: dispose without ever calling `get()` | Briefly reaches 3,037, then returns to 37 |

Counts came from macOS `proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDLISTFDS)`. Both native diagnostic tests passed and exited normally. These numbers are **not measurements from the unmodified-package reproduction above**. They demonstrate the resource impact under the isolated engine experiment, not a validated engine fix or a deployed Cloudflare Workflows defect.

#### Related reports

- [#15809](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/issues/15809) concerns completed engines retaining file handles without Vitest introspection. This report concerns inspection/cleanup reopening and retaining resources even after execution resources can be released.
- [PR #15708](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15708) remains open. At inspected head `9c13670657fcc109e4fe632d2bf3660c64ff8aaa`, it releases modifiers during disposal, but leaves constructor-time acquisition and workflow-wide cleanup fan-out unchanged. This report is complementary to that cleanup fix.

### Please provide any relevant error logs

The unmodified-package reproduction printed:

```json
{"phase":"read-only-get","modifierAcquisitions":1000,"abortCalls":0,"peakConcurrentAborts":0}
{"phase":"dispose-without-get","modifierAcquisitions":1000,"abortCalls":1000,"peakConcurrentAborts":1000}
```

Both regression tests failed as expected: modifier acquisition was 1,000 instead of zero, and peak cleanup concurrency equaled the entire 1,000-instance set. Runtime infrastructure completed normally; these are assertion failures, not an injected resource-exhaustion crash.

## References

- [Introspector at the reproduced Miniflare release](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/blob/miniflare%405.20260921.1-alpha/packages/workflows-shared/src/introspection.ts) — owns eager modifier acquisition, workflow-wide synchronization and disposal fan-out.
- [Introspector at the inspected disposal PR head](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/blob/9c13670657fcc109e4fe632d2bf3660c64ff8aaa/packages/workflows-shared/src/introspection.ts) — modifier disposal changes do not remove eager acquisition or bound workflow-wide cleanup.
- [Workers RPC lifecycle](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/rpc/lifecycle/) — explains why retained RPC stubs matter to execution-context lifetimes and require explicit disposal.

issues.title: Clarify SQLite Durable Object PITR residual retention and bookmark expiry
issues.body:
### Existing documentation URL(s)

- https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/sqlite-storage-api/#pitr-point-in-time-recovery-api
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/sqlite-storage-api/#deleteall
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/reference/durable-objects-migrations/#delete-a-durable-object-class

### What changes are you suggesting?

The PITR API documents recovery to points in the past 30 days, and the class-deletion page says stored data is removed permanently. Neither explicitly gives a maximum age for *all platform copies capable of reconstructing deleted SQL/KV content*, nor says when a retained bookmark expires. Cloudflare's [Storage Relay Service description](https://blog.cloudflare.com/sqlite-in-durable-objects/#bonus-feature-point-in-time-recovery) says obsolete logs and snapshots are **marked** for deletion 30 days later, but does not give a no-later-than deletion bound. For public self-service Workers Paid (no Enterprise arrangement or private exception), could the docs give a product-level statement or explicitly say that no such guarantee is currently published for:

1. The latest time after a SQL row deletion, table drop, successful `deleteAll()`, or namespace/class deletion by which *every* log, snapshot (including a current snapshot), follower buffer, object-storage copy, backup/replica, and internal metadata copy capable of reconstructing that content becomes irrecoverable. If there is a finite bound, what event starts its clock (commit, obsolescence, replacement snapshot, `deleteAll()`, deallocation, etc.), and is completion of deletion bounded separately from scheduling/marking it?
2. The expiry/invalidity rules for bookmarks returned by `getCurrentBookmark()`, `getBookmarkForTime()`, and the undo bookmark from `onNextSessionRestoreBookmark()`. Can a stored bookmark restore a state older than the 30-day **timestamp lookup** window? What precisely happens at day 30 (boundary and authoritative clock), and what error/result is returned for an expired bookmark?

Please distinguish the documented recovery lookback from a residual-data maximum; if either bound is not guaranteed on self-service Workers Paid, saying so explicitly would help applications avoid interpreting a restore-lookup limit as proof of deletion.

### Additional information

A hosted test restored deleted SQL/KV through an earlier bookmark after successful `deleteAll()` and same-object reaccess. That is an observation, not a purge or maximum-retention measurement. We need a documented, generally applicable retention/expiry statement to reason about sensitive-data lifecycles, rather than an account-specific support exception.

repository.name: quiche
repository.description: 🥧 Savoury implementation of the QUIC transport protocol and HTTP/3

issues.title: BBRv2 connection can stay in PROBE_RTT indefinitely: exit condition is missing the minimum-window clause from the reference implementation
issues.body:
## Problem Description

In gcongestion BBRv2, the only way to leave PROBE_RTT is to first drain `bytes_in_flight` below `inflight_target` (0.5 × BDP), which arms a 200ms exit timer. However, the congestion window a sender can actually drain down to is floored at the *initial* congestion window, and that floor is applied **after** the PROBE_RTT mode cap. When `0.5 × BDP < initial_cwnd`, a continuously saturated sender keeps `bytes_in_flight` pinned near `initial_cwnd`, the drain condition can never be satisfied, the exit timer is never armed, and the connection remains in PROBE_RTT indefinitely with cwnd pinned at `initial_cwnd`. There is no wall-clock fallback.

Google quiche (the reference this implementation is ported from) has a second clause in the exit check that makes this state unreachable; the port dropped it.

Found by code inspection while comparing the port against the reference implementation; not (yet) tied to a production incident. It is adjacent to, but distinct from, #2496 — that report is about never *entering* PROBE_RTT; this one is about never *leaving* it.

## Reference implementation behavior

Google quiche arms the exit timer when in-flight drops below the inflight target **or** below the minimum congestion window ([`bbr2_probe_rtt.cc`](https://github.com/google/quiche/blob/main/quiche/quic/core/congestion_control/bbr2_probe_rtt.cc#L28-L41)):

```cpp
if (exit_time_ == QuicTime::Zero()) {
    if (congestion_event.bytes_in_flight <= InflightTarget() ||
        congestion_event.bytes_in_flight <=
            sender_->GetMinimumCongestionWindow()) {
      exit_time_ = congestion_event.event_time + Params().probe_rtt_duration;
```

`GetMinimumCongestionWindow()` is `cwnd_limits().Min()` — the same lower bound the sender's cwnd is clamped by. That makes the check exhaustive over both clamp outcomes: either the PROBE_RTT cap wins (`cwnd ≤ target`, so in-flight reaches the first clause) or the floor wins (`cwnd == min window`, so in-flight reaches the second clause). Either way the timer is armed within roughly one RTT, so PROBE_RTT cannot wedge.

## Relevant Source Code (0.29.3)

The port only kept the first clause ([`bbr2/probe_rtt.rs:96-105`](https://github.com/cloudflare/quiche/blob/0.29.3/quiche/src/recovery/gcongestion/bbr2/probe_rtt.rs#L96-L105)):

```rust
match self.exit_time {
    None => {
        if congestion_event.bytes_in_flight <=
            self.inflight_target(params)
        {
            self.exit_time = Some(
                congestion_event.event_time + params.probe_rtt_duration,
            )
        }
```

`inflight_target` is bare `0.5 × BDP(max_bandwidth)` with no floor ([`probe_rtt.rs:71-77`](https://github.com/cloudflare/quiche/blob/0.29.3/quiche/src/recovery/gcongestion/bbr2/probe_rtt.rs#L71-L77)).

Meanwhile the cwnd update applies the PROBE_RTT cap first, then the global limits ([`bbr2.rs:603-621`](https://github.com/cloudflare/quiche/blob/0.29.3/quiche/src/recovery/gcongestion/bbr2.rs#L603-L621)):

```rust
self.cwnd = self
    .mode
    .get_cwnd_limits(&self.params)   // no_greater_than(min(…, inflight_target))
    .apply_limits(self.cwnd);
self.cwnd = self.cwnd_limits.apply_limits(self.cwnd);  // .max(lo).min(hi)
```

with `cwnd_limits.lo` set to the initial congestion window ([`bbr2.rs:517-520`](https://github.com/cloudflare/quiche/blob/0.29.3/quiche/src/recovery/gcongestion/bbr2.rs#L517-L520)). So the effective window in PROBE_RTT is `max(min(cwnd, 0.5 × BDP), initial_cwnd)`; when the target is below the floor, the cap is overridden entirely.

Since `probe_rtt_pacing_gain` and `probe_rtt_cwnd_gain` are both 1.0 ([`bbr2.rs:311-313`](https://github.com/cloudflare/quiche/blob/0.29.3/quiche/src/recovery/gcongestion/bbr2.rs#L311-L313)), the cwnd cap is the *only* drain mechanism PROBE_RTT has — and in this parameter region it is exactly the part that gets overridden.

## Failure scenario

- `initial_congestion_window` = 100 packets ≈ 135 KB (MSS 1350).
- Path: `max_bandwidth` ≈ 1 Gbps, `min_rtt` ≈ 1.6 ms → BDP ≈ 200 KB, `inflight_target` = 100 KB < 135 KB.
- A bulk transfer keeps the pipe saturated: in-flight hovers at cwnd = 135 KB, dipping by the size of each ACK aggregate when a congestion event is processed.
- Arming the exit timer requires a single event to observe in-flight ≤ 100 KB, i.e. > 35 KB acknowledged at once. Depending on ACK aggregation this may occasionally happen — or never. Until it does, the connection sits in PROBE_RTT at `initial_cwnd`, and only an application-limited dip or full quiescence (`on_exit_quiescence`) can rescue it.

Large initial windows on low-RTT paths make this region easy to reach; the trigger probability is timing-dependent, which also makes it hard to reproduce deterministically — the stuck state is directly visible in qlog as `bbr_probe_rtt` persisting far beyond `probe_rtt_duration`.

A secondary divergence from the reference widens the affected region: Google's global floor is the constant `kDefaultMinimumCongestionWindow = 4 × MSS` ([`bbr2_misc.h`](https://github.com/google/quiche/blob/main/quiche/quic/core/congestion_control/bbr2_misc.h#L69-L73), [`bbr2_sender.cc:66`](https://github.com/google/quiche/blob/main/quiche/quic/core/congestion_control/bbr2_sender.cc#L66)), whereas the port floors at the initial window. With the missing clause, Google's floor would confine the problem to BDP < ~11 KB (practically unreachable); flooring at a large initial window turns it into a reachable configuration.

## Suggested fix

Restore the reference's second clause:

```rust
if congestion_event.bytes_in_flight <= self.inflight_target(params) ||
    congestion_event.bytes_in_flight <= cwnd_lower_limit
{
```

where `cwnd_lower_limit` is the sender's `cwnd_limits.min()` (needs to be plumbed into `ProbeRTT::on_congestion_event`, e.g. alongside the existing `cwnd` argument). Under the current floor semantics this makes PROBE_RTT degrade to a plain 200ms dwell when the target is below the floor — the min_rtt sample may read high, but liveness is preserved, matching the reference behavior.

Whether the floor itself should follow Google (`4 × MSS` instead of the initial window) is a separate question with much broader behavioral impact; this report only proposes restoring the exit-condition clause.

issues.title: Server keeps PTO timer armed at the anti-amplification limit
issues.body:
# Server keeps PTO timer armed at the anti-amplification limit

## Summary
When a server has exhausted its anti-amplification budget before address validation, [RFC 9002 Section 6.2.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9002.html#section-6.2.2.1) requires that the server's PTO timer not be armed. quiche enforces the send budget in `send()` but leaves the recovery timer armed after the last allowed flight exhausts `max_send_bytes`.

## Standard Requirement

[RFC 9002 Section 6.2.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9002.html#section-6.2.2.1):

```text
If no additional data can be sent, the server's PTO timer MUST NOT be
armed until datagrams have been received from the client because
packets sent on PTO count against the anti-amplification limit.

When the server receives a datagram from the client, the
amplification limit is increased and the server resets the PTO timer.
If the PTO timer is then set to a time in the past, it is executed
immediately.
```

[RFC 9002 Appendix A.8](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9002.html#appendix-A.8) models the timer rule as:

```text
if (server is at anti-amplification limit):
  loss_detection_timer.cancel()
  return
```

So the required state is simple: unvalidated server + no remaining send budget means no armed PTO timer.

## Relevant Source Code

`quiche/src/lib.rs:4024` limits server output by `max_send_bytes` before address validation:

```rust
if !send_path.verified_peer_address && self.is_server {
    left = cmp::min(left, send_path.max_send_bytes);
}
```

`quiche/src/lib.rs:5496` deducts the budget after a packet is written and records when it reaches zero:

```rust
let had_send_budget = path.max_send_bytes > 0;
path.max_send_bytes = path.max_send_bytes.saturating_sub(written);
if self.is_server &&
    !path.verified_peer_address &&
    had_send_budget &&
    path.max_send_bytes == 0
{
    self.amplification_limited_count =
        self.amplification_limited_count.saturating_add(1);
}
```

`quiche/src/recovery/congestion/recovery.rs:504` has no server-at-limit cancellation branch:

```rust
if self.bytes_in_flight.is_zero() &&
    handshake_status.peer_verified_address
{
    self.loss_timer.clear();
    return;
}

if let (Some(timeout), _) = self.pto_time_and_space(handshake_status, now)
{
    self.loss_timer.update(timeout);
} else {
    self.loss_timer.clear();
}
```

`quiche/src/recovery/gcongestion/recovery.rs:662` has the same timer logic for gcongestion.

## Implementation Behavior

The server send path correctly stops sending once `max_send_bytes` reaches zero. However, the recovery layer does not know that the server is now anti-amplification limited. It can keep a PTO/loss timer armed even though no additional PTO packet may be sent until another client datagram increases the budget.

## Inconsistency Reason

[RFC 9002 Section 6.2.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9002.html#section-6.2.2.1) requires canceling the server PTO timer while the server is blocked by the anti-amplification limit. quiche only applies the limit at packet generation time and does not clear the recovery timer when the last allowed packet consumes the remaining budget. This leaves `loss_detection_timer` armed in a state where the standard says it must not be armed.

## Runtime Evidence

The focused anti-amplification timer test was run from `implementions/quiche`:

```text
cargo test -p quiche codex_tmp_server_amp_limited_must_disarm_pto_timer --features gcongestion --release -- --nocapture
```

The command exited with code `101`, which is the expected reproducer signal for the failing assertions below.

Observed output:

```text
cubic: client_sent=1200 server_sent=3600 max_send_bytes=0 verified_peer_address=false loss_timer_armed=true
bbr2_gcongestion: client_sent=1200 server_sent=3600 max_send_bytes=0 verified_peer_address=false loss_timer_armed=true

test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 2 failed
```

The failure is the expected reproducer signal: the server is unvalidated and has no remaining send budget, but the timer is still armed for both legacy CUBIC and BBR2/gcongestion.

## Impact

The application can observe a PTO/loss timeout while the server is not allowed to send PTO probes. This diverges from [RFC 9002 Section 6.2.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9002.html#section-6.2.2.1)'s anti-amplification timer state and can cause unnecessary timeout wakeups or incorrect PTO handling around handshake blocking.

## Fix Direction

Make timer scheduling aware of the server anti-amplification state. When the active path is unvalidated and `max_send_bytes == 0`, clear the PTO/loss timer. When a client datagram increases the budget, re-run loss timer setup and execute the timeout immediately if the recomputed timer is already in the past.
