issues.title: Support ML-DSA (FIPS 204) post-quantum signature algorithms for certificate signing
issues.body:
France's ANSSI will [stop certifying non-PQC products from 2027](https://gizmodo.com/the-quantum-threat-to-encryption-is-coming-france-just-set-a-2027-deadline-2000773650). The US [Executive Order 14409](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/06/securing-the-nation-against-advanced-cryptographic-attacks/) mandates PQC for all federal systems, with key establishment by 2030 and digital signatures by 2031. Australia's ASD/ACSC has published [post-quantum vendor guidance](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/secure-design/quantum/post-quantum-questions-to-ask-your-vendors) urging organizations to assess PQC readiness across their supply chain.

## Context

cfssl is Cloudflare's widely used PKI toolkit for certificate signing, bundling, and verification. While Cloudflare has been a leader in deploying PQC at the network level (X25519MLKEM768 enabled across their CDN), cfssl itself has zero post-quantum algorithm support.

Organizations using cfssl to run internal CAs cannot issue ML-DSA signed certificates, even though NIST standardized ML-DSA (FIPS 204) in August 2024.

## Proposal

Add ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and ML-DSA-87 as supported key/signature types in cfssl:

1. **Key generation**: `cfssl genkey` with `-algo mldsa65` support
2. **Certificate signing**: CA signing with ML-DSA keys
3. **CSR handling**: Parse and validate ML-DSA CSRs
4. **Hybrid support**: Consider hybrid RSA+ML-DSA or ECDSA+ML-DSA certificates for transition

Go 1.27 will ship `crypto/mldsa` in stdlib. Until then, `filippo.io/mldsa` provides a bridge implementation.

## References

- [NIST FIPS 204 (ML-DSA)](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/204/final)
- [US Executive Order 14409](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/06/securing-the-nation-against-advanced-cryptographic-attacks/)
- [Australia ASD PQC Vendor Guidance](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/secure-design/quantum/post-quantum-questions-to-ask-your-vendors)

issues.title: Support Go native FIPS 140 mode (GODEBUG=fips140=only)
issues.body:
Go 1.24 introduced native FIPS 140-3 support via `GODEBUG=fips140=only`, which rejects all non-FIPS algorithms at runtime, including `crypto/sha1`.

 cfssl uses `SHA-1` in several hardcoded places that can't be configured:

1. `ComputeSKI()`: hardcoded `sha1.Sum()` for `SubjectKeyId` computation, no option to use SHA-256
2. `FillTemplate()`: unconditionally calls `ComputeSKI()`, overwriting any pre-set SubjectKeyId
3. Various helpers: use crypto primitives that trigger `fips140=only` panics

While SHA-1 for SKI is recommended by [`RFC 5280 §4.2.1.2`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.2:~:text=Other%20methods%20of%20generating%20unique%20numbers%20are%20also%20acceptable.), it's not mandatory, the RFC allows any method that provides unique identification. SHA-256 truncated to 20 bytes is a FIPS-compliant alternative.

Suggested fixes (any of):
    - Make the SKI hash algorithm configurable (default `SHA-1`, option for `SHA-256`)
    - Don't overwrite `SubjectKeyId` in `FillTemplate` if the caller already set it
    - Detect `fips140=only` at runtime and switch to SHA-256 automatically

issues.title: crl_override (and extensions) in /api/v1/sign request body are silently ignored by the HTTP API
issues.body:
Version: 1.6.5 (also present on master as of this writing) · Go 1.20.14

## Summary
signer.SignRequest defines a CRLOverride field (JSON tag crl_override) that the local signer honors to set a per-request CRL Distribution Point. However, when signing through the HTTP /api/v1/sign (and /api/v1/authsign) API, the field is silently dropped. The issued certificate contains no CRL Distribution Points extension (2.5.29.31), and no error or warning is returned. The same applies to the extensions field.

## Expected behavior
Posting crl_override to /api/v1/sign embeds a CRLDistributionPoints (2.5.29.31) extension in the issued certificate, matching the behavior of the local signer library and the documented SignRequest schema.

## Actual behavior
The request succeeds, but the returned certificate has no 2.5.29.31 extension. crl_override is accepted (no validation error) yet has no effect.

## Root cause
The HTTP handler does not unmarshal the body into `signer.SignRequest`. It uses an intermediate `jsonSignRequest` struct, then `jsonReqToTrue()` copies only a fixed subset of fields into the real SignRequest. Neither `crl_override` nor extensions is part of that struct or the copy:

api/signhandler/signhandler.go:

```
// This type is meant to be unmarshalled from JSON so that there can be a
// hostname field in the API
// TODO: Change the API such that the normal struct can be used.
type jsonSignRequest struct {
	Hostname string          `json:"hostname"`
	Hosts    []string        `json:"hosts"`
	Request  string          `json:"certificate_request"`
	Subject  *signer.Subject `json:"subject,omitempty"`
	Profile  string          `json:"profile"`
	Label    string          `json:"label"`
	Serial   *big.Int        `json:"serial,omitempty"`
	Bundle   bool            `json:"bundle"`
}
func jsonReqToTrue(js jsonSignRequest) signer.SignRequest {
	// ... never sets CRLOverride or Extensions ...
	return signer.SignRequest{
		Hosts:   js.Hosts,
		Subject: sub,
		Request: js.Request,
		Profile: js.Profile,
		Label:   js.Label,
		Serial:  js.Serial,
	}
}
```

By contrast, signer/local/local.go does honor CRLOverride (so it works when CFSSL is used as a Go library), which makes the API behavior surprising:

```
if req.CRLOverride != "" {
	safeTemplate.CRLDistributionPoints = []string{req.CRLOverride}
}
// ... preserved across FillTemplate via save/restore of distPoints ...
```
The existing `TODO: Change the API such that the normal struct can be used.` comment acknowledges this divergence.

## Steps to reproduce

Run a CFSSL server with any signing profile (no crl_url set in config.json):
```
cfssl serve -address 0.0.0.0 -port 8888 -ca ca.pem -ca-key ca-key.pem -config config.json
```

Sign a CSR via the HTTP API with crl_override:
```
curl -s http://localhost:8888/api/v1/cfssl/sign -d '{
  "certificate_request": "'"$(awk 'NF {sub(/\r/,""); printf "%s\\n",$0}' test.csr)"'",
  "crl_override": "http://example.com/my.crl"
}' | jq -r '.result.certificate' > out.pem
```

Inspect the issued certificate:
```
openssl x509 -in out.pem -noout -text | grep -A2 "CRL Distribution"
# (no output — extension is absent)
```

Observed: no X509v3 CRL Distribution Points in the certificate. 
Expected: the extension present with URI http://example.com/my.crl.


## Workaround
Set crl_url in the signing profile (config.json), which FillTemplate applies server-side:
```
{ "signing": { "default": { "crl_url": "http://example.com/my.crl", "expiry": "8760h", "usages": ["signing","server auth"] } } }
```

This works but is static per-profile and cannot vary per request.

## Suggested fix
Add CRLOverride string \json:"crl_override"`(andExtensions) to jsonSignRequestand copy them in both branches ofjsonReqToTrue(), or follow the existing TODO and unmarshal directly into signer.SignRequest`. Alternatively, if per-request override is intentionally unsupported over HTTP, document it and return a validation error when these fields are supplied.

issues.title: Brotli response compression never finishes the stream (flush instead of finish), strict decoders reject every `br` body
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

`Compressor::encode` in `pingora-core/src/protocols/http/compression/brotli.rs` handles `end == true` by calling `flush()` on the `brotli::CompressorWriter`.
`flush()` runs `BROTLI_OPERATION_FLUSH`, which emits the pending data but never the final `ISLAST` meta-block.
Nothing ever runs `BROTLI_OPERATION_FINISH` (that only happens in `into_inner()` or `Drop`, and the output `Vec` has already been taken with `mem::take` by then).

The result is that every `Content-Encoding: br` body Pingora produces is a valid prefix of a brotli stream with no end-of-stream marker.

Lenient decoders (curl, Chrome, Firefox) return the full body and never complain, so this is easy to miss.
Strict decoders reject it:

- Google's `brotli` CLI: `corrupt input`
- Node `zlib.brotliDecompressSync`: `Z_BUF_ERROR`
- Node `zlib.createBrotliDecompress()` (what `fetch` / undici use): `unexpected end of file`

Node's `fetch` sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br` by default, so any Node client behind a Pingora proxy with `ResponseCompressionBuilder` enabled gets a failed body read on every response.
Gzip (`try_finish()`) and zstd finish their streams correctly; only brotli is affected.

The code on `main` today is unchanged from 0.9.0 in this respect.

## Pingora info

pingora-core 0.9.0 (also `main` at the time of filing), brotli 8.0.4, Linux and macOS.

## Steps to reproduce

Standalone, without a running proxy.
This does exactly what `Compressor::encode` does on `end`, and compares it with a finished stream.

`Cargo.toml`

```toml
[package]
name = "br-repro"
version = "0.0.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
brotli = "=8.0.4"
```

`src/main.rs`

```rust
use std::io::Write;
use brotli::CompressorWriter;

fn main() {
    let body = b"<html><body>hello, world</body></html>".repeat(20);

    // What pingora-core 0.9.0 does on `end`: write_all + flush, then take the Vec.
    let mut w = CompressorWriter::new(Vec::new(), 4096, 6, 19);
    w.write_all(&body).unwrap();
    w.flush().unwrap();
    let flushed = std::mem::take(w.get_mut());

    // A finished stream: into_inner runs BROTLI_OPERATION_FINISH.
    let mut w2 = CompressorWriter::new(Vec::new(), 4096, 6, 19);
    w2.write_all(&body).unwrap();
    let finished = w2.into_inner();

    std::fs::write("flushed.br", &flushed).unwrap();
    std::fs::write("finished.br", &finished).unwrap();
    println!("flushed={} bytes finished={} bytes", flushed.len(), finished.len());
}
```

```sh
cargo run -q
# flushed=44 bytes finished=43 bytes

brotli -d -c flushed.br > /dev/null
# corrupt input [flushed.br]   (exit 1)

brotli -d -c finished.br | wc -c
# 760                          (exit 0)

node -e 'require("fs").createReadStream("flushed.br").pipe(require("zlib").createBrotliDecompress()).on("error", e => console.log(e.code, e.message)).resume()'
# Z_BUF_ERROR unexpected end of file
```

Appending the one-byte empty last meta-block (`0x03`, i.e. `ISLAST=1, ISLASTEMPTY=1`) to `flushed.br` makes it decode to bytes identical to `finished.br`, which confirms the only thing missing is the finish step.

Against a live Pingora proxy with `ResponseCompressionBuilder::enable(6)`:

```sh
curl -sS -H 'Accept-Encoding: br' https://<any host behind pingora>/ \
  | node -e 'process.stdin.pipe(require("zlib").createBrotliDecompress()).on("error", e => console.log(e.message)).resume()'
# unexpected end of file
```

The same request with `Accept-Encoding: gzip` decodes cleanly.

## Expected behavior

When `end` is true the encoder should finish the stream so the output is a complete brotli stream that strict decoders accept, matching what the gzip compressor does with `try_finish()`.

## Observed results

strict decode errors

issues.title: check_regions rejects "CHINA", so China Network load balancer pools cannot be managed
issues.body:
### Confirmation

- [X] This is a bug with an existing resource and is not a feature request or enhancement.
- [X] I have searched the issue tracker and my issue isn't already found.
- [X] I have replicated my issue using the latest version of the provider and it is still present.

### Terraform and Cloudflare provider version

```
Terraform v1.15.8
on windows_amd64
+ provider registry.terraform.io/cloudflare/cloudflare v5.23.0
```

Also reproduced on v5.22.0.

### Affected resource(s)

- `cloudflare_load_balancer_pool`
- `cloudflare_healthcheck`

### Terraform configuration files

```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    cloudflare = {
      source  = "cloudflare/cloudflare"
      version = "5.23.0"
    }
  }
}

resource "cloudflare_load_balancer_pool" "example" {
  account_id    = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
  name          = "example-pool"
  check_regions = ["CHINA"]
  origins = [{
    address = "203.0.113.10"
    enabled = true
    name    = "example-origin"
    weight  = 1
  }]
}

resource "cloudflare_healthcheck" "example" {
  zone_id       = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
  name          = "example-healthcheck"
  address       = "203.0.113.10"
  type          = "HTTPS"
  check_regions = ["CHINA"]
}
```

### Link to debug output

https://gist.github.com/sgreinerCNS/6b71fce2a2261640f16d8a07237b4498

### Panic output

_No response_

### Expected output

`check_regions = ["CHINA"]` is accepted, so a load balancer pool that health-checks
from the China region can be declared and managed in Terraform.

`CHINA` is a real, live value for this attribute: on an account with China Network
enabled, the dashboard offers **China** under a pool's *Health Monitor Regions*, and
the REST API then returns that pool as:

```json
"check_regions": ["CHINA"]
```

`cf-terraforming generate --resource-type cloudflare_load_balancer_pool` reproduces
it faithfully, emitting `check_regions = ["CHINA"]` — config the provider then
refuses to accept.

### Actual output

The attribute is rejected by a schema-level enum validator, so it fails at
`terraform validate`, before any API call:

```
Error: Invalid Attribute Value Match

  with cloudflare_load_balancer_pool.example,
  on main.tf line 13, in resource "cloudflare_load_balancer_pool" "example":
  13:   check_regions = ["CHINA"]

Attribute check_regions[0] value must be one of: ["WNAM" "ENAM" "WEU" "EEU"
"NSAM" "SSAM" "OC" "ME" "NAF" "SAF" "SAS" "SEAS" "NEAS" "ALL_REGIONS"], got:
"CHINA"

Error: Invalid Attribute Value Match

  with cloudflare_healthcheck.example,
  on main.tf line 27, in resource "cloudflare_healthcheck" "example":
  27:   check_regions = ["CHINA"]

Attribute check_regions[0] value must be one of: ["WNAM" "ENAM" "WEU" "EEU"
"NSAM" "SSAM" "OC" "ME" "NAF" "SAF" "IN" "SEAS" "NEAS" "ALL_REGIONS"], got:
"CHINA"
```

### Steps to reproduce

Minimal (no Cloudflare credentials or China Network entitlement needed — the
validator runs during `ValidateResourceConfig`):

1. Save the configuration above as `main.tf`.
2. `terraform init`
3. `terraform validate` → both errors above.

How it shows up in practice, adopting an existing China Network pool:

1. On an account with China Network enabled, create a load balancer pool in the
   dashboard and set *Health Monitor Regions* to **China**.
2. `terraform import cloudflare_load_balancer_pool.example <account_id>/<pool_id>`
   succeeds, and state correctly holds `check_regions = ["CHINA"]`.
3. Generating config for it — via `import` block plus
   `terraform plan -generate-config-out=`, or via `cf-terraforming` — emits
   `check_regions = ["CHINA"]`.
4. That generated config fails validation, so the pool cannot be expressed in HCL.
   `-generate-config-out` reports the error against the file it just wrote:

   ```
   Error: Invalid Attribute Value Match

     with cloudflare_load_balancer_pool.example,
     on generated.tf line 2:
     (source code not available)

   Attribute check_regions[0] value must be one of: [...], got: "CHINA"
   ```

### Additional factoids

**Omitting the attribute is not a workaround.** `check_regions` is `optional` and
not `computed`, so leaving it out plans `["CHINA"] -> null`, and per the attribute's
own description ("Null means every Cloudflare data center") applying that would
widen health checks from China-only to every data center — a live behaviour change,
and a permanent diff until it is applied. The only way I found to adopt such a pool
without changing it is to leave `check_regions` out of the config and pin the live
value in state:

```hcl
lifecycle {
  ignore_changes = [check_regions]
}
```

That keeps `terraform plan` clean, at the cost of the attribute going out as null
if the resource is ever recreated.

**Likely upstream.** Cloudflare's own API documentation for
[Create Pool](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/load_balancers/subresources/pools/methods/create/)
lists the same 13 regions plus `ALL_REGIONS` and omits `CHINA`, so the provider's
validator appears to mirror the OpenAPI schema accurately and the fix probably
belongs in the schema the provider is generated from.

**Minor, possibly unrelated:** the two enums differ by one element — the pool list
has `SAS` where the healthcheck list has `IN`. That may well be intentional; noting
it in case it isn't.

### References

I could not find an existing issue or PR for this.

issues.title: cloudflare_bot_management: bot_preference_sync_enabled is never sent or read, update fails with "inconsistent result after apply"
issues.body:
### Confirmation

- [X] This is a bug with an existing resource and is not a feature request or enhancement.
- [X] I have searched the issue tracker and my issue isn't already found.
- [X] I have replicated my issue using the latest version of the provider and it is still present.

### Terraform and Cloudflare provider version

```
Terraform v1.16.2
on windows_amd64
+ provider registry.terraform.io/cloudflare/cloudflare v5.25.0
```

### Affected resource(s)

- `cloudflare_bot_management`

### Terraform configuration files

```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    cloudflare = {
      source  = "cloudflare/cloudflare"
      version = "5.25.0"
    }
  }
}

resource "cloudflare_bot_management" "example" {
  zone_id                     = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
  ai_bots_protection          = "block"
  auto_update_model           = true
  bm_cookie_enabled           = true
  bot_preference_sync_enabled = true
  crawler_protection          = "disabled"
  enable_js                   = false
  is_robots_txt_managed       = false
  suppress_session_score      = false
}
```

### Link to debug output

https://gist.github.com/sgreinerCNS/3c0d44c4cd70826b906aaa248690ee6c

The gist is an excerpt of the relevant parts (the refresh GET, then the failing
PUT with its response and the error); IDs, names and cookies are redacted.

### Panic output

_No response_

### Expected output

`bot_preference_sync_enabled`, added in v5.25.0, is sent to the API on create and
update, read back on refresh, and the apply completes with the value in state.

The API does return the field. The `cloudflare_bot_management` data source reads
it correctly (for example `bot_preference_sync_enabled = true` on a zone where
the dashboard's managed robots.txt toggle is on), so it is available to the
resource as well.

### Actual output

Every apply that changes the attribute on an existing resource fails:

```
Error: Provider produced inconsistent result after apply

When applying changes to cloudflare_bot_management.example, provider
"provider[\"registry.terraform.io/cloudflare/cloudflare\"]" produced an
unexpected new value: .bot_preference_sync_enabled: was cty.True, but now null.

This is a bug in the provider, which should be reported in the provider's own
issue tracker.
```

The value also never reaches Cloudflare. The debug log shows the request body
of the `PUT /client/v4/zones/<zone_id>/bot_management` without it:

```json
{"ai_bots_protection":"block","auto_update_model":true,"bm_cookie_enabled":true,"crawler_protection":"disabled","enable_js":false,"is_robots_txt_managed":false,"suppress_session_score":false}
```

The API response to that same request does contain the field
(`"bot_preference_sync_enabled": true`), so the provider receives the value and
discards it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Take a zone with Bot Management and bring its settings into state without the
   attribute: `terraform import cloudflare_bot_management.example <zone_id>`, or
   any state written by v5.24.0 or earlier.
2. Add `bot_preference_sync_enabled = true` to the configuration above.
3. `terraform plan` shows `+ bot_preference_sync_enabled = true`.
4. `terraform apply` fails with the error above.
5. Read the zone with `data "cloudflare_bot_management"`: the live value is
   unchanged, so nothing was sent.

`terraform plan` keeps showing the same change afterwards, because state holds
`null`, and every further apply fails the same way.

### Additional factoids

The attribute exists only in the Terraform model. It is missing from every code
path that talks to the API (all links at `v5.25.0`):

- **Never sent.** `BotManagementAPIModel`, the request and response struct in
  [`model.go`](https://github.com/cloudflare/terraform-provider-cloudflare/blob/v5.25.0/internal/services/bot_management/model.go#L18-L35),
  has no `bot_preference_sync_enabled` field, and
  [`ToAPIModel()`](https://github.com/cloudflare/terraform-provider-cloudflare/blob/v5.25.0/internal/services/bot_management/model.go#L86-L109)
  has no line for `BotPreferenceSyncEnabled`, so the value is dropped from the
  request body.
- **Never read.**
  [`UpdateFromAPIModel()`](https://github.com/cloudflare/terraform-provider-cloudflare/blob/v5.25.0/internal/services/bot_management/model.go#L158)
  does not set `BotPreferenceSyncEnabled`, so refresh never picks up the live
  value and a plan cannot show drift on it.
- **Overwritten on update.**
  [`Update()`](https://github.com/cloudflare/terraform-provider-cloudflare/blob/v5.25.0/internal/services/bot_management/resource.go#L154)
  does `*data = *state` before `UpdateFromAPIModel()`, so the planned value is
  replaced by the prior state (`null`), which produces the error. On create the
  planned value survives, so a create "succeeds" without the value being sent.

The v5.25.0 changelog entry "mark `bot_preference_sync_enabled` optional-only;
`Computed` caused 'unknown after apply' errors" looks like the same root cause
seen from the other side: with nothing reading the field from the API, a
computed value could never become known.

Why it matters: since Cloudflare's move to AI bot policies on 2026-09-15, the
dashboard's managed robots.txt toggle (AI Crawl Control) is backed by
`bot_preference_sync_enabled`, not `is_robots_txt_managed`. With the attribute
unmanageable, managed robots.txt can no longer be set through Terraform. The
only workaround is to leave the attribute out of the configuration and switch the
toggle in the dashboard.

**The same class of bug affects other attributes:**

- `content_bots_protection` is not sent either. `ToAPIModel()` has no line for
  `ContentBotsProtection`, although `BotManagementAPIModel` has the field. The
  configuration above sets `content_bots_protection = "disabled"`, and the request
  body in the log does not contain it.
- `cf_robots_variant` is absent from `BotManagementAPIModel`. The code comment says
  it "is not returned by API", but the response in the log returns
  `"cf_robots_variant": "off"`.
- The response also carries `ai_training`, `ai_search` and `ai_user`, which the
  resource does not model at all. The v5.25.0 changelog describes
  `bot_preference_sync_enabled` as syncing bot preferences from these three.

### References

I could not find an existing issue or PR for this.

issues.title: account_subscription: rate_plan.id enum rejects per-product subscription SKUs that the same API returns
issues.body:
`cloudflare_account_subscription` cannot represent 25 of 56 live subscriptions on our account with provider `5.25.0`, because `rate_plan.id` is validated against an enum of **account plans** while `GET /accounts/{id}/subscriptions` also returns **per-product subscription SKUs**.

## What happens

```
Error: Invalid Attribute Value Match

  on cloudflare_account_subscription.tf line 10, in resource "cloudflare_account_subscription" "...":
  Attribute rate_plan.id value must be one of: ["free" "lite" "pro" "pro_plus"
  "business" "enterprise" "partners_free" "partners_pro" "partners_business"
  "partners_enterprise"], got "ratelimiting_ipbased_ent"
```

Repeated 25 times, once per subscription.

## The values, from one real account

Configuration generated by `cf-terraforming` from the live API — these are what Cloudflare returned, unmodified:

| count | `rate_plan.id` | accepted |
|---:|---|---|
| 16 | `enterprise` | yes |
| 15 | `free` | yes |
| 4 | `ratelimiting_ipbased_ent` | **no** |
| 2 | `api_shield_zone` | **no** |
| 1 | `workers_ent` | **no** |
| 1 | `workers_for_platforms_ent` | **no** |
| 1 | `r2_ent` | **no** |
| 1 | `teams_ent` | **no** |
| 1 | `zero_trust_essential` | **no** |
| 1 | `zaraz_ent` | **no** |
| 1 | `bot_zone_ent` | **no** |
| 1 | `load_balancing_ent` | **no** |
| 1 | `advanced_cert_manager_account` | **no** |
| 1 | `app_sec_premier` | **no** |
| 1 | `app_performance_essential` | **no** |
| 1 | `smart_shield_argo_ent` | **no** |
| 1 | `smart_shield_argo_zone_ent` | **no** |
| 1 | `web3_ethereum_ent` | **no** |
| 1 | `web3_ipfs_ent` | **no** |
| 1 | `images_v2_stream_ent` | **no** |
| 1 | `core_base` | **no** |
| 1 | `rate_limiting` | **no** |
| 1 | `enterprise_customer_portal_standard` | **no** |

**31 accepted, 25 rejected, 56 total.**

## The mismatch

`internal/services/account_subscription/schema.go` validates `rate_plan.id` with `stringvalidator.OneOfCaseInsensitive` over ten values, all of which are *account plans*. But the subscriptions endpoint returns a row per **product subscription** as well — Workers, R2, Zero Trust, Argo, Bot Management, Images/Stream, Web3, and so on. Those SKUs are not account plans and will never appear in that list.

So the enum is not incomplete by a few values; it is enumerating a **different thing** from what the field carries. Adding `ratelimiting_ipbased_ent` and friends would be chasing an open-ended vendor SKU list.

## Suggested fix

Drop the `OneOfCaseInsensitive` validator on `rate_plan.id`, or relax it to a format check. A plan/SKU identifier is vendor-controlled, unbounded, and changes as products ship — the provider cannot usefully enumerate it, and validating it means the resource rejects data its own API produced.

The `Description` can keep listing the common account plans as guidance without the validator enforcing them.

## Impact

Any account with per-product subscriptions — which is any Enterprise account — cannot import or manage its subscriptions with this resource. It is not a partial limitation: we can represent the 15 `free` and 16 `enterprise` rows and none of the 25 product rows, which makes the resource unusable for its apparent purpose on exactly the accounts most likely to want it.

Happy to send a PR removing the validator if that is the direction you would take.

issues.title: Three more schema/model mismatches break state refresh: account_subscription, ai_search_instance, stream_download (like #7177, #7301)
issues.body:
## Summary

`cloudflare_account_subscription`, `cloudflare_ai_search_instance` and `cloudflare_stream_download` each declare a field in `model.go` with a `tfsdk` tag that `schema.go` never defines. Every read of those resources fails with a `Value Conversion Error`, which makes the resource type unusable rather than degraded.

This is the same defect as #7177 (`workers_script` / `propagation_policy`, fixed in #7186) and #7301 (`email_routing_settings` / `support_subaddress`, still open). Filing the remaining instances together because the interesting part is that there are exactly four, and one check would have caught all of them.

## The instances, at v5.25.0

| service | declared in `model.go` | present in `ResourceSchema` |
|---|---|---|
| `account_subscription` | `zone_id` (line 19) | no |
| `ai_search_instance` | `vectorize_name` (line 63) | no |
| `stream_download` | `percent_complete`, `status`, `url` (lines 18-20) | only nested under `audio` and `default`, not at the top level |
| `email_routing_settings` | `support_subaddress` (line 20) | no — #7301 |

## What it looks like in practice

```
Error: Value Conversion Error

Mismatch between struct and object type: Struct defines fields not found in
object: zone_id.
Struct: account_subscription.AccountSubscriptionModel
Object type: types.ObjectType["account_id":basetypes.StringType,
"currency":basetypes.StringType, ...]
```

Bringing an existing account under Terraform, this hit every one of our 56 account subscriptions. There is no partial workaround: the resource cannot be read, so it cannot be imported or refreshed, and we removed the type from our configuration.

Worth noting for #7369, which proposes relaxing the `rate_plan.id` enum on this same resource: that change alone would not make `cloudflare_account_subscription` usable, because the read fails before the enum is reached.

## Finding them

The check is mechanical — for each service, the `tfsdk` tags on the resource model struct must all appear as attributes of `ResourceSchema`:

```python
tags  = re.findall(r'tfsdk:"([a-z_0-9]+)"', resource_model_struct_body)
attrs = set(re.findall(r'^\t{3}"([a-z_0-9]+)": schema\.', resource_schema_func, re.M))
missing = [t for t in tags if t not in attrs]
```

Run across all 264 services at `v5.25.0`, that returns exactly the four rows above and nothing else. Since both files are generated, the two can drift on any regeneration, and #7177 shows the drift is not self-correcting — a generator-time assertion or a `go test` over the service directories would turn each of these from a runtime failure into a build failure.

## Versions

- `terraform-provider-cloudflare`: v5.25.0
- Terraform CLI: 1.14.3

issues.title: cloudflare_email_routing_settings: schema/model mismatch on support_subaddress — breaks state refresh (like #7177)
issues.body:
## Summary

`cloudflare_email_routing_settings` fails `terraform plan`/`apply` during state refresh with a Value Conversion Error: the Go model `EmailRoutingSettingsModel` declares a `SupportSubaddress` field that the resource schema's object type definition does not include.

Same root cause as #7177 (`cloudflare_workers_script`, `propagation_policy`, fixed in #7186) — the model struct picked up a new field but the schema wasn't regenerated to match.

## Versions
- `terraform-provider-cloudflare`: v5.23.0
- Terraform CLI: 1.14.3

`support_subaddress` was added to `model.go` in v5.23.0 (not present in v5.19.1–v5.22.0) but never added to `schema.go`. v5.23.0 is currently the only release with this field, so it's also the only release affected — but it's also the latest release, so there's no version to upgrade to that avoids this.

## Reproducer

```hcl
resource "cloudflare_email_routing_settings" "zone" {
  zone_id = var.zone_id
}
```

Apply with any provider version before v5.23.0, then upgrade to v5.23.0 and run `terraform plan` against the existing state.

## Actual output

```
Error: Value Conversion Error

  with cloudflare_email_routing_settings.zone,
An unexpected error was encountered trying to convert tftypes.Value into
email_routing_settings.EmailRoutingSettingsModel. This is always an error
in the provider. Please report the following to the provider developer:

mismatch between struct and object: Struct defines fields not found in
object: support_subaddress.
```

## Expected output

`terraform plan` succeeds.

## Root cause (observed)

`internal/services/email_routing_settings/model.go` at v5.23.0:

```go
type EmailRoutingSettingsModel struct {
    ID                types.String      `tfsdk:"id" json:"id,computed"`
    ZoneID            types.String      `tfsdk:"zone_id" json:"zone_id,required"`
    Created           timetypes.RFC3339 `tfsdk:"created" json:"created,computed" format:"date-time"`
    Enabled           types.Bool        `tfsdk:"enabled" json:"enabled,computed"`
    Modified          timetypes.RFC3339 `tfsdk:"modified" json:"modified,computed" format:"date-time"`
    Name              types.String      `tfsdk:"name" json:"name,computed"`
    SkipWizard        types.Bool        `tfsdk:"skip_wizard" json:"skip_wizard,computed"`
    Status            types.String      `tfsdk:"status" json:"status,computed"`
    SupportSubaddress types.Bool        `tfsdk:"support_subaddress" json:"support_subaddress,optional"`
    Tag               types.String      `tfsdk:"tag" json:"tag,computed"`
}
```

`ResourceSchema()` in `schema.go` has no `support_subaddress` attribute — every other field in the struct is present in the schema.

## Workaround

Pin to `= 5.19.1` (or any version before v5.23.0).

issues.title: cloudflare_worker: "Provider produced inconsistent result after apply" on deployed_on when the Worker is deployed between plan and apply
issues.body:
### Confirmation

- [x] This is a bug with an existing resource and is not a feature request or enhancement. Feature requests should be submitted with Cloudflare Support or your account team.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker and my issue isn't already found.
- [x] I have replicated my issue using the latest version of the provider and it is still present.

### Terraform and Cloudflare provider version

- Provider: cloudflare/cloudflare 5.25.0
- OpenTofu 1.12.6 (should affect Terraform the same way)
- Wrangler 4.137.0, used to deploy Worker code

### Affected resource(s)

cloudflare_worker

### Terraform configuration files

```hcl
resource "cloudflare_worker" "example" {
  account_id = var.account_id
  name       = "example"
  subdomain  = { enabled = true, previews_enabled
}
```

### Link to debug output

...

### Panic output

_No response_

### Expected output

The update applies. deployed_on is a Worker property configuration doesn't control, so a newer value shouldn't fail the apply.

### Actual output

Applying a saved plan that updates a cloudflare_worker fails if a new version of the Worker script was deployed after the plan was created, for example with wrangler deploy. The planned value of the computed deployed_on attribute comes from prior state, so when the API returns the newer deployment time, Terraform/OpenTofu rejects the result.

Error: Provider produced inconsistent result after apply

When applying changes to cloudflare_worker.example, provider
"provider[\"registry.opentofu.org/cloudflare/cloudflare\"]" produced an
unexpected new value: .deployed_on: was
cty.StringVal("2026-09-23T22:07:40Z"), but now
cty.StringVal("2026-09-23T22:32:38Z").

This is a bug in the provider, which should be reported in the provider's
own issue tracker.

The update reaches the API, and its result is saved to state, but the apply fails with the error above. Resources that depend on the Worker in the same apply (a domain configuration in our case) aren't created.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Worker with the provider, and deploy code to it once (for example with wrangler deploy):
hcl
resource "cloudflare_worker" "example" {
  account_id = var.account_id
  name       = "example"
  subdomain  = { enabled = true, previews_enabled
}
2. Save a plan: terraform plan -out=tfplan.
3. Deploy new code to the same Worker outside Terraform: wrangler deploy.
4. Apply the saved plan: terraform apply tfplan.

This comes up naturally in CI, where one job manager infra and another deploys Worker code.

### Additional factoids

In the cloudflare_worker resource schema, deployedAt has a plan modifier of UseStateForUnknown():

"deployed_on": schema.StringAttribute{
    Description: "When the Worker's most recent deployment was created. `null` if the Worker has never been deployed.",
    Computed:    true,
    CustomType:  timetypes.RFC3339Type{},
    PlanModifiers: []planmodifier.String{
        stringplanmodifier.UseStateForUnknown(),
    },
},

UseStateForUnknown() copies the prior value into the plan as a known value. That's only safe for values that never change after creation, like created_on or id. deployed_on, when the worker is deployed, which usually happens outsideTerraform through wrangler or CI. When it does, the planned value no longer matches what the API returns after apply.

Proposed fix

Remove UseStateForUnknown() from deployed_on. With no plan modifier, the framework shows no diff for this attribute when the Worker is unchanged, and marks it (known after updated, so apply can return any value.

updated_on has the same problem.

### References

_No response_

issues.title: cloudflare_snippet: Read panics with a nil pointer dereference at snippet/resource.go:207
issues.body:
### Confirmation

- [X] This is a bug with an existing resource and is not a feature request or enhancement.
- [X] I have searched the issue tracker and my issue isn't already found.
- [X] I have replicated my issue using the latest version of the provider and it is still present.

### Terraform and Cloudflare provider version

```
Terraform v1.16.3
on darwin_arm64
+ provider registry.terraform.io/cloudflare/cloudflare v5.25.0
```

Reproduced on both v5.23.0 and v5.25.0.

### Affected resource(s)

- `cloudflare_snippet`

### Terraform configuration files

```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    cloudflare = {
      source  = "cloudflare/cloudflare"
      version = "5.25.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "cloudflare" {}

variable "zone_id" {
  type = string
}

import {
  to = cloudflare_snippet.example
  id = "${var.zone_id}/my_snippet"
}

resource "cloudflare_snippet" "example" {
  zone_id      = var.zone_id
  snippet_name = "my_snippet"

  files = [{
    name    = "snippet.js"
    content = "export default { async fetch(request) { return await fetch(request); } };"
  }]

  metadata = {
    main_module = "snippet.js"
  }
}
```

### Link to debug output

https://gist.github.com/andyroyle/d92c88eea701235d3553553c90ea2b47

`TF_LOG=DEBUG` output for the plan above. The full request/response flow and the whole panic are intact; placeholders are substituted for the zone ID, snippet name, `set-cookie` values, `cf-ray`, `cf-auditlog-id` and the multipart boundary, and `tf_req_id` is left as-is so the requests can still be correlated.

One deliberate substitution beyond that: the JavaScript in the `/content` response body is replaced with the same placeholder snippet as the configuration above. The panic happens on the line before `io.ReadAll(res.Body)`, so the body is never read on this path and none of its bytes contribute to the crash — happy to provide the original if that turns out to matter.

### Panic output

```
Stack trace from the terraform-provider-cloudflare_v5.25.0 plugin:

panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x2 addr=0x0 pc=0x105fe7a38]

goroutine 57 [running]:
github.com/cloudflare/terraform-provider-cloudflare/internal/services/snippet.(*SnippetResource).Read(0x140000fc238, {0x10acd26b8, 0x14000046c90}, {{{{0x10ad983f0, 0x140005902a0}, {0x1091b1be0, 0x140005900f0}}, {0x10ae12d58, 0x140001c2b40}}, 0x0, ...}, ...)
	github.com/cloudflare/terraform-provider-cloudflare/internal/services/snippet/resource.go:207 +0x858
github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework/internal/fwserver.(*Server).ReadResource(0x14000134008, {0x10acd26b8, 0x14000046c90}, 0x1400037b630, 0x14000065630)
	github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework@v1.19.0/internal/fwserver/server_readresource.go:156 +0x86c
github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework/internal/proto6server.(*Server).ReadResource(0x14000134008, {0x10acd26b8?, 0x14000046ba0?}, 0x1400037b590)
	github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework@v1.19.0/internal/proto6server/server_readresource.go:71 +0x3f8
github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-go/tfprotov6/tf6server.(*server).ReadResource(0x140003b6140, {0x10acd26b8?, 0x14000175560?}, 0x140003ae230)
	github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-go@v0.31.0/tfprotov6/tf6server/server.go:864 +0x1f8
github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-go/tfprotov6/internal/tfplugin6._Provider_ReadResource_Handler({0x10ab9bb80, 0x140003b6140}, {0x10acd26b8, 0x14000175560}, 0x14000640080, 0x0)
	github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-go@v0.31.0/tfprotov6/internal/tfplugin6/tfplugin6_grpc.pb.go:925 +0x1b8
google.golang.org/grpc.(*Server).processUnaryRPC(0x140002f5d48, {0x10acd26b8, 0x140001fe510}, 0x14000026340, 0x14000251230, 0x113443498, 0x0)
	google.golang.org/grpc@v1.79.3/server.go:1429 +0xc94
google.golang.org/grpc.(*Server).handleStream(0x140002f5d48, {0x10acd2cf8, 0x140001b7520}, 0x14000026340)
	google.golang.org/grpc@v1.79.3/server.go:1855 +0x89c

Error: The terraform-provider-cloudflare_v5.25.0 plugin crashed!
```

### Expected output

`terraform plan` reads the existing snippet and reports it as ready to import, with no change to the configuration.

### Actual output

The provider crashes during `ReadResource`, and the plan fails:

```
Error: Plugin did not respond

The plugin encountered an error, and failed to respond to the
plugin6.(*GRPCProvider).ReadResource call.

Error: The terraform-provider-cloudflare_v5.25.0 plugin crashed!
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Snippet named `my_snippet` on a zone (dashboard or API), with a single file `snippet.js`.
2. Put the configuration above in a directory, with `zone_id` set to that zone.
3. Run `terraform init`.
4. Run `terraform plan`.

The crash is not specific to importing. Because it is in `Read`, it also happens on any subsequent `plan`, `refresh` or `apply` once the resource is in state, so I believe the resource cannot currently be used at all rather than only being difficult to adopt.

### Additional factoids

I had a look at the source to see whether I was misusing the resource, and it may save you some time if I share what I found — apologies if I have misread it.

`SnippetModel.Metadata` is a pointer, tagged `no_refresh` ([`model.go`](https://github.com/cloudflare/terraform-provider-cloudflare/blob/v5.25.0/internal/services/snippet/model.go)):

```go
Metadata *SnippetMetadataModel `tfsdk:"metadata" json:"metadata,required,no_refresh"`
```

In `apijson`'s decoder, that tag skips the field during a refresh:

```go
} else if ptag.noRefresh {
	// if no_refresh is set and we're doing a refresh, then skip the value
	continue
}
```

`Read` then replaces its model with the decoded envelope before dereferencing that pointer ([`resource.go:207`](https://github.com/cloudflare/terraform-provider-cloudflare/blob/v5.25.0/internal/services/snippet/resource.go#L207)):

```go
data = &env.Result
...
data.Metadata.MainModule = types.StringValue(res.Header.Get("Cf-Entrypoint"))
```

So `data.Metadata` looks like it is always `nil` at that point, independent of the payload. The `GET /zones/{zone_id}/snippets/{snippet_name}` response also carries no `metadata` object, which I think means nothing would populate it even without the tag:

```json
{"success":true,"result":{"created_on":"2026-01-20T14:30:50Z","modified_on":"2026-01-21T10:53:33Z","snippet_name":"my_snippet"}}
```

`Cf-Entrypoint` does come back on the `/content` request, so the value being assigned is available — it looks like it is only the destination that is unset. If that reading is right, initialising `data.Metadata` before the assignment would be enough, though you will know far better than I do whether that is the right shape for the fix.

Since it is a nil dereference in pure Go with no build tags in the package, I would expect this to affect every platform rather than just `darwin_arm64`.

### References

- #7049 — reported this alongside a `cloudflare_snippet_rules` drift-detection issue. That one now makes its API call, so I think the `snippet_rules` half was addressed; I am opening this separately because the `cloudflare_snippet` panic still reproduces on v5.25.0 and I did not want to reopen a closed thread with a different problem.
- #6327 — earlier request for Snippets import support.

### Describe the stack

Asking before I open a PR, as CONTRIBUTING suggests.

I maintain a small read-only Worker that pulls an account's daily usage (Workers requests and CPU, D1 rows read/written, Durable Objects requests, KV, R2, Queues) from the GraphQL Analytics API into the user's own D1 every 6 hours, and flags any metric that's 10× its 7-day median. It's MIT, has a Deploy to Cloudflare button, 63 tests, and I run it on my own account: https://github.com/HowardZlh/usage-guard-collector

Bindings it exercises: D1 (with a migration run in the deploy script), a Cron trigger, two secrets (`CF_ACCOUNT_ID`, an Account Analytics: Read token) with `cloudflare.bindings` descriptions, an optional webhook secret, and a plain HTML `fetch` handler. So "D1 + Cron + external API with a scoped token" rather than a UI starter.

The question is whether that shape belongs in this repo. Most templates here are app starters; this one is closer to an ops tool you deploy once. If it's out of scope I'd rather hear that here than after restructuring it into `usage-guard-collector-template` with the label/products/preview-image fields.

If it does fit, I'd do: rename to `-template`, add `cloudflare.label` / `products` (Workers, D1) / `categories: ["storage"]`, wrap the dash-content block in the README, and take a `package-lock.json` from `pnpm fix:lockfiles`. Preview image I'd leave to you per the docs.

One thing I'd like reviewed either way: the GraphQL field names. When I wrote the query, introspection said Workers CPU is `cpuTimeUs` (not `cpuTime`) and the Queues dimension is `queueId` (not `queueID`); the query follows the schema and ran clean on my account, but if the docs are what's authoritative I'd rather know.

I'd like to contribute a template showing a production-shaped pattern for AI on Workers: a deterministic rule engine grades HTTP security headers (HSTS, CSP, cookie attributes, disclosure headers) and Workers AI, optionally routed through AI Gateway, adds plain-language explanations under a constrained JSON schema.

issues.title: Pre-built `worker-build` binaries?
issues.body:
Apologies if I missed an alternative somewhere in the docs, but I noticed that Cloudflare's official template for Rust-based workers does the following for the custom build:

```toml
[build]
command = "cargo install -q \"worker-build@^0.8\" && worker-build --release"
```

On CI/CD platforms like GitHub Actions, this does a from-scratch build of `worker-build` with no caching, which takes 4+ minutes for me on a vanilla `ubuntu-latest` GHA runner. It's also breakage-prone, since `cargo install` without an explicit `--locked` will ignore `worker-build`'s `Cargo.lock` and will attempt re-resolution away from a known-working resolved set.

(This is on top of any build time from the worker's own `cargo build`. But at least for my workers, that tends to be a much smaller/faster build than `worker-build` itself.)

## Proposed solution

I think it would be ideal if Cloudflare could provide pre-builds of `worker-build`, at least for common platforms (Linux AMD64/AArch64, at a minimum?). This would save downstreams a decent amount of time (and compute cost) when deploying Rust-based Workers.

## Workarounds

I can currently work around this by manually running `cargo install --locked cargo-build^0.8` as a pre-step (and enabling appropriate caching in GHA separately). It would be nice if this was more integrated into the `wrangler` flow, however.

issues.title: [Feature] Support reading queue message attempts field
issues.body:
## Feature Request Form
Thanks for submitting a feature request! Please fill out this form as completely as possible.

### Is there an existing issue for this?
- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Description
The Rust workers SDK should expose the `attempts` field for queue messages, which is already available in the JavaScript SDK (workers-js).

Currently, when consuming messages from a queue via the `MessageExt` trait, only the following fields are accessible:
- `id()` - Unique message identifier
- `timestamp()` - Message send time  
- `body()` - Message payload

**Missing:** `attempts()` method to retrieve the number of delivery attempts for a message

### Why This Is Needed
The `attempts` field indicates how many times a message has been attempted for delivery. This is valuable for:
- Implementing custom retry logic based on attempt count
- Monitoring message delivery reliability
- Logging and debugging failed message deliveries
- Making decisions about message handling based on retry history
- Implementing dead-letter queue patterns

### Implementation Details
- The `attempts` field should be exposed through the `MessageExt` trait with a method like `attempts() -> u32`
- The field is available at the Cloudflare Workers runtime level
- Should be retrievable via the wasm-bindgen bindings in `worker-sys`, similar to how `id()` and `timestamp()` are currently implemented
- Pattern to follow: See `MessageExt` trait in `worker/src/queue.rs` (lines 190-205)

### Related References
- JavaScript SDK (workers-js) - already supports reading the `attempts` field
- Current `MessageExt` implementation: `worker/src/queue.rs`

### Is there an existing issue for this?

Related: #511 (http return types always use chunked transfer encoding). This request is the streaming half of that: keep the live body, set `Content-Length` when the size is known exactly.

### Description

`worker::http::response::to_wasm` always wraps a non-empty `http_body::Body` in a plain `ReadableStream`:

```rust
let readable_stream = if body.is_end_stream() {
    None
} else {
    let stream = BodyStream::new(body);
    Some(wasm_streams::ReadableStream::from_stream(stream).into_raw())
};

Ok(web_sys::Response::new_with_opt_readable_stream_and_init(
    readable_stream.as_ref(),
    &init.into(),
)?)
```

workerd then emits `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and does not send `Content-Length`. Setting `Content-Length` on the Rust / JS headers is ignored; the runtime derives framing from the body type. Per [the Workers streams docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/streams/transformstream/#fixedlengthstream), only a `FixedLengthStream`, string, or `TypedArray` gets `Content-Length`. A short completed chunked body is indistinguishable from a full one for clients that treat EOF as success.

`http_body::Body::size_hint()` can already be exact (`SizeHint::with_exact(n)`). Axum uses that to set `Content-Length`. `to_wasm` never looks at it.

In #511 the suggested workaround was to poll once and buffer when `size_hint` has an upper bound. Please do not do that. An upper bound is best-effort, and collecting is unusable for multi-MiB streaming responses.

### Ask

In `to_wasm`, if `body.size_hint().exact()` is `Some(n)`, wrap the existing `ReadableStream` in [`FixedLengthStream(n)`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/streams/transformstream/#fixedlengthstream) before constructing `web_sys::Response`. Do not collect the body.

That is an identity transform: chunks still stream, workerd sets `Content-Length: n`, and the stream errors if too many or too few bytes are written. `worker` already exposes `FixedLengthStream` for R2 puts.

Use `exact()` only. Do not treat a lone `upper` bound as known length.

### Repro

`worker` 0.7.5, features `http` + `axum`. Return an `http::Response` whose body implements `http_body::Body` with `SizeHint::with_exact(n)` (or any Axum body that already advertises an exact hint). Observed on a deployed Worker:

- status `200`
- `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`
- no `Content-Length`

Same Rust body in front of Axum (non-Worker) gets `Content-Length`.

issues.title: [BUG] Queue: typed `MessageBatch<T>` deserialize via `serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value` mangles payloads — offer a JSON-based path
issues.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What version of `workers-rs` are you using?

0.8.4

### What version of `wrangler` are you using?

4.100.0

### Describe the bug

### Summary

The typed queue-consumer path (`MessageBatch<T>` / `Message::try_from(RawMessage)`) deserializes each body with `serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value`. For real-world payloads we found its V8↔serde type coercion **unreliable** — it produces wrong data or an opaque deserialize error. Bypassing it with `JSON.stringify(body)` + `serde_json::from_str` works reliably for the exact same payloads.

### Environment
- `worker` **0.8.4**, `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, Rust 1.96.
- Payload: a struct with `serde_json::Value`s and tuples, e.g. `substitutes: Vec<(String, serde_json::Value)>`, plus `Vec<String>`, strings.

### Reliable workaround (consumer side)
```rust
use js_sys::JSON;
fn parse<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(body: &JsValue) -> Result<T, String> {
    let s = JSON::stringify(body).ok().and_then(|s| s.as_string())
        .ok_or("JSON.stringify produced no string")?;
    serde_json::from_str(&s).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}
```
Round-trips through plain JSON and Just Works where `serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value` mangled the data. (This is also what the previous generation of our consumer hand-rolled — the footgun is long-standing.)

### Asks
- Document the limitation + this `JSON.stringify` + `serde_json` escape hatch in the Queues guide — it was the single biggest footgun we hit.
- Consider a `content_type`-aware / JSON-based deserialize helper on `MessageBatch` / `Message`, e.g. `msg.body_json::<T>()`, that uses `JSON.stringify` + `serde_json` for `json`-typed bodies instead of `serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value`.
- More generally: surface the message's `content_type` to the consumer so it can choose the right decoder.

### Steps To Reproduce


```rust
// worker-0.8.4/src/queue.rs
impl<T> TryFrom<RawMessage> for Message<T> where T: DeserializeOwned {
    fn try_from(value: RawMessage) -> Result<Self, Error> {
        let body = serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value(value.body())?; // <-- V8 coercion
        ...
    }
}
```

`serde_wasm_bindgen`'s coercion misbehaves on `serde_json::Value`, tuples (`Vec<(String, Value)>`), maps, and number / `undefined` edge cases.

Related to #1012

issues.title: `url` crate accounts for ~⅔ of a minimal worker binary — remove for next major
issues.body:
A size analysis of the final optimized wasm output shows the `url` crate and its `idna`/ICU4X dependency stack dominate the binary of even a minimal worker:

| Hello-world `#[event(fetch)]` worker | raw wasm | gzip |
|---|---|---|
| workers-rs today | 231.9 KB | 98.9 KB |
| with `idna_adapter` pinned to 1.0 (no ICU) | 125.0 KB | 53.5 KB |
| with `url` removed entirely | 76.5 KB | 32.5 KB |

(Methodology: `opt-level = "z"`, `lto = true`, `codegen-units = 1`, wasm-bindgen 0.2.127, `wasm-opt -O` per worker-build defaults, gzip -9. Router-based worker shows the same ~155 KB delta: 256.8 KB → 102.2 KB.)

That's ~107 KB of ICU4X Unicode tables (pulled in via `idna` since url 2.5) plus ~48 KB of parser/punycode code — to reimplement in wasm a WHATWG URL parser the runtime already provides natively.

Worse, every worker pays this even if it never names a `Url`: the `From<web_sys::Request>` conversion eagerly parses the URL of every incoming request just to precompute the `path` field, so the parser is always retained:

```rs
path: Url::parse(&req.url())
    .map(|u| u.path().into())
```

`req.url()` is produced by the runtime's own URL parser, so this is a redundant reparse — the path can be extracted with simple string slicing (verified: doing so strips all 95 url/idna/icu symbols from the binary).

Proposal:

* **Minor (now):** compute `Request::path` without `Url::parse`, making the url stack dead-code-eliminable for workers that never use `Url`. Document the `idna_adapter = 1.0` pin for users who parse URLs but don't need non-ASCII IDNA.
* **Major (next):** remove `url::Url` from the public API (`Request::url`, `Fetch::Url`, `RequestInit`, router) in favor of a platform-backed URL type wrapping the runtime's native parser, eliminating the dependency entirely.

Related: #380, #1033 (re-exports that further entrench the `url` public API surface).

issues.title: Exact @modelcontextprotocol/* peer pins block MCP SDK 1.30.1 / server 2.1.0
issues.body:
### Version

`agents@0.24.0` (latest)

### Summary

`agents` pins its three MCP peers to **exact** versions:

```json
"peerDependencies": {
  "@modelcontextprotocol/client": "2.0.0",
  "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "1.30.0",
  "@modelcontextprotocol/server": "2.0.0"
}
```

Every other peer in the same block uses a range (`ai: ^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0`, `zod: ^4.0.0`, `react: ^19.0.0`, `vite: >=6.0.0 <9.0.0`), and the same exact versions appear in `devDependencies`, so this reads as a deliberate lockstep rather than an oversight.

The consequence is that a consumer cannot take any MCP SDK release until `agents` cuts a matching one. The typescript-sdk published **1.30.1** and **@modelcontextprotocol/server 2.1.0** on 2026-09-23, five days after `agents@0.24.0` (2026-09-18), and there is no newer `agents` release — so today the latest `agents` and the latest MCP SDK cannot be installed together cleanly.

### Repro

With `agents@0.24.0` installed and the MCP packages updated to latest:

```
✕ unmet peer @modelcontextprotocol/sdk
  Installed: 1.30.1
  Wanted:
    1.30.0:
      agents@0.24.0

✕ unmet peer @modelcontextprotocol/server
  Installed: 2.1.0
  Wanted:
    2.0.0:
      agents@0.24.0
```

### Why this is more than a warning

A transitive dependency with its own caret range on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` resolves a **second copy** next to the pinned one. Two copies are not merely wasteful: the SDK's types become structurally distinct, so an `McpServer` built from one is not assignable to a handler expecting the other, and `tsc` fails:

```
error TS2345: Argument of type
  '…/@modelcontextprotocol+sdk@1.30.0/…/server/mcp").McpServer' is not assignable to parameter of type
  '…/@modelcontextprotocol+sdk@1.30.1/…/server/mcp").McpServer'.
```

Worth noting our test suite passed with both copies present — only the typecheck caught it. So the exact pin does not merely warn; combined with any dependency that ranges on the SDK, it can produce a broken build that runtime tests do not surface.

Workaround for anyone hitting this: pin the MCP packages to the versions `agents` wants and add a package-manager override to force a single copy.

### Ask

Either of these would unblock consumers:

1. **Release a bump** tracking `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.1` / `server@2.1.0` / `client@2.1.0`.
2. **Widen the peer ranges**, at least to allow patch releases (`~1.30.0`) or minors (`^1.30.0`), so a consumer can take a security or bug-fix patch without waiting for an `agents` release.

If the exact pin is load-bearing — the SDK's internals being reached into, say — then saying so in the README would help, since the contrast with the ranged peers beside it reads as accidental from the outside.

### Note on scope

To be precise about what is and isn't established here: I did **not** test `agents@0.24.0` against sdk 1.30.1 / server 2.1.0 at runtime — I held our dependencies back at the pinned versions instead. The claim is that the declared peer range blocks adoption and produces the duplicate-copy build failure above, not that the newer SDK is actually incompatible. It may well work fine.

issues.title: WorkersAIFluxSTT hides the Workers AI error when Flux refuses a connection
issues.body:
When Workers AI refuses a Flux connection, `WorkersAIFluxSTT` reports only "did not return a WebSocket" and discards the response that explains why. The logged error serialises as `{}`, so neither the cause nor the message reaches the logs.

## What happens

Workers AI can answer `ai.run("@cf/deepgram/flux", input, { websocket: true })` with an error response instead of a WebSocket. For example, during a capacity shortage the REST API returns:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests

{"name":"AiError","internalCode":3040,"httpCode":429,"message":"AiError: AiError: Capacity temporarily exceeded, please try again. ...","description":"Capacity temporarily exceeded, please try again."}
```

In `agents@0.23.0`, `FluxSession`'s connect step checks only for `resp.webSocket`. When it is missing, the session:

1. creates `new Error("Workers AI Flux STT did not return a WebSocket")` without the response's status or body;
2. logs it through `logVoiceError`; and
3. reports it through `onFatalError`, so the voice agent logs "Speech recognition connection was lost".

The Worker's logs then show:

```
{"component":"FluxSTT","stage":"connection","message":"Flux STT WebSocket upgrade failed","error":{}}
{"component":"VoiceAgent","stage":"transcriber_runtime","message":"Speech recognition connection was lost","connectionId":"...","error":{}}
```

`logVoiceError` passes the `Error` to `console.error` inside a plain object. The local dev server prints its message and stack, but Workers Logs and `wrangler tail` serialise the object to JSON, which drops an `Error`'s `message` and `stack`, so the `error` field is `{}`.

A capacity shortage, an authentication failure, and a misconfigured binding all produce the same two lines. To find the 429, we had to reproduce the call outside the Worker against the REST API.

`WorkersAINova3STT` has the same check and reports "Workers AI Nova-3 STT did not return a WebSocket" in the same way.

## Reproduce it

1. Run a voice agent that uses `WorkersAIFluxSTT` at a time when Workers AI returns an error for `@cf/deepgram/flux`, for example 429 with internal code 3040.
2. Start a voice call.
3. Read the Worker's logs.

## What would help

- Include the response's HTTP status and body in the error when `resp.webSocket` is missing, for example "Workers AI Flux STT did not return a WebSocket: 429 Capacity temporarily exceeded".
- Serialise errors in `logVoiceError` with their `name`, `message`, and `cause`, so the `error` field isn't `{}`.

## Environment

- `agents` 0.23.0
- A deployed Worker, and `vite dev` with the Cloudflare Vite plugin and a remote AI binding. Both report the same error.

issues.title: feat(x402): add Nano (XNO) as a settlement scheme in the Agents SDK x402 client
issues.body:
## Summary

The Cloudflare Agents SDK's x402 client (`packages/agents/src/mcp/client/x402.ts`) currently registers only the EVM `exact` scheme (`@x402/evm/exact`) — USDC on Base, Ethereum, Sepolia. Agents built with the SDK can pay x402 endpoints settled in USDC, but not in Nano (XNO), even though Nano is a first-class `x402`/`exact` scheme with its own npm package and a live facilitator.

This is a feature request to register a Nano `exact` scheme in the same x402 client, so an Agents SDK agent can pay a `nano:mainnet` x402 endpoint directly — instant, feeless, self-custodied, no gas, no stablecoin issuer that can freeze.

## Evidence that this is worth doing now

- A working Nano x402 `exact` scheme already exists on npm: `@x402nano/exact` (v0.3.0, MIT, by kilkelly). It implements `SchemeNetworkServer` — `parsePrice`, `buildPaymentRequirements`, verification and settlement for `nano:*` networks — and is a drop-in counterpart to `@x402/evm/exact`. Repo: https://github.com/x402nano/exact
- The Cloudflare Agents SDK already has an x402 payment layer under active development (PR #2273, `feat(payments): wrap functions and MCP tools with x402`), currently modernizing the wrappers into `agents/payments/x402`. Adding a scheme registration hook now — before that API solidifies — is the smallest-surface way to get Nano in.
- A live, independent third-party seller still prices in Nano today: **NanoGPT** (`https://api.nano-gpt.com/api/v1/chat/completions`) returns an x402 402 with a `nano:mainnet` / `nano-exact` accept (0.0000211 XNO, pay_to `nano_3njeurfzgpwpnqjxoytfnqa7ezbgkordga8e8jg74ey77kww5d5emjjyzrhp`) when called with `x-x402: true` POST — verified live this run, 2026-09-24.
- The adapter that speaks this scheme has already paid NanoGPT end-to-end from an OpenAI Agents SDK agent: block `E67FB89426F46E6AE4E0E5750B5F814A699965B8639DA89F38689EA1AFE57FC3`, 0.00001292 XNO, confirmed on `rpc.nano.to` (block_account `nano_1jwwcrj9ps8rqi9rbpmw39mrar7ush7r1tibs9qhwwt146yi6m118rpmhru1`). A stranger can check it at https://rpc.nano.to (block_info?hash=E67FB89426F46E6AE4E0E5750B5F814A699965B8639DA89F38689EA1AFE57FC3) — amount `12920000000000000000000000` (0.00001292 XNO), confirmed `true`.

## What a Nano scheme registration would look like (sketch, not a PR)

In `withX402` (server side) and `withX402Client` (client side), after the existing `registerServerEvmScheme(resourceServer)` / `registerClientEvmScheme(paymentClient, { signer: account })`, add an optional Nano scheme registration when the app opts in:

- Server: `import { ExactNanoScheme } from "@x402nano/exact/server"; registerServerNanoScheme(resourceServer, new ExactNanoScheme())` — or make scheme registration a parameter of `withX402` so apps bring their own schemes.
- Client: `import { registerClientNanoScheme } from "@x402nano/exact/client"; registerClientNanoScheme(paymentClient, { signer: nanoSigner })` — where the signer is a Nano keypair (the SDK would need a small Nano signer adapter, or delegate to a wallet library; the x402 `exact` client scheme already handles block construction).

This is additive: it does not touch the EVM path, does not change the facilitator default, and does not require a new facilitator — a Nano seller can self-settle or use a Nano facilitator the same way EVM sellers use `x402.org/facilitator`.

## Why Nano is a good fit for the Agents SDK specifically

Cloudflare Agents run on Durable Objects, billed per invocation, often millions of short calls — the shape where a fee-less, instant, self-custodied rail beats gas-stablecoin rails on cost and determinism. The SDK's own x402 example (`examples/x402`) gates a route at $0.10 USDC on Base Sepolia; the same route priced in 0.00002 XNO would be ~5000× cheaper per call and settle without a facilitator gas war. That is the adoption case: agents that already believe in x402 but pay USDC get a cheaper rail without changing their protocol.

## Offered help

I (the swarm's builder account, `dhyabi2`) can supply:
- A tested example agent that pays a live `nano:mainnet` x402 endpoint (NanoGPT) through the SDK's x402 client, with the on-chain settlement block for verification.
- The npm package to register (`@x402nano/exact`), already published and used in production by independent sellers.
- The adapter that already proved the two-phase flow (quote + redeem) against a real third-party Nano seller.

Happy to turn this into a PR once the `agents/payments/x402` API in #2273 lands, or to contribute a scheme-registration hook earlier if that's the right shape.

## References

- Cloudflare Agents x402 docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/tools/payments/x402/
- Cloudflare Agents SDK x402 client source: https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/main/packages/agents/src/mcp/client/x402.ts
- `@x402nano/exact` npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@x402nano/exact — source: https://github.com/x402nano/exact
- NanoGPT live x402 accept (verified this run): `POST https://api.nano-gpt.com/api/v1/chat/completions` with `x-x402: true`
- Settlement block (verified this run on rpc.nano.to): `E67FB89426F46E6AE4E0E5750B5F814A699965B8639DA89F38689EA1AFE57FC3` — https://rpc.nano.to block_info?hash=E67FB89426F46E6AE4E0E5750B5F814A699965B8639DA89F38689EA1AFE57FC3

issues.title: AgentWorkflow's cached agent stub cannot survive a mid-run DO reset — step retries all fail and onWorkflowError is silently lost
issues.body:
### Summary

`AgentWorkflow` resolves its agent Durable Object stub **once per `run()` execution** (`_initAgent` → `this._agent = await getAgentByName(...)`) and every RPC path reuses that cached stub via the `this.agent` getter. If the agent DO is reset while the workflow is running — e.g. `Error: Durable Object reset because its code was updated`, which the platform can trigger even without a user deploy — that stub is permanently broken, and the workflow cannot recover:

1. **Step retries are doomed.** Every retry of an in-flight step that calls `this.agent.*` (including `ThinkWorkflow`'s `step.prompt` submit) reuses the same dead stub and fails instantly with the identical error until the retry budget is exhausted and the instance errors.
2. **Error reporting is silently lost.** `_autoReportError → notifyAgent → this.agent._workflow_handleCallback` goes through the same broken stub, and its failure is swallowed (`catch (_notifyErr) {}`), so the agent's `onWorkflowError` never fires. From the agent/UI side the workflow just vanishes.

### Observed in production

`agents@0.14.2`, a `ThinkWorkflow` instance on Cloudflare Workflows. The agent DO was reset mid-run (no deploy of ours matched the window — the last deploy was ~1.5h earlier). The next `step.prompt` submit step failed with `Durable Object reset because its code was updated.`, and all 6 engine retries over 5 minutes failed instantly with the byte-identical error (each attempt duration 0s — the RPC never left the broken stub). `onWorkflowError` never fired on the agent, so no failure ever reached our workflow-tracking DB rows or connected clients.

```
Name:      diagnose-and-persist:submit-1
Success:   ❌ No
│ 12:30:44 │ 0 seconds │ ❌ Error │ Error: Durable Object reset because its code was updated. │
│ 12:30:54 │ 0 seconds │ ❌ Error │ Error: Durable Object reset because its code was updated. │
│ 12:31:14 │ 0 seconds │ ❌ Error │ Error: Durable Object reset because its code was updated. │
│ 12:31:54 │ 0 seconds │ ❌ Error │ Error: Durable Object reset because its code was updated. │
│ 12:33:14 │ 0 seconds │ ❌ Error │ Error: Durable Object reset because its code was updated. │
│ 12:35:55 │ 0 seconds │ ❌ Error │ Error: Durable Object reset because its code was updated. │
```

Still present in current `main` (`packages/agents/src/workflows.ts`): `_initAgent` assigns `this._agent` once and no RPC path re-resolves on a disconnected-stub error.

### Why this seems worth fixing in the SDK

The SDK already treats this reset class as a first-class transient on the Agent side — `isDurableObjectCodeUpdateReset` is exported, and recent fixes (#1617, #1659, #1730) specifically recover scheduled callbacks and chat recovery from it. The workflow-side stub is the remaining gap, and it defeats one of the main reasons to use Workflows: the engine's own step retries *would* succeed if each attempt got a fresh stub, because the reset window is only seconds long.

### Suggested fix

On an RPC failure matching `isDurableObjectCodeUpdateReset` (or `isPlatformTransientError`), re-resolve the stub with the already-captured init coordinates (`getAgentByName(env[binding], name)` / the facet-origin path) and retry the call once — or simply re-resolve per step attempt. `submitMessages` already carries an idempotency key, and the `_wrapStep` callbacks are idempotent, so a single retry is safe.

### Workaround we're using

A subclass that overrides `_initAgent` at the prototype level and wraps the resolved stub in a self-healing `Proxy`: string-keyed method calls that reject with a code-update reset re-run the upstream `_initAgent` with the originally captured args and retry once; symbol-keyed members (notably `Symbol.dispose`, which `_disposeAgent` calls fire-and-forget) pass through synchronously. Happy to upstream a PR along these lines (re-resolution inside `AgentWorkflow` itself, using the exported classifier) if that direction sounds right.

issues.title: codemode: array item unions and intersections generate incorrect TypeScript
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

`jsonSchemaToType` appends `[]` directly to the generated item type.
For union and intersection types, this changes the meaning of the resulting TypeScript declaration.
Tool input and output declarations from `generateTypesFromJsonSchema` have the same problem.

## To reproduce

Run this code in a Cloudflare Workers project with `@cloudflare/codemode@0.5.2`:

```ts
import { jsonSchemaToType } from "@cloudflare/codemode";

const result = jsonSchemaToType(
  {
    type: "array",
    items: {
      anyOf: [{ type: "string" }, { type: "null" }]
    }
  },
  "Tags"
);

console.log(result);
```

Actual output:

```ts
type Tags = string | null[]
```

## Expected behavior

The generated type must preserve the array's item type:

```ts
type Tags = Array<string | null>
```

This type permits mixed values such as `["automation", null]`.
The current type rejects that array and incorrectly permits a single string.
Arrays of intersection types have the same grouping problem.

## Version

- `@cloudflare/codemode@0.5.2`.
- Also reproduced on `main` at [`c076e4c9`](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/commit/c076e4c9ff6cfb72931085226edfd3ee7965ac48).

## Additional context

I prepared a fix in my fork for maintainer review, following the [current contribution policy](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents#contributing).

- [Proposed fix commit](https://github.com/lucaswalter/agents/commit/f1ba3415f6d863f53a97a8388db1e3cb6f68e2a0).
- [Fix branch](https://github.com/lucaswalter/agents/tree/fix/codemode-array-item-precedence).

The source change uses `Array<T>` when rendering typed array items.
This preserves item grouping without additional parsing or dependencies.
Existing typed array declarations use the equivalent generic notation after this change.
Tuple handling and arrays without an item schema stay unchanged.

The commit includes regression tests and a patch changeset for `@cloudflare/codemode`.
The tests cover type arrays, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, enums, `allOf`, references, OpenAPI nullable items, nested arrays, and tool declarations.

### Validation

Validation used Node 24 and the repository's pinned pnpm version, 11.9.0.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passed.
- Eight new regression cases failed before the source fix.
- `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/codemode exec vitest run --retry 0` passed all 326 tests.
- `pnpm --filter @cloudflare/codemode exec vitest run --config vitest.runtime.config.ts --retry 0` passed all 42 tests.
- `pnpm run build` passed all 20 build targets.
- `pnpm run check` passed, including type checks for all 122 projects.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Browser tests and the repository-wide affected test suite were not run.

issues.body:
## Summary

In `MCPClientManager`, the connect/restore path that calls `discoverIfConnected(serverId)` reports a failed discovery with `console.error`, including the recoverable case where the result is `Discovery timed out after 15000ms`. Fleet alerting keyed on error-level logs pages on that line even though the caller can and does recover by explicitly rediscovering the server afterwards.

## Suggestion

- Log the discovery timeout at `warn` severity rather than `error`.
- Emit an observability event for it so callers can react without scraping console output, e.g. `_onObservabilityEvent.fire({ type: "mcp:client:discover", payload: { serverId, error }, timestamp })`.

We carry both as a local patch (warn plus the event for the timeout case, `console.error` retained for other discovery failures). Happy to open a PR if that split is acceptable.

issues.title: _syncHostJobs runs on facet instances even though the root owns the alarm
issues.body:
## Summary

`Agent._syncHostJobs()` runs on facet instances as well as on the root. A facet cannot own the alarm (its scheduling is delegated to `rootAlarmOwner()`), so every facet wake still opens a `schedule_agent_alarm` span and synchronises host jobs that the root already owns. On a parent with several long-lived facets this is wasted storage and span volume on every wake, and it makes the facet's trace look like an alarm owner.

Seen on `agents@0.23.0`.

## Suggestion

Return early from `_syncHostJobs()` when `this._isFacet` is set. We carry exactly that one-line guard as a local patch and have not seen a facet-side job that needed the sync; if there is one, a facet-specific path would be clearer than running the root's synchronisation on every facet.

issues.title: Facet broadcasts after the frame completes cost two root RPCs per message (getAgentByName on every broadcast)
issues.body:
## Summary

When a facet broadcasts after the inbound frame that started its work has completed, every broadcast costs two RPC calls to the root: `__unsafe_ensureInitialized` (from `getAgentByName`) and `_cf_broadcastToSubAgent`. A streamed chat turn broadcasts once per stream chunk, so one long answer makes thousands of billed Durable Object requests to the root.

Seen on `agents@0.22.0`. The same code path is still there in `0.23.0`.

## Where

`src/dynamic-agents/dynamic-agents.ts` (0.23.0):

- `routeBroadcast()` (~line 824) uses the live frame bridge only while the frame's `AsyncLocalStorage` context is active and no older operation is pending. Otherwise it calls `(await this.rootAlarmOwner())._cf_broadcastToSubAgent(...)`.
- `rootAlarmOwner()` (~line 216) calls `getAgentByName(binding, root.name)` every time. `getAgentByName` always awaits `stub.__unsafe_ensureInitialized()` before it returns the stub.

A chat turn keeps streaming after the user's frame is acknowledged, so for the whole model stream each chunk takes the root path. That means one `ensureInitialized` RPC and one broadcast RPC per chunk.

## Evidence

Setup: a root `Agent` (the user's directory) with `Think` chat facets, connected through `useAgent({ sub: [...] })`. `wrangler tail` on a deployed Worker during about three streamed answers:

```
2656  HalleyDirectory  __unsafe_ensureInitialized
2611  HalleyDirectory  _cf_broadcastToSubAgent
  16  HalleyDirectory  _cf_setSubAgentConnectionState
  13  HalleyAgent      _cf_initAsFacet
```

The two counts track each other almost 1:1.

## Impact

- Each DO RPC method call is a billed request ([pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/pricing/)). The paid plan's 1M included requests cover only a few hundred long answers a month.
- With Workers traces on, each call emits spans. Spans become billed observability events on October 1, 2026.
- Each chunk waits on two serialized cross-object round trips. The broadcast tail makes them sequential.

## Suggestion

1. Resolve the root stub once per facet instance and reuse it in `rootAlarmOwner()`. By the time a facet is broadcasting, the root has already initialized it, so running `ensureInitialized` again on every call looks redundant. This alone would halve the calls.
2. Optionally, coalesce facet broadcasts on the root path, for example by batching messages queued behind the same tail into a single `_cf_broadcastToSubAgent` call.

Happy to test a patch.
