issues.title: Settling a workflow-tool run writes three full copies of session state (cancel/release steps)
issues.body:
**eve 0.64.1**, unchanged in 0.66.3 and on `main` (cd82f57). `execution/session-workflow-tool-run.ts`, `execution/tools/subagent/task-cancel.ts`, `execution/tools/subagent/invoke-step.ts`.

### Summary

Every time a blocking workflow-tool run finishes, `handleWorkflowToolRunOutcome` runs two steps, and both take the whole `DurableSessionState` as input. `releaseAgentInvocationOwnerStep` also returns it as its result, even when nothing changed. So each tool completion appends three full copies of the session state to the owner run's event log. In our longest session that was 41% of the log.

### Code

`handleWorkflowToolRunOutcome` ([0.64.1 L70-L83](https://github.com/vercel/eve/blob/eve%400.64.1/packages/eve/src/execution/session-workflow-tool-run.ts#L70-L83), [0.66.3 L71-L84](https://github.com/vercel/eve/blob/eve%400.66.3/packages/eve/src/execution/session-workflow-tool-run.ts#L71-L84)):

```ts
await cancelAgentInvocationOwnerStep({
  ownerId: message.from.runId,
  serializedContext: cursor.serializedContext,
  sessionState: cursor.sessionState,
});
const released = await releaseAgentInvocationOwnerStep({
  cancelled: message.result.status === "cancelled",
  ownerId: message.from.runId,
  sessionState: cursor.sessionState,
});
```

`cancelAgentInvocationOwnerStep` ([task-cancel.ts L25-L41](https://github.com/vercel/eve/blob/eve%400.66.3/packages/eve/src/execution/tools/subagent/task-cancel.ts#L25-L41), same in both versions) is a `"use step"` that only reads the handles claimed by `ownerId` (`getAgentHandleStore(state).handles` filtered to `phase === "claimed"`) and returns early when there are none.

`releaseAgentInvocationOwnerStep` ([0.64.1 L507-L527](https://github.com/vercel/eve/blob/eve%400.64.1/packages/eve/src/execution/tools/subagent/invoke-step.ts#L507-L527), [0.66.3 L498-L518](https://github.com/vercel/eve/blob/eve%400.66.3/packages/eve/src/execution/tools/subagent/invoke-step.ts#L498-L518)) returns its input state when the handle store did not change:

```ts
return {
  sessionState:
    session === durable
      ? input.sessionState
      : replaceDurableSessionSnapshot({ session, state: input.sessionState }),
};
```

Our workflow tools never invoke agents, so they own no handles. The cancel step is a no-op and the release step returns its input, but both still persist the full state (the cancel step also persists `serializedContext`).

### Measurement

Setup: Next.js app on Vercel, eve 0.64.1 (bundled `@workflow/core` 5.0.0-beta.55), Gemini Flash via Vertex. An image-generation agent whose model calls fan out about 10 blocking `defineWorkflowTool` generation tools per turn.

We decrypted every payload in one long session's owner-run event log (about 26 h, 57 user messages, 1,255 payloads, 392 MB as stored) and summed stored bytes by step and field:

| Step | Field | Copies | Stored MB | Share |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `turnStep` | input | 225 | 106 | 27% |
| `turnStep` | result | 225 | 106 | 27% |
| `cancelAgentInvocationOwnerStep` | input | 135 | 54 | 14% |
| `releaseAgentInvocationOwnerStep` | input | 135 | 52 | 13% |
| `releaseAgentInvocationOwnerStep` | result | 135 | 52 | 13% |
| `dispatchCoordinationStep` | input + result | 50 | 21 | 5% |

- The cancel/release rows add up to 159 MB (41% of the log) from 135 tool completions.
- Every `releaseAgentInvocationOwnerStep` result was the size of its input (within about 100 bytes). Every cancel result was 38 bytes.
- Late in the session one state copy was about 0.8 MB stored (1.6 MB before compression). One 9-tool fan-out appended 19 MB of cancel/release payloads in 11 s.
- Re-encoding the same log with those two steps carrying no state gives 232 MB instead of 392 MB.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an agent with one blocking `defineWorkflowTool` that returns a short string and does not invoke agents.
2. Have a few turns of conversation, then ask the model to call the tool several times in one turn.
3. In the owner run's event log, compare the `cancelAgentInvocationOwnerStep` input and the `releaseAgentInvocationOwnerStep` input and result with the `turnStep` input. All four are full session-state copies.

### Current vs. expected behavior

Current: three full session-state copies per workflow-tool completion, whether or not the run owns any agent handles.

Expected: settling a run that owns no agent handles writes nothing proportional to session size, and a run that does own handles writes only what changed.

### Suggested fix

- Look up the handles owned by `message.from.runId` in the workflow body, the way `handleWorkflowToolRunOutcome` already reads `cursor.sessionState` for `findBlockingWorkflowToolRun`, and skip both steps when there are none.
- When there are handles, pass each step only what it needs: the claimed handles (address, identity) plus context for cancel, and the owner id plus handle list for release.
- Have release return the new handle list, or a no-change marker such as `{ changed: false }`, instead of the whole `DurableSessionState`. The transitions it calls (`applyTaskAgentHandleCommand`, `abandonAgentInvocationOwners`) are pure, so they could also run in the workflow body.

#3507 (turn-step delta returns) keeps full checkpoints for coordination steps like these, so it does not cover this.

issues.title: Tool result serialization crashes on nested undefined values
issues.body:
## Summary

A tool can execute successfully and then fail the parent `turnStep` when its result contains an `undefined` property. The failure happens while Eve projects the result into model-visible JSON.

## Reproduction

Define a blocking workflow tool that returns the raw result of `ctx.ask()`:

```ts
import { defineWorkflowTool } from "eve/tools";
import { z } from "zod";

export default defineWorkflowTool({
  description: "Ask a yes-or-no question.",
  inputSchema: z.object({}),
  async execute(_input, ctx) {
    "use workflow";
    return await ctx.ask({
      prompt: "Would you like to continue?",
      display: "select",
      options: [
        { id: "yes", label: "Yes" },
        { id: "no", label: "No" },
      ],
      allowFreeform: true,
    });
  },
});
```

Call the tool and select an option. The question resolves successfully, but the parent turn fails after retries.

## Observed behavior

With `eve@0.66.3+git.cd82f57e61b4fc64`:

```text
FatalError: Step "step//eve@0.66.3+git.cd82f57e61b4fc64//turnStep" failed after 3 retries: Cannot convert undefined or null to object

TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object
    at Object.entries (<anonymous>)
    at toMutableJsonValue (.../eve.mjs:117381:28)
    at toMutableJsonValue (.../eve.mjs:117381:47)
    at toToolResultOutput (.../eve.mjs:117374:10)
    at projectToolResultOutput (.../eve.mjs:117356:59)
    at resolvePendingCoordination (.../eve.mjs:117276:20)
```

Tracing shows that the workflow action itself completed with an answer equivalent to:

```json
{"status":"answered","optionId":"yes"}
```

The likely trigger is an optional property on the underlying result whose value is `undefined`. `toMutableJsonValue()` handles `null` and JSON primitives but falls through to `Object.entries(value)` for `undefined`.

## Expected behavior

Tool result projection should tolerate nested `undefined` values—either by omitting object properties (matching `JSON.stringify`) or converting them to a supported JSON value—rather than failing the entire session.

## Workaround

Normalize the response before returning it, constructing an object that contains only defined properties.

issues.title: Session history keeps tool-result images and Gemini thought signatures from every completed turn (~85% of each persisted state copy)
issues.body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

**eve 0.64.1**, unchanged in 0.66.3 and on `main`. eve persists the full session state, including `snapshot.session.history`, as the input or result of most workflow steps, so everything kept in history is written again on every step. For an image agent two things dominate that history, and both stay for every later turn:

- image bytes in `tool-result` outputs (a tool that shows generated images to the model returns them as file parts via `toModelOutput`);
- Gemini thought signatures (`thoughtSignature` in the parts' `providerOptions`).

Media is stubbed only when compaction runs. `stubContentOutputFileParts` ([compaction-prompt.ts, 0.64.1 L247](https://github.com/vercel/eve/blob/eve%400.64.1/packages/eve/src/harness/compaction-prompt.ts#L247), [0.66.3 L239](https://github.com/vercel/eve/blob/eve%400.66.3/packages/eve/src/harness/compaction-prompt.ts#L239)) is called only from `capToolResults` inside `toolResultCapHeuristic` ([compaction.ts, 0.64.1 L308-L322](https://github.com/vercel/eve/blob/eve%400.64.1/packages/eve/src/harness/compaction.ts#L308-L322), [0.66.3 L307-L321](https://github.com/vercel/eve/blob/eve%400.66.3/packages/eve/src/harness/compaction.ts#L307-L321)):

```ts
const output = stubContentOutputFileParts(part.output) as typeof part.output;
```

Inbound attachments already follow a different rule: `hydrateSandboxAttachments` ([attachment-staging.ts L129-L136](https://github.com/vercel/eve/blob/eve%400.66.3/packages/eve/src/harness/attachment-staging.ts#L129-L136)) inlines bytes for one model call and keeps history ref-only. Tool-result media gets no such treatment.

Setup: Next.js app on Vercel, eve 0.64.1, Workflow 5.0.0-beta.55, Gemini Flash via Vertex, an image-generation agent that fans out about 10 generation tools per turn. One session: 57 user messages, 392 MB owner-run log.

- In the largest persisted state copies (about 0.8 MB stored, 1.6 MB raw), inline image data was about 52% of stored bytes and thought signatures about 34%, so about 85% together. Neither compresses much.
- History held 16 images before the session's only compaction (threshold about 258K tokens on a 1M-token model), which ran at user message 48 of 57. The first turn's image was rewritten into every state copy until then.

Method: decrypted each state copy, applied the change to `history`, re-encoded with the same serializer and zstd level, and compared stored sizes. "Completed turns" means every message before the last real user message.

| Change applied to every state copy | Log size | vs. actual |
|---|---:|---:|
| none (actual) | 392 MB | |
| stub tool-result images in completed turns (current turn keeps bytes) | 212 MB | -46% |
| drop thought signatures in completed turns | 269 MB | -31% |
| both | 88 MB | -77% |

This also interacts with #3799 and its fix #3802: once image bytes stop counting toward the compaction estimate (correct for tokens), compaction, the only place media is stubbed today, will run even less often for image-heavy agents.

### Proposed solution

1. Keep tool-result media out of persisted history the way inbound attachments are: store a reference in history and hydrate the bytes only for the model call.
2. Where no store is available, stub file parts in tool results of completed turns with the existing `stubContentOutputFileParts` when the turn settles. The stub keeps filename and media type. An option could keep today's behavior for agents that need to look at old images again.
3. Thought signatures: if the Google provider confirms that signatures from completed turns are not needed on later requests, drop them from completed turns. We have not verified this; the provider and `@ai-sdk/google` owners would need to confirm it, and it should not ship without that.

### Alternatives considered

- A lower compaction threshold. About 100K tokens cut the same log by about 59% in simulation, but it summarizes away conversation the model still uses, and images are still rewritten on every step until each compaction.
- App-side changes can only shrink what tools return. What history retains, and for how long, is decided by eve.

issues.title: CLI preview deployments are unexpectedly created with target=production
issues.body:
### Vercel CLI version

55.0.0 (Node.js 24.15.0, macOS)

### Expected behavior

According to the [Vercel CLI deployment documentation](https://vercel.com/docs/projects/deploy-from-cli), `vercel deploy` creates a Preview deployment and `--prod` is required for Production. An explicit `--target=preview` should produce a Preview deployment.

### Actual behavior

On a newly linked project with no previous deployments, both commands below returned a deployment object classified as `target="production"`.

Attempt 1 — 2026-07-13T07:17:22Z:

```sh
vercel deploy --target=preview --yes
```

Result: `finalDeployment.target="production"`

Attempt 2 — 2026-07-13T07:44:32Z:

```sh
npx vercel@latest deploy --yes --no-wait --meta phase=staging-preview
```

Result:

```text
target="production"
environment=null
readyState="BUILDING"
region="sin1"
```

No `--prod` flag was used. Both deployments were canceled and deleted immediately.

### Project state before both attempts

- New, linked Next.js project
- No prior deployments or aliases
- Preview-only environment-variable records; zero Production records
- No custom domain
- No Git integration
- No custom deployment environment
- No project target override
- No `VERCEL_*` shell variables, CLI wrapper, `--prod`, or `VERCEL_TARGET_ENV=production` configuration

Current state is still zero deployments and zero aliases.

### Redacted correlation data

- Team: `viktor…projects`
- Project: `viktor-home…page`
- Project ID: `prj_XRn…lSKu`
- Attempt 1 Deployment ID: `dpl_74FU…n4Hq`
- Attempt 2 Deployment ID: `dpl_E4Gr…Dbdn`
- Attempt 1 event ID: `uev_qmQ6…FtQl`
- Attempt 2 event ID: `uev_xjE7…oL87`

### Documentation conflict

The documented default is Preview when `--prod` is absent. The first attempt additionally passed `--target=preview`, yet the returned Deployment target was Production.

Please clarify whether first deployments are intentionally forced to Production even when `--target=preview` is supplied. If so, please document that behavior and provide a supported way to create the first deployment as Preview only. If not, please investigate the deployment target classification.

issues.title: docs: `vercel redirects upload` CSV/JSON examples use `status`, which the CLI ignores — all redirects silently become 307
issues.body:
## Summary

The CSV and JSON examples documented at https://vercel.com/docs/cli/redirects for
`vercel redirects upload` use a `status` field. The CLI never reads that field, so
every redirect silently falls back to `307`, with no error and no warning.

## Documented format (from the docs page)

```csv
source,destination,status,caseSensitive,preserveQueryParams
/old-path,/new-path,301,false,true
```

The JSON example on the same page has the same problem (`"status": 301`).

## Why it fails

The actual schema field is `statusCode`, not `status`. See
[Bulk Redirects → Available fields](https://vercel.com/docs/routing/redirects/bulk-redirects),
where `statusCode` is documented with a default of `307`.

In the CLI:

- [`packages/cli/src/commands/redirects/upload.ts:318`](https://github.com/vercel/vercel/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/redirects/upload.ts#L318)
  reads only `statusCode` / `permanent`:

  ```ts
  const status = redirect.statusCode || (redirect.permanent ? 308 : 307);
  ```

- [`packages/cli/src/commands/redirects/validate-redirects.ts:137-158`](https://github.com/vercel/vercel/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/redirects/validate-redirects.ts#L137-L158)
  (`validateCSVStructure`) checks only that the header contains `source` and
  `destination`. Any unrecognised column passes validation silently.

So the documented format parses "successfully" and produces the wrong status code
on every row.

## Impact

I uploaded 111 redirects, every row `301`, using the header exactly as documented.
All 111 were created as `307`. I noticed this in the dashboard's bulk CSV upload
(same schema), where the review step proposed `307` for all of them.

A `307` where a `301` or `308` was intended is a silent SEO regression: search
engines treat it as temporary and do not transfer ranking signals. Because nothing
warns you, the mistake is only discoverable by inspecting the staged result row by
row, and on a large migration nobody checks all of them.

## Second issue on the same page

The example `/legacy/*` to `/modern/:splat` uses wildcard matching, but the Bulk
Redirects docs state: *"Bulk redirects do not support wildcard or header matching."*

## Suggested fixes

1. Fix both examples on `/docs/cli/redirects` to use `statusCode`, and remove the
   wildcard example.
2. Make `validateCSVStructure` warn (or fail) on unrecognised columns. The silent
   default to `307` is the dangerous part, since the wrong docs would have been
   harmless with a warning.
3. Optionally accept `status` as an alias for `statusCode`, given that it has been
   published as the official format.

issues.title: [services] @vercel/backends makes an outputDirectory that holds the entrypoint the function root, so a pnpm workspace service cannot load
issues.body:
**Environment**
- Vercel Services (Beta), Vercel CLI 59.25.4 with `@vercel/backends` 8.0.2. The builder code in `dist/index.mjs` is the same in 10.0.0, pinned by CLI 60.0.1.
- pnpm 10 workspace. The service lives below the repository root (`root: "apps/api"`).
- NestJS 12 app, ESM (`"type": "module"` in `apps/api/package.json`), Node 24.

**Configuration**

```json
{
  "services": {
    "api": {
      "root": "apps/api",
      "framework": "nestjs",
      "buildCommand": "pnpm build",
      "outputDirectory": "dist"
    }
  },
  "rewrites": [{ "source": "/(.*)", "destination": { "service": "api" } }]
}
```

`pnpm build` runs `nest build` and writes `apps/api/dist/main.js`.

**What happens**
- The build succeeds, but every request fails. The function log shows:

  ```
  Warning: Failed to load the ES module: /var/task/main.js. Make sure to set "type": "module" in the nearest package.json file or use the .mjs extension.
  SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module
  ```

- `maybeDoBuildCommand` finds `main.js` in `dist` and globs `dist/**` relative to `dist`. So the function's `filePathMap` puts `main.js` at the root (`main.js -> apps/api/dist/main.js`). The traced dependencies keep their repository paths (`node_modules/.pnpm/…`, `apps/api/node_modules/…`).
- `/var/task/main.js` therefore has no `package.json` with `"type": "module"` beside it, and its bare imports cannot resolve. A local copy of the function filesystem shows the same failure: `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'reflect-metadata' imported from …/main.js`.
- Leaving `outputDirectory` unset gives the same layout, because the builder then searches `dist`, `build` and `output` after the build command.
- Naming the built file instead (`"entrypoint": "dist/main.js"`) is rejected before the build: `Service "api" has entrypoint "dist/main.js" but that path does not exist.` The builder itself finds the entrypoint after the build command (#17284), but the services resolver checks for it before the build.

**Expected**
- Either keep the output directory's files at their repository path, as the `@vercel/nestjs` wrapper does (it returns `join(dir, entrypointFromOutputDir)`, so the handler stays at `dist/main.js` beside the service's `package.json` and `node_modules`),
- or accept a service `entrypoint` that the build command creates.

**Workaround**
`"entrypoint": "src/main.ts"` together with `"outputDirectory": "."` makes the builder compile the source instead of reusing `dist`. The `"."` behaviour is from #16761. Without `"."`, a `dist` left in the tree is picked up again.

**Reproduction**
1. Create a pnpm workspace with `apps/api`: a NestJS app with `"type": "module"`, `src/main.ts` calling `app.listen()`, and `"build": "nest build"`.
2. Add the `vercel.json` above at the repository root, and set the project framework to Services.
3. Run `vercel build`. Then open `.vercel/output/services/api/functions/index.func/.vc-config.json`: `handler` is `main.js` and `filePathMap` maps it to `apps/api/dist/main.js`. Deploy, and request any path.

issues.title: "vercel pull" fails when using project-scoped token, "Error: Could not retrieve Project Settings"
issues.body:
`vercel pull` is nonfunctional when using a project-scoped token. It only works when using a team-scoped token. This makes little sense, since the command is acting on a single project and should only require a project-scoped token to retrieve settings for that project.

https://github.com/vercel/vercel/issues/10874 is about the same error message, and correctly points out that the error message is bad. However, this issue is separate and reports the fact that the command should not be failing in the first place.

Frankly, I'm at a loss for how to properly configure GitHub Actions to deploy to Vercel, with this bug. As far as I'm aware, running `vercel pull` is what you're supposed to do (followed by `vercel build`, `vercel deploy`), but if it doesn't work when using a project-scoped token, then every individual repository ends up getting deploy access to every single project, which is just terrible from a security point of view.

Error trace, when using a project-scoped token:

```

Vercel CLI 59.1.3 (Node.js 26.4.0)
```

issues.title: vercel logs returns duplicate entries when there are more than 50 results and --limit > 50
issues.body:
`vercel logs --since <window> --json --limit N` returns duplicate entries once there are more than 50 logs in the time window. The first page (50 records) is fetched correctly; every subsequent page returns the same first page again. The CLI faithfully accumulates duplicates until --limit is reached.

The first 50 results get duplicated over and over until they fill the --limit

### Minimal reproduction 
Depends on the actual number of logs in your time window
```bash
# Window is small enough to fit in one page → no duplicates
$ vercel logs --since 7min --json --limit 100 \
  | awk '{n++; u[$0]++} END {print "total:", n; print "unique:", length(u)}'
total: 28
unique: 28

# Window crosses the page boundary → 50 unique entries returned twice
$ vercel logs --since 10min --json --limit 100 \
  | awk '{n++; u[$0]++} END {print "total:", n; print "unique:", length(u)}'
total: 100
unique: 50

# Actually any sufficiently large --since window is enough to reproduce this
$ vercel logs --since 12h --json --limit 100 \
  | awk '{n++; u[$0]++} END {print "total:", n; print "unique:", length(u)}'
total: 100
unique: 50
```

Duplicates are byte-identical — same id, same timestamp, same everything.

### Expected behaviour

The API should return the next page of results when ?page=N is incremented, and the cli should return distinct logs (if there are more than 50 logs, --limit 100 should return between 50 and 100 distinct logs)

### Assumption about the root cause

The request-logs endpoint (`/api/logs/?page=N&...`) appears to ignore page N and returns the same first page each time while still reporting `pagination.hasMore: true`. 
The CLI loop that drives this in `fetchAllRequestLogs` calls `fetchRequestLogs(..., { ...options, page })` with page = 0, 1, 2, ... and trusts `response.pagination.hasMore`. The pagination logic in the CLI itself looks correct; I suspect the server side is the issue.

https://github.com/vercel/vercel/blob/5b4ece0b528756012c21da9086ac8197eb134cfa/packages/cli/src/util/logs-v2.ts#L243-L272

Environment

- Vercel CLI: 53.1.0 (also 53.3.2)
- Node: 22.x
- macOS

issues.title: Update tar dependency to 7.5.9 in @vercel/fun to resolve deprecated warning
issues.body:
## Description

Installing the latest Vercel CLI (`vercel@50.22.0`) produces a deprecated package warning for `tar@7.5.7`:

```
npm warn deprecated tar@7.5.7: Old versions of tar are not supported, and contain widely publicized security vulnerabilities, which have been fixed in the current version. Please update. Support for old versions may be purchased (at exorbitant rates) by contacting i@izs.me
```

## Root Cause

The issue is caused by `@vercel/fun@1.3.0` having a hardcoded dependency on `tar@7.5.7` in its `package.json`, while the current version of `tar` is `7.5.9`.

## Dependency Tree

```
vercel@50.22.0
├─┬ @vercel/fun@1.3.0
│ └── tar@7.5.7 (deprecated)
└─┬ @vercel/backends@0.0.36
  └─┬ @vercel/nft@1.3.0
    └─┬ @mapbox/node-pre-gyp@2.0.3
      └── tar@7.5.7 (deduped)
```

## Reproduction Steps

1. Create a clean project: `mkdir test && cd test && npm init -y`
2. Install Vercel CLI: `npm install vercel@latest`
3. Observe the deprecated warning for `tar@7.5.7`

## Expected Behavior

Vercel CLI should use the latest version of `tar` (`7.5.9`) to avoid deprecated warnings and ensure security vulnerabilities are patched.

## Suggested Fix

Update `@vercel/fun` package to use `tar@^7.5.9` or `tar@latest` instead of the hardcoded `7.5.7` version.

## Environment

- Vercel CLI version: `50.22.0`
- Node.js version: `18.19.1` / `20.x`
- npm version: `9.2.0` / `10.x`
- OS: Linux (Ubuntu), macOS

## Additional Context

This issue affects CI/CD pipelines where deprecated warnings can clutter build logs and trigger security scanning alerts. While the security impact may be minimal for CLI usage, keeping dependencies up-to-date is a best practice.

Related: Issue #11543 (tar v4.4.18 was previously fixed in PR #13070)

issues.title: vercel.json schema declares draft-04 but uses draft-06+ keywords, so strict validators reject it
issues.body:
The schema at `https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json` declares `draft-04` but uses keywords that do not exist in draft-04, so it fails validation against the metaschema it names. Tools that honour `$schema` reject the document rather than applying it.

### Reproduce

```bash
curl -sO https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json
```

```python
import json, jsonschema
s = json.load(open("vercel.json"))
print(s["$schema"])                      # http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#
jsonschema.Draft4Validator.check_schema(s)
```

```
jsonschema.exceptions.SchemaError: {'type': 'object', 'additionalProperties': False,
 'required': ['root'], 'properties': {'root': {'description': 'Path to the servic...
```

Behaviour across metaschemas (`jsonschema` 4.26.0), same file, unchanged:

| metaschema | result |
| --- | --- |
| **draft-04** (the one it declares) | **REJECTED** |
| draft-06 | accepted |
| draft-07 | accepted |
| 2020-12 | accepted |

### Keywords that force this

Counting occurrences in the served file:

| keyword | count | introduced in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `const` | 21 | draft-06 |
| `if` / `then` | 15 / 15 | draft-07 |
| `propertyNames` | 2 | draft-06 |
| `exclusiveMinimum` | 3 | boolean in draft-04, **numeric** from draft-06 |

`exclusiveMinimum` is the one worth pausing on: in draft-04 it is a boolean modifier on `minimum`; from draft-06 it is a number. It is not merely unrecognised here, it means something different.

### Why it matters

Editors resolve this URL from `$schema` and from schema catalogues, and apply it while you type. A strict loader refuses the whole document at that point, which means no completion and no diagnostics — a config file with a typo looks exactly like a config file without one. Ajv in `strictSchema` mode is in the same position, and so is every Go/Java/Rust validator that reads `$schema` to pick its dialect.

Two things make this easy to miss from the inside: the file is consumed by Vercel's own tooling through a purpose-built reader (`packages/config/scripts/generate-types.ts` parses it by hand for code generation) rather than a general validator, and Vercel's TypeScript reader already assumes the newer keywords.

### Suggested fix

Change the dialect declaration to the one the content already uses:

```diff
-  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#",
+  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
```

No other change is required. draft-07 accepts everything currently in the file, and it accepts the `$data` references only as opaque annotations, which is the same treatment they receive today. If the intent is to keep `$data` functional, note that it is an Ajv extension rather than a spec keyword, so a `$comment` saying so would help other consumers.

### How this came up

I wrote a small mutation tester for validators — it feeds a validator inputs that ought to be rejected and reports what it lets through. Pointing it at served JSON schemas surfaced this one as a special case: the schema does not merely accept something it should reject, it cannot load at all under the dialect it names. The tool is https://github.com/simin-yuan/greencheck (MIT, no dependencies); the reproduction above stands on its own without it.

issues.title: CLI: every request fails with `TypeError: fetch failed` on Node.js 26 when a proxy env var is set (bundled undici 5 dispatcher vs Node's built-in undici 8)
issues.body:
### Summary

On Node.js 26, every Vercel CLI command fails with `TypeError: fetch failed` as soon as any proxy environment variable is present.

`dist/index.js` installs a global fetch dispatcher whenever a proxy env var exists:

```js
function hasProxyConfig(){return["HTTP_PROXY","HTTPS_PROXY","http_proxy","https_proxy","ALL_PROXY","all_proxy"].some(v=>process.env[v])}
// ...
if (hasProxyConfig()) {
  const { EnvProxyDispatcher } = await import("./chunks/fetch-proxy-<hash>.js");
  setFetchDispatcher(new EnvProxyDispatcher);
}
```

`EnvProxyDispatcher` is built on the CLI's bundled `undici@5.29.0` (`Agent` / `ProxyAgent`). That dispatcher is then handed to Node's **built-in** `fetch`. Node 24 embeds undici 7.x and accepts it; Node 26 embeds undici 8.x, which [removed legacy handler wrappers in v8.0.0](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/releases/tag/v8.0.0), so the v5 dispatcher rejects the new handler shape.

Root error (unwrapped `cause`):

```
TypeError: fetch failed
  cause: UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG: invalid onError method
```

### Reproduction

With `HTTPS_PROXY` (or any of the six names above) pointing at a working proxy:

```
$ vercel whoami        # Node 26.8.2
Error: An unexpected error occurred in whoami: TypeError: fetch failed
```

Minimal, without the CLI:

```js
// Node 26.8.2, using undici@5.29.0 as bundled by the CLI
import { ProxyAgent } from 'undici';           // 5.29.0

await fetch('https://api.vercel.com/v2/user', { dispatcher: new ProxyAgent(process.env.https_proxy) });
// -> TypeError: fetch failed  { cause: UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG: invalid onError method }

await new ProxyAgent(process.env.https_proxy).request({ origin: 'https://api.vercel.com', path: '/v2/user', method: 'GET' });
// -> 403  (the proxy itself works fine)
```

Node's own proxy support works on the same machine, same proxy:

```
$ NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 node -e 'fetch("https://api.vercel.com/v2/user").then(r=>console.log(r.status))'
403
```

### Environment

| | |
| --- | --- |
| CLI | 59.18.0 and 59.23.1 (`latest`) — both resolve `undici@5.29.0`; `packages/cli/package.json` on `main` pins `"undici": "5.29.0"` |
| Fails | Node 26.8.2 — `process.versions.undici` = `8.10.2` |
| Works | Node 24.21.0 — `process.versions.undici` = `7.29.1` |
| OS | macOS (arm64) |
| Proxy | local HTTP proxy with basic auth; `no_proxy` does not cover `api.vercel.com` |

`packages/cli/package.json` declares `"engines": { "node": ">= 18" }`, so Node 26 is inside the supported range.

### Notes

- This is not proxy-specific in its mechanism: `EnvProxyDispatcher`'s `directAgent` is also an undici 5 `Agent`, so once `hasProxyConfig()` is true, even requests that `no_proxy` excludes go through a v5 dispatcher.
- There is no documented way to opt out of the shim; the only inputs are `all_proxy` / `http_proxy` / `https_proxy` / `no_proxy`.
- `--debug` only prints `TypeError: fetch failed` and retries; the `cause` is not surfaced, which makes this look like a network/sandbox problem.

### Suggested fixes

1. Bump the bundled `undici` to `^8` (or to a version whose dispatcher handler shape matches the Node versions in `engines`).
2. Or skip the custom dispatcher when the runtime provides proxy support natively — Node's [`--use-env-proxy` / `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY`](https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#--use-env-proxy) (added v24.5.0 / v22.21.0) already parses `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` at startup.
3. Independently: surface `error.cause` in the CLI's error output so this fails loudly instead of as a generic `fetch failed`.

issues.title: @workflow/builders: JSON import attribute still stripped in 4.1.14 and 5.0.0-beta.57, all local steps fail with Nitro on Node 26
issues.body:
Related to #3157, which reported this on `@workflow/builders` 4.1.3 with Next.js + `@workflow/vitest` on Node 22. It still reproduces on the latest releases (4.1.14 and 5.0.0-beta.57), on Node 26, and with the Nitro integration. The fix proposed in #3160 has not been merged yet.

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| node | v26.8.2 |
| workflow | 4.8.9 (latest) |
| @workflow/builders | 4.1.14 |
| nitro | 3.0.260903-beta (`modules: ["workflow/nitro"]`, rolldown dev builder) |
| package manager | pnpm 12 |
| OS | macOS |

### Symptom

`start()` returns a run id and the workflow handler runs, but no step ever executes. Every step request returns 500 and the local queue retries indefinitely (256 attempts before I cancelled the run):

```
Handler error: TypeError [ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING]: Module "file:///…/node_modules/.pnpm/builtin-modules@5.0.0/node_modules/builtin-modules/builtin-modules.json" needs an import attribute of "type: json"
[world-local] Queue message failed (attempt 256, HTTP 500) { queueName: '__wkf_step_step//./src/steps/…', … }
```

### Why every app is affected, not only apps that import JSON

The generated `steps.mjs` contains builder code of its own. Right after the `step//workflow@4.8.9//fetch` registrations there is a top-level:

```js
var nodeBuiltins = builtin_modules_default.join("|");
new RegExp(`(?:from\\s+['"](?:node:)?((?:${nodeBuiltins})…`, "g");
```

So every project's step bundle depends on `builtin-modules`, and its externalized `./builtin-modules.json` import loses `with { type: 'json' }`. No app code is involved.

### Production builds are unaffected

Nitro's production build re-bundles `steps.mjs` with rolldown, which inlines the JSON (`.output/server/_libs/builtin-modules.mjs` holds the array), so only local dev breaks.

### Regression window

Local steps worked on `workflow` 4.2.0 / `@workflow/builders` 4.0.1 and broke after upgrading to `workflow` 4.8.9 / `@workflow/builders` 4.1.14. `builtin-modules` was already a dependency of 4.0.1, so the regression is in how the step bundle is produced.

### Not fixed in the v5 beta

In the published `@workflow/builders@5.0.0-beta.57` tarball there is still no `keepImportAttributes`, no esbuild `import-attributes` support override, and the esbuild target is still `es2022`, the same as 4.1.14.

### Suggested fix

#3160 looks like the complete fix: keep import attributes in the SWC transform and mark import attributes as supported for esbuild. Is anything blocking its review? Happy to test a canary.

issues.title: Durable run streams lose acknowledged chunks, and the live read blocks forever at the hole
issues.body:
## Summary

Chunks that a run's default user stream acknowledged, and that a live reader
received at write time, are later missing from the stream. The result is a
permanent hole in the chunk index sequence. Two consequences:

1. `streams.getChunks` (the paginated listing) skips the missing indices, and
   `streams.getInfo` still reports the original tail, so the loss is visible
   only as gaps in `index`.
2. The live read (`GET /v3/runs/:runId/stream/:name?startIndex=N`, used by
   `Run.getReadable({ startIndex })`) stops at the first missing index of a
   stream that is not closed. It delivers nothing more until the server ends
   the response at its maximum duration, about 121 seconds later. Reconnecting
   from the same index blocks again, so a reader that starts at or before a hole
   can never reach the tail. The core reconnecting reader
   (`createReconnectingFramedStream`) retries that index indefinitely.

## Versions

From our lockfile at the time of the incident:

- `workflow` 5.0.0-beta.53
- `@workflow/core` 5.0.0-beta.53
- `@workflow/world` 5.0.0-beta.36
- `@workflow/world-vercel` 5.0.0-beta.48
- `@workflow/errors` 5.0.0-beta.21

Our deployment carries local patches to these packages. The one on the stream
path bounds stream PUTs with a per-request wire deadline over HTTP/1.1 and never
replays an ambiguous append. It does not touch reads, and the chunks below were
acknowledged (the PUT returned 2xx) and delivered live before they went missing.

## Evidence

Production burst of 108 concurrent runs on one project, 2026-09-23 03:35 to
03:47 UTC, several streaming runs per function instance.

Example: `wrun_41M3659GYK0GZ2DP8ARBXR83JA` (769 separate holes, 832 indices)

- Live read during the run, 03:35:06 to 03:49:05 UTC: one connection, no
  reconnects, every frame delivered in order through the run's terminal frame.
- Afterwards: `streams.getInfo` reports `tailIndex: 19841`; paging
  `streams.getChunks` (limit 1000) returns 19,010 chunks, so 832 indices are
  missing. The first missing indices are 339, 424, 470.
- `GET /v3/.../stream?startIndex=0` delivers 339 frames (indices 0 to 338),
  then nothing until the server ends the response about 121 s later.
- `startIndex=339` delivers 0 frames until the server ends the response about
  121 s later.
- `startIndex=340` resumes and runs to the next missing index.
- A replay attempt after the run delivered the first 154 projected events in
  122.9 s and could not progress further.

Timing: a shorter run from the same burst replayed completely at 03:37 UTC and
later stalled at a hole on a fresh replay. The chunks were durable and readable
first, and disappeared afterwards; this is not a write that never landed.

A second campaign on a later deployment (2026-09-23 05:39 to 06:15 UTC), which
overlapped a second 108-run burst from 05:48, shows the same pattern: 7 of 18 streams now have holes
(340 missing of 41,534 chunks). Two of them replayed every index through their
terminal right after the run and lost chunks afterwards:

- `wrun_41M36CF0G60GJN4M233414KTVE`: full replay of 3,475 events after the run;
  now tail 3627 with indices 3377, 3443, 3444 and 3600 missing.
- `wrun_41M36CEZ3Y0GMP3RN4AXT73N3B`: full replay of 5,901 events after the run;
  now tail 6082 with 61 single-index holes, first at 3313.

Nearly every hole is a single index between two consecutive deltas of the same
tool call or text block, which one writer appends in order, often in one
multi-chunk PUT. The client never sends an index (HTTP PUT bodies carry only
length-prefixed chunks; we do not enable the WebSocket stream writer). Streams written at lower concurrency have no holes: 10 runs
from 04:38 to 05:40 UTC (about 20 to 30 concurrent runs on the project) span
1,143,156 chunks with none missing, and a 5-run campaign from 04:39 to 05:17
spans 26,807 with none missing. The loss appears to scale with concurrent
write load.

## Expected

- An acknowledged chunk stays readable for the stream's retention period.
- If a chunk can be lost, the live read should not wait forever on a missing
  index below the stream's known tail. It could skip to the next existing index,
  or return an error that names the missing range, so a reader can resume from
  the next existing chunk instead of timing out repeatedly.

## Related question: streams never report closed

Every completed run we sampled (7 of 7, 3 to 45 minutes after completion, tails
227 to 3273) reports `done: false` from `streams.getInfo`, for example
`wrun_41M36CEW2X0GR5K7Q447Q5V2TE` (tail 227), `wrun_41M3667J960GNT1TZYAJF7160M`
(tail 272) and `wrun_41M369KEVY0GKW44KP95C11SC1` (tail 3273). Our steps release
their writers and never call `close()`, relying on the documented behavior
("Streams are automatically closed when the workflow run completes"). We could
not find a client-side close at run completion in `@workflow/core` beta.53, so
we assume the close is server-side. Is it expected to happen for runs completed
through `run_completed`? A closed stream would let `isVerifiedComplete` accept a
clean EOF and let the live read end at the tail instead of waiting for the
server's maximum duration.

## Our mitigation

Readers keep one `Run.getReadable` read per connection. When it stalls or ends
below the tail `streams.getInfo` reported, they page `streams.getChunks`, which
lists only existing chunks and never blocks, decode the pages with the SDK's own
deserializer, skip and count the missing indices, and resume the live read after
the tail. `getChunks` has no start index, so reaching a hole at index N costs
N / 1000 pages from the first chunk; during the burst our read-only scanner also
received HTTP 429 on every stream it listed. A `startIndex` (or an index-seeking
cursor) on `getChunks` would make this cheap. This routes around the stall but
cannot restore the lost content.

issues.title: world-postgres: job attempt cap equals core's max-deliveries delivery, so a post-ceiling retry strands the run
issues.body:
## What happens

Once a workflow message goes past `MAX_QUEUE_DELIVERIES` (48), core stops doing real work and makes a single attempt to write `run_failed` (`MAX_DELIVERIES_EXCEEDED`). With #4421 (main) and #4422 (stable), a *transient* failure of that write (429, 5xx, `TRANSPORT`/`TIMEOUT`) throws instead of acking. The queue is expected to redeliver, and the redelivery retries only the terminal write.

world-postgres gives that throw nowhere to go. Every Graphile job is added with `maxAttempts: MAX_GRAPHILE_JOB_ATTEMPTS = 49`:

```ts
// packages/world-postgres/src/queue.ts:140
// Core records MAX_DELIVERIES_EXCEEDED on delivery 49.
const MAX_GRAPHILE_JOB_ATTEMPTS = 49;
```

Delivery 49 is the first post-ceiling delivery, and it is also the job's last attempt. If the handler throws there, `fail_job` leaves `attempts = max_attempts`, so `is_available` is false forever. The job is retired and the run stays `running`, which is the same end state the core fix set out to remove. On world-vercel the same throw is redelivered: VQS has no delivery cap, and it leaves about 14 h of the 24 h message TTL for retries. world-local allows 256 deliveries.

## Expected

The world-postgres job should keep a few attempts past core's ceiling, so the post-ceiling redelivery can actually happen.

## Notes

- Graphile's retry backoff is `exp(least(attempts, 10))` seconds (`graphile-worker@0.16.6` `failJob`). From attempt 10 onward each retry waits about 6.1 h, so extra attempts cost nothing in steady state and cannot hot-loop.
- The extra budget also leaves some slack for the lost-worker attempts described in #3992. It does not fix that issue: attempts are still spent on claim.
- On `stable`, jobs use `maxAttempts: 3` (#3994), so the core ceiling is never reached there. This issue is about `main` only.

Found while investigating #4421 / #4422.

issues.title: A handled getWritable() failure still fails the step after its body returns
issues.body:
## Summary

A step that writes to `getWritable()` fails after its body returns whenever any write to that stream failed, even when the step body caught the write error and finished its own work. There is no way to mark a step stream as best-effort, so a transient platform fault on a **secondary** output turns a completed step into a failed one.

## Versions

- `@workflow/core` 5.0.0-beta.51
- `@workflow/world-vercel` 5.0.0-beta.46

## What happens

1. The step body writes UI chunks to `getWritable()`. A PUT to `/v2/runs/<run>/stream/<name>` fails (for example `Stream write failed: HTTP 503`, or `transport failure after 300005ms (UND_ERR_INFO)`). `world-vercel` correctly doesn't retry the append (`streamer.js`, stream retry options skip 5xx because appends aren't idempotent).
2. The step body catches the rejected `writer.write()`, stops writing to that stream, and finishes its real work (it persists the result elsewhere and settles billing). Then it returns normally.
3. `getWritable()` pushed the flushable state's promise into `ctx.ops` (`step/writable-stream.js`: `ctx.ops.push(state.promise)`). The pipe failure rejects it (`flushable-stream.js`, `flushablePipePerChunk` catch → `state.reject(err)`).
4. After the body returns, `runtime/step-executor.js` awaits `Promise.all(ops)` in the `opsSettled` race and rethrows every rejection except `AbortError` / `ResponseAborted` (`isClientDisconnectError`). So the step fails with the stream's error. With `maxRetries: 0` the run ends `failed`, and anything the workflow does after the step (settling state, enqueueing analytics from the step's return value) never runs.

Result: the user-visible work is complete, but the run is recorded as failed and the step's return value is lost.

## Expected

A way for a step to own the failure of a stream it wrote to. Any of these would work for us:

- an option such as `getWritable({ failStepOnError: false })` (or a best-effort mode) that keeps the stream out of the step's fatal ops;
- an API to abandon or detach a writable after a handled failure, so its rejection no longer fails the step;
- treating a stream failure the step body already observed (the writer's `write()` / `close()` rejected into user code) as handled.

## Repro sketch

In a step: get a writer from `getWritable()`, write a few chunks, make a write fail at the sink (a world whose `streams.write` rejects with a `StreamError` of status 503 reproduces it), catch the rejection, release the lock, and return a value. The step fails with the stream error instead of completing with the value.

issues.title: Shared Postgres world: queue namespaces don't isolate claiming, and startup recovery re-enqueues other applications' active runs
issues.body:
## Summary

When multiple independent applications share one `@workflow/world-postgres` database, they execute each other's workflow runs. Queue namespaces (`WORKFLOW_QUEUE_NAMESPACE`) do not prevent this, for two independent reasons:

1. **Claiming ignores namespaces.** The graphile-worker task identifiers are `${jobPrefix}flows` / `${jobPrefix}steps` — the namespace only prefixes the topic string *inside* the message. Any consumer polling the same database claims any namespace's jobs, and `createTaskHandler` then reconstructs the queue name using the *consumer's own* prefix (`const queueName = `${queue}${messageData.id}``), so the foreign job is executed locally instead of being skipped.
2. **Startup recovery is unscoped.** `reenqueueActiveRuns` lists **all** pending/running runs with no namespace/deployment filter and re-enqueues each under the *booting* application's namespace prefix. So every application boot takes over every other application's in-flight runs. #2888 fixed *which* namespace the recovered runs are enqueued under, and #2667 scoped world-local recovery by tag — but the Postgres world still passes its raw, unfiltered `storage.runs` into recovery (`packages/world-postgres`'s `start()`), so cross-application takeover remains. Notably, `workflow_runs.deployment_id` exists in the schema but world-postgres hardcodes `getDeploymentId()` to `'postgres'`, so it can't be used for scoping today.

Code references (checked against `@workflow/world@5.0.0-beta.21` and `@workflow/world-postgres@5.0.0-beta.27`, the latest betas as of 2026-07-17):

- `packages/world/src/recovery.ts` — `runs.list({ status, resolveData: 'none', ... })` with no scoping parameter.
- `packages/world-postgres/src/queue.ts` — `getJobQueueName()` derives the task identifier from `jobPrefix` only; `createTaskHandler()` rebuilds the queue name from the local prefix without validating the producer's namespace.
- `packages/world-postgres/src/index.ts` — `start()` → `reenqueueActiveRuns(storage.runs, queue.queue, 'world-postgres', config.namespace)`.

## How we hit this

We run a self-hosted platform that hosts many independent Eve agents (each is its own app/process), and initially pointed all of them at one `WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL`. Eve already derives a distinct `WORKFLOW_QUEUE_NAMESPACE` per agent, so topics were namespaced — yet agents intermittently executed each other's turns with the wrong application's code and credentials (surfacing as flaky provider/API-key errors, depending on which runner won the claim). Tracing it led to the two mechanisms above.

## Repro sketch

1. Two apps A and B (any two workflow apps with same-named workflows — e.g. two instances of the same framework), same `WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL`, distinct `WORKFLOW_QUEUE_NAMESPACE`.
2. Start a long-running workflow in A.
3. While it is `running`, boot B. B logs `[world-postgres] Re-enqueued N active run(s) on startup` including A's run, under B's namespace.
4. B's runner claims and executes A's run (same `workflow_flows` task id; handler reconstructs the topic with B's prefix). With distinct `WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_JOB_PREFIX` values the takeover becomes deterministic: the re-enqueued foreign run can *only* be claimed by B.

## Suggested directions

Either would resolve this class of issue:

- Scope claiming and recovery to the world's identity — e.g. include the namespace in the graphile task identifier (or validate the producer namespace in the handler and re-enqueue/skip on mismatch), and give `runs.list` a filter that `reenqueueActiveRuns` passes through (the `deployment_id` column looks like a natural hook, similar in spirit to the world-local tag scoping in #2667).
- Or, if a Postgres world database is intended to be exclusive to a single application, state that explicitly in the world-postgres docs — today nothing fails loudly when two applications share one database; they just silently cross-execute.

## Workaround

We moved to one Postgres database per application (derived from a base URL, created + `workflow-postgres-setup` bootstrapped on demand). That fully isolates storage, queue, and recovery, and has been working well — sharing it here for other self-hosters who hit the same symptom.

issues.title: Refuse to replay a run stamped above core's SPEC_VERSION_MAX_SUPPORTED on every World
issues.body:
From the formal-model review of #4327 / #4366 / vercel/workflow-server#1044 (vercel/workflow#4406, findings C4, E1 and W1).

`requiresNewerWorld` is only called in world-local and world-postgres, and it compares against the World package's `SPEC_VERSION_MAX_SUPPORTED`, not core's. On the Vercel path nothing refuses a run whose `specVersion` is above what the executing core can read. Such runs are reachable through:

- an explicit `start({ specVersion })`, a same-deployment replay, or a CLI fallback stamp above the target's version (C4). The model shows an explicit 8 on a spec-7 or `stable` victim unlocks hook force-claim, and the victim's `await hook` is stranded.
- a package skew where world-postgres is newer than core (W1).

Fix: in core's runtime, before replaying, fail closed (the same error `requiresNewerWorld` raises) when `run.specVersion > SPEC_VERSION_MAX_SUPPORTED` from `@workflow/core`'s own view, on every World. This is one check, and it covers all of the above. (E1, where an executor attests more than it was validated for, is fixed separately in #4366.)

issues.title: Lower the cross-deployment probe-miss floor to spec 3 once executors raise under-stamped runs
issues.body:
Follow-up to #4327 (review: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/pull/4327#discussion_r4098627141).

When a cross-deployment `start()` gets no answer from the target's capability probe, #4327 stamps the run with `SPEC_VERSION_SUPPORTS_SLOT_IDENTITY` (6). That is the lowest version a v5 runtime can execute on the Vercel World, but a `stable` (spec 3) target rejects the run. #4327 therefore gives the first probe to a deployment a 10 s budget, caches answers per deployment, and gives later probes after a miss 2 s.

Once executors attest their version on `run_started` and the backend raises an under-stamped run to it, a v5 target heals a stamp that is too low. The probe then only has to prevent a stamp that is too high, so the miss floor can drop to `SPEC_VERSION_SUPPORTS_CBOR_QUEUE_TRANSPORT` (3) and the first-probe budget back to 2 s.

Blocked on, all deployed:
- [ ] #4366: world-vercel sends `executorSpecVersion` on `run_started`.
- [ ] vercel/workflow-server#1044: the backend raises the run, including
  - [ ] the resilient-start path (`run_started` arriving before `run_created`, which both v4 and v5 `start()` allow since they send the two in parallel), and
  - [ ] a retryable response instead of a doomed fall-through when a fresh log is required but not yet readable (`run-created-not-committed`, and `log-not-fresh` / `run-created-not-first` on a pending run).

The formal model on #4406 (finding C3) adds two constraints:
- [ ] The raise is **enabled** on the whole server fleet (it ships behind `run-spec-version-upgrade`, default off), and every v5 target a caller can reach sends `executorSpecVersion`. A published v5 beta without #4366 that misses the probe would otherwise be stamped 3 and fail every delivery.
- [ ] Decide the `attributes` gate on a miss. A floor of 3 refuses `attributes` / `experimental_retention` on every slow or missed probe, since both need 4. Either floor at `SPEC_VERSION_SUPPORTS_ATTRIBUTES` (4), which a v5 target still heals, or skip that gate on a miss.

Then change `resolveCrossDeploymentSpecVersion` in `packages/core/src/runtime/start.ts` and `CROSS_DEPLOYMENT_CAPABILITY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`.

issues.title: Example proposal: cookieless analytics with native MCP integration for AI agents
issues.body:
## Proposal

A `solutions/` example showing how to integrate **cookieless web analytics** into a Next.js app, with **native MCP** so coding agents (Cursor, Claude, Codex, Windsurf) can install + query analytics in one prompt. Would slot in next to `script-component-strategies` and `script-component-ad`, which cover related `<Script>` patterns.

The framework already has `framework-boilerplates/xmcp` showing how to *build* an MCP server. This proposal is the complementary case: how to *consume* an MCP-aware analytics service from a Next.js app, end to end.

## What the example would demonstrate

1. **Cookieless tracker installation** — one `<Script>` in `app/layout.tsx`, gated on `NEXT_PUBLIC_GIZMO_KEY`. No cookie banner needed under CNIL/EDPB. `afterInteractive` strategy so the tracker doesn't compete with LCP.
2. **MCP server integration** — the AI coding agent connects via the hosted MCP endpoint, OAuth onboarding via dynamic client registration (RFC 7591), and can run setup operations (`setup_analytics_for_site`, `verify_install`), workflow operations (`summarize_all_sites`, `explain_traffic_change`), and query primitives (filterable breakdowns, time series).
3. **Custom event tracking via Vercel functions** — a small API route showing how to fire server-side events alongside the client tracker.

## Why this is useful here

- Vercel's audience increasingly uses AI coding agents — this is the only end-to-end example showing the "talk to your analytics from your editor" workflow.
- Cookieless analytics is the de-facto choice for any EU-facing Next.js site that doesn't want a consent banner. There's no example covering that pattern today.
- Builds naturally on `script-component-strategies` (script loading), which is the closest existing example.

## Why I'm raising it as an issue first

I'd build this against [Gizmo Analytics](https://gizmoanalytics.io) since that's the MCP-first analytics service I'm familiar with (free tier, MIT-licensed MCP server, hosted endpoint with full OAuth, [official MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=gizmoanalytics) listed). But I don't want to assume a brand-specific example is what you want — wanted to check first.

Three paths I can take, ordered by preference:

1. **Brand-agnostic** — `solutions/cookieless-analytics-mcp` using Gizmo as the concrete provider, with the README explicitly noting it's swappable for any MCP-aware analytics provider that follows the same `<Script>` + `gizmoanalytics.io/mcp`-style remote endpoint pattern.
2. **Branded** — `solutions/gizmo-analytics` similar to how `solutions/platforms-slate-supabase` is brand-specific.
3. **Built into an existing example** — fold the integration into one of the existing `solutions/` examples (e.g., a blog template) as an opt-in analytics layer.

Happy to build whichever fits your conventions, or skip if it's not a fit. Just looking for a thumbs-up + direction before I spend the time.

issues.title: onSuccess can fire for an obsolete request after the key changes to null
issues.body:
# Bug report ## Description / Observed Behavior When a `useSWR` request is in flight and the SWR key changes from a valid key to `null`, the previous request can still invoke `onSuccess`. This can cause a race condition when `onSuccess` closes over values from the latest render. For example: 1. Render with `conversationId = "A"` and a valid SWR key. 2. The request for conversation A starts. 3. Before the request completes, the component changes to `conversationId = "B"`. 4. Because another condition is temporarily not satisfied, the SWR key becomes `null`. 5. The request for A completes. 6. `onSuccess` is still called, but the callback comes from the latest render and therefore sees `conversationId = "B"`. This results in: ```text data: A conversationId: B ``` and can lead to application state being written to the wrong conversation. ## Expected Behavior Once the SWR key changes from a valid key to `null`, I would expect an in-flight request associated with the previous key to be treated as obsolete. In particular, its `onSuccess` callback should not be invoked after the hook has transitioned to the `null` key. ## Repro Steps / Code Example The following example uses a manually controlled promise so the race can be reproduced deterministically. ```tsx import { useState } from 'react' import useSWR from 'swr' let resolveA: (() => void) | undefined const fetcher = async ([, conversationId]: [string, string]) => { return new Promise(resolve => { if (conversationId === 'A') { resolveA = () => { resolve(`data-for-${conversationId}`) } } else { resolve(`data-for-${conversationId}`) } }) } export default function App() { const [enabled, setEnabled] = useState(true) const conversationId = enabled ? 'A' : 'B' // When enabled becomes false, the key becomes null. const key = enabled ? ['/api/conversation', conversationId] : null useSWR(key, fetcher, { onSuccess(data) { console.log('onSuccess:', { data, conversationId }) } }) return (
) } ``` ### Steps 1. Start the example. 2. The request for `conversationId = "A"` starts. 3. Click **"Switch to B (key -> null)"**. 4. `conversationId` is now `"B"` and the SWR key is `null`. 5. Click **"Resolve A request"**. 6. `onSuccess` is invoked. Observed output: ```text onSuccess: { data: "data-for-A", conversationId: "B" } ``` ## Additional Context SWR version: ```text 2.5.1 ``` React version: ```text 18.3.0 ``` The behavior appears to be related to the interaction between `keyRef`, `configRef`, and `callbackSafeguard` in `src/index/use-swr.ts`. In the current implementation, the effect that updates the key ref contains: ```ts useIsomorphicLayoutEffect(() => { if (!key) return // ... keyRef.current = key // ... }, [key]) ``` So when the key changes from a valid key to the falsy serialized value produced by `null`, the effect returns before updating `keyRef.current`. Later, `callbackSafeguard()` checks: ```ts const callbackSafeguard = () => { if (IS_REACT_LEGACY) { return ( !unmountedRef.current && key === keyRef.current && initialMountedRef.current ) } return key === keyRef.current } ``` At that point, the old request still has the old key and `keyRef.current` may still contain that same old key, so the safeguard passes. The success callback is then invoked through: ```ts getConfig().onSuccess(newData, key, config) ``` `configRef.current` is updated separately on each render, which means the callback can come from the latest render even though `newData` belongs to the obsolete request. Relevant source: https://github.com/vercel/swr/blob/main/src/index/use-swr.ts I am not sure whether the intended fix is to update `keyRef.current` before the `if (!key) return`, or to add an additional safeguard for the `key -> null` transition. I wanted to report the reproducible behavior first. ## Reproduction [StackBlitz reproduction](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-rmgkyxee?file=src%2FApp.tsx)

issues.title: `useSWRImmutable` ignores hook-level `refreshInterval`  since 2.4.0 (regression of #4208)
issues.body: # Bug report ## Description / Observed Behavior Since v2.4.0, `useSWRImmutable` ignores a `refreshInterval` passed **directly to the hook**, not just one inherited from a global ``. #4208 ("fix: Ensure useSWRImmutable overrides global refreshInterval") added this line to the `immutable` middleware: ```ts config.refreshInterval = 0 ``` However, middleware runs *after* the hook-level options have been merged with the context config. At that point the middleware cannot distinguish a globally configured `refreshInterval` from one passed as hook options, so it silently disables both. Polling that worked on ≤ 2.3.x stops with no error or warning after upgrading. ## Expected Behavior A `refreshInterval` passed directly to `useSWRImmutable(key, fetcher, { refreshInterval })` should still be honored — only a `refreshInterval` inherited from a parent `` (the case #4208 was about) should be ignored. If ignoring the hook-level option is intentional, it would be worth documenting as a breaking change, since it silently changes runtime behavior in a minor release. ## Repro Steps / Code Example ```tsx import useSWRImmutable from 'swr/immutable' function Status() { // On swr 2.3.6: fetches every second. // On swr >= 2.4.0: fetches exactly once, refreshInterval is discarded. const { data } = useSWRImmutable('/api/status', fetcher, { refreshInterval: 1000, }) return {data?.status} } ``` No global `` is involved. https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/thqfwl ## Additional Context SWR version: 2.5.0 (regression introduced in 2.4.0 via #4208; 2.3.6 behaves as expected).

issues.title: Suspense mode passes an uncached promise to use(), triggering React's uncached-promise warning
issues.body:
# Bug report ## Description / Observed Behavior In Suspense mode, `useSWR` calls `use()` with a promise that is re-created on every render ([`src/index/use-swr.ts#L875-L885`](https://github.com/vercel/swr/blob/v2.5.0/src/index/use-swr.ts#L875-L885)): ```ts const revalidation = hasKeyButNoData && isUndefined(preloadData) ? revalidate(WITH_DEDUPE) : resolvedUndef if (!isUndefined(returnedData) && hasKeyButNoData) { revalidation.status = 'fulfilled' revalidation.value = true } use(revalidation) ``` While there is no data this is a fresh pending promise returned by `revalidate()`; once data arrives it is the module-level `resolvedUndef`. React records the thenable passed to `use()` per hook index and errors when a re-render passes a different instance at the same index: ``` A component was suspended by an uncached promise. Creating promises inside a Client Component or hook is not yet supported, except via a Suspense-compatible library or framework. ``` React's current contract is that the promise handed to `use()` must be cached by the library ("except via a Suspense-compatible library or framework"), so this surfaces as an SWR-side warning. ## Expected Behavior No warning — the promise handed to `use()` should be stable across renders for the same key. ## Repro Steps / Code Example Two sibling `useSWR(..., { suspense: true })` components under one ``, with fetchers that resolve immediately: ```tsx const A = () =>

{useSWR('a', () => Promise.resolve('a'), { suspense: true }).data}

const B = () =>

{useSWR('b', () => Promise.resolve('b'), { suspense: true }).data}

createRoot(el).render( loading

}> ) ``` One `uncached promise` error is logged, for `B`. ### Why only some hooks hit it I instrumented `react-dom-client.development.js` (19.2.8) to log `trackUsedThenable` and which work-loop path each suspend takes. Trace for the repro above: ``` -- renderRootSync track i=0 status=fulfilled <- use(resolvedUndef) track i=1 status=pending <- use(revalidate(...)), A suspends UNWIND A <- throwAndUnwindWorkLoop, resets thenableState -- renderRootConcurrent track i=0 status=fulfilled <- A re-renders, data present track i=1 status=fulfilled track i=0 status=fulfilled <- B mounts track i=1 status=pending <- B suspends -- renderRootConcurrent REPLAY B <- replaySuspendedUnitOfWork, keeps thenableState track i=0 prev=same track i=1 prev=DIFFERENT <- warning ``` The deciding factor is which render pass the hook suspends in: | Path | Handling of `SuspendedOnImmediate` | `thenableState` | Warning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `renderRootSync` | always `throwAndUnwindWorkLoop` | reset to `null` | no | | `renderRootConcurrent` | `SuspendedAndReadyToContinue`, then `replaySuspendedUnitOfWork` if the thenable settled before the loop resumes | retained | **yes** | So a single suspense hook mounted on the initial (sync) render never warns — it always unwinds and re-renders with a fresh thenable state. A hook that first suspends inside a concurrent render, and whose promise settles before React resumes the yielded loop, hits the replay path and sees a different promise at the same index. That makes it easy to hit in practice, because mounting inside a Suspense retry counts: in a Next.js 16 app with a suspense `useSWR` component rendered from another suspense `useSWR` component's data (both hitting real API routes), the child warned on roughly every other page load — 8 occurrences over 5 reloads. ## Additional Context - Reproduced on swr 2.4.2 and 2.5.0, react / react-dom 19.2.8. - Development builds only — the warning does not exist in React's production build, so this is noise rather than broken behaviour. - Caching the promise per key and reusing it until it settles removes the warning in my testing, but I have not checked that approach against the `preload` / `keepPreviousData` / RSC `cacheData` paths.

issues.body:
# Bug report ## Description / Observed Behavior ```tsx async function formAction(formData: FormData) { const username = formData.get('username') as string; await trigger({ username }); await mutate({ username }); }

After clicking the button, the button's text should change to "Saving..."

``` When the button is clicked, the button never shows `Saving...` and is stuck with `Update`. ## Expected Behavior When the button is clicked, the button text should transition to `Saving...`, and back to `Update` after mutatoin is finishes. ## Repro Steps / Code Example Reproduction: https://github.com/sukka-reproductions/swr-mutation-transition Online demo: https://swr-mutation-transition.pages.dev/ ## Additional Context SWR version: 2.4.1 `useSWRMutation`'s `trigger` updates `isMutaing` via `setState({ isMutaing: true })`. However, `
`'s `action` prop creates a React async transition (similar to `startTransition`) here. In React async transitions, any state update (like `setState({ isMutaing: true })` in `useSWRMutation`) gets scheduled and "delayed", and will only happen (and re-render) after the async function is resolved/rejected. But this also means the `isMutaing` never got a chance to be rendered as `true`.

issues.title: Authentication Chapter (Chapter 14) Bug: Middleware Fails to Guard Routes
issues.body:
This report identifies three related issues in the authentication setup that collectively prevent the core security middleware from functioning correctly in current Next.js versions (tested on a recent version running Turbopack).

1. Critical Error: Middleware File Name Convention Failure
Issue: The global request interceptor (middleware) is non-functional because the required file name is not being used, causing the entire security layer to fail.

Observed Behavior: When the file is named proxy.ts (as used or implied in the tutorial), the Next.js console does not log a middleware compilation step, and the application allows unauthorized access to protected routes (e.g., /dashboard).

Fix Required: The file must be named middleware.ts. Upon renaming the file to middleware.ts and restarting the server, the console correctly logs ✓ Compiled middleware..., and the security logic is executed.

Impact: High. This breaks the core security feature of the entire lesson.

2. Logic Error: Incomplete Matcher Regular Expression
Issue: The provided regex in the middleware.ts file's export const config is incomplete, which is inefficient and required manual correction to achieve a clean redirect flow.

Provided Regex (Needs correction):

matcher: ["/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|.*\\.png$).*)"],

Problem: The |login path is missing from the exclusion list. This ensures the middleware runs efficiently and does not perform checks on the public login page.

Suggested Fix: The regex should be updated to explicitly exclude the login page:

matcher: ['/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|login|.*\\.png$).*)'],

Impact: Medium-High. Required for a clean, reliable, and efficient security implementation.

3. Implementation Gap: Post-Login callbackUrl Redirect Usage
Issue: The tutorial needs to ensure it explicitly includes the code to use the callbackUrl (passed as redirectTo in the form) for the final post-login navigation, as this step is crucial for completing the feature.

Suggested Fix: Ensure the final code for the authenticate Server Action explicitly shows how to retrieve the hidden redirectTo field from formData and calls redirect(redirectTo) upon success.

issues.title: Build Failure: bcrypt Module Not Found During Production Build
issues.body:
Hi Team,

I'm encountering a build failure while following the Next.js dashboard tutorial ([https://nextjs.org/learn/dashboard-app/getting-started](https://nextjs.org/learn/dashboard-app/getting-started)). The issue occurs during the production build process (`pnpm build`).

#### Description of the Issue

The build process fails with a "Module Not Found" error related to the `bcrypt` package. Specifically, the error message indicates that the native bindings for `bcrypt` cannot be located.

```
nextjs-dashboard % pnpm build
> @ build /Users/.../nextjs-dashboard
> next build

   ▲ Next.js 15.1.6

   Creating an optimized production build ...
 ✓ Compiled successfully
 ✓ Linting and checking validity of types    
   Collecting page data  ..[Error: Cannot find module '.../nextjs-dashboard/node_modules/.pnpm/bcrypt@5.1.1/node_modules/bcrypt/lib/binding/napi-v3/bcrypt_lib.node'
Require stack:
- .../nextjs-dashboard/node_modules/.pnpm/bcrypt@5.1.1/node_modules/bcrypt/bcrypt.js
- .../nextjs-dashboard/.next/server/app/seed/route.js
- .../nextjs-dashboard/node_modules/.pnpm/next@15.1.6_react-dom@19.0.0_react@19.0.0__react@19.0.0/node_modules/next/dist/server/require.js
- .../nextjs-dashboard/node_modules/.pnpm/next@15.1.6_react-dom@19.0.0_react@19.0.0__react@19.0.0/node_modules/next/dist/server/load-components.js
- .../nextjs-dashboard/node_modules/.pnpm/next@15.1.6_react-dom@19.0.0_react@19.0.0__react@19.0.0/node_modules/next/dist/build/utils.js
- .../nextjs-dashboard/node_modules/.pnpm/next@15.1.6_react-dom@19.0.0_react@19.0.0__react@19.0.0/node_modules/next/dist/build/worker.js
- .../nextjs-dashboard/node_modules/.pnpm/next@15.1.6_react-dom@19.0.0_react@19.0.0__react@19.0.0/node_modules/next/dist/compiled/jest-worker/processChild.js] {
  code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND',
  requireStack: [Array]
}

> Build error occurred
[Error: Failed to collect page data for /seed] { type: 'Error' }
 ELIFECYCLE  Command failed with exit code 1.
```


#### Context

This issue occurs during the `pnpm build` command, specifically when Next.js is attempting to collect page data. The error prevents a production build from being created.

#### Environment

- **Next.js version**: 15.1.6 (as per the tutorial)
- **pnpm version**: 10.6.5
- **Node.js version**: v20.18.0
- **Package Manager**: pnpm


#### Additional Information

During `pnpm install`, the following warning was also displayed:

```
Warning
Ignored build scripts: bcrypt, sharp.
Run "pnpm approve-builds" to pick which dependencies should
be allowed to run scripts.
```


#### Possible Root Cause

The `bcrypt` package relies on native bindings, which may not be correctly compiled or located during the build process, especially in a Next.js environment. The warning about ignored build scripts could be related.

#### Suggested Solution/Workaround

A workaround that resolves the issue is to replace `bcrypt` with `bcryptjs`. `bcryptjs` is a pure JavaScript implementation and does not require native bindings.

```
pnpm remove bcrypt
pnpm add bcryptjs
```


#### Impact

This build failure prevents users from completing the Next.js dashboard tutorial and deploying a production-ready application.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I hope this information is helpful in resolving the issue.

issues.title: add --open to the CLI
issues.body:
### Description

It'd be nice if there was a `--open` flag that just ran [open-cli](https://github.com/sindresorhus/open-cli) with the server URL, so folks don't need to either copy-paste URL strings, or set up parallel scripts that have to guess at the URL that needs to be opened.

### Why

Because it's one less "tiny bother that adds up over the course of a day's worth of testing" thing folks need to do in order to just focus on their work.

### Alternatives

everyone who needs it can manually install `open-cli`, add it to their npm script, and then run `serve` and `open-cli` in parallel. However, the "in parallel" part is not exactly trivial (with `npm-run-all` being effectively abandoned, and `&` not being cross-platform compatible syntax) and you'd have to "guess" the server URL. It's _probably_ localhost:3000 but that's configurable so it might not be. Also, looking at the dependency list for `serve`, adding `open-cli` to that would barely have an impact on `serve`'s footprint while making dev life just that bit easier.
