issues.title: Forum Facelift Meta Issue: Make /questions a place builders come back to
issues.body: ## What do you need? A restructure of the forum at `posthog.com/questions` so it stops behaving like a public inbox. **Interactive mock of the proposed page:** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/f9fbc5f1-12fc-49a9-a8b5-760c5c703e4e (i didnt wanna make a PR but also wanted to give us a visual to discuss what we're looking at and pick pieces for scope). **Why this, and the data behind it:** [channel POV doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1FG60R6pP8CLdL-XTQQBadStoxnP9P0iE50Ip4z0S5Do/edit) — short version, 4% of forum contributors ever post twice vs 17% in Discord, and ~95% of what gets posted is a question. This issue is the umbrella. If we agree on the shape I'll split it into the individual issues listed at the end. ## Schema changes? Mostly no. I initially thought we'd need schemas for discussions vs questions, but i think there's some existing escape hatches we can work with. A discussion type already sorta exists In `Squeak/components/Reply.tsx`: `topics?.data?.every((topic) => !topic.attributes.label.startsWith('#'))` Any thread whose topics all start with `#` already has "Mark as solution" suppressed. So topics can carry post kind, and the schema doesn't move. Two types of posts: **polls** (resolves) and **everything else** (doesn't). A poll isn't a `#` topic — it's the absence of one, so polls keep "Mark as solution" and the reputation flow, and **all 7,614 existing threads are already correct with no backfill.** I thought maybe we'd want article, but a long-form "here's how I did it" post is a discussion with a long body... calling it an article vs discussion just makes it more confusing and may not encourage discussion. **What does need backend work:** pinned posts (a new field on Question) and thread-level upvotes (#19660 — worth knowing post-level voting already works on roadmap items via `roadmapLikes`, `likeRoadmap()` and `VoteBox`, so that one's a copy job). Everything else below is frontend. ## The asks ### 1. Post kinds/category via topics - New `#` topics for the conversation kinds: `#building-with-ai` (may also call this self driving but im not sure the term is widely enough known and might feel too restrictive), `#shipped-and-learned`. Polls need no new topic — they're the default. - **Delete the line that filters Off-topic out of the compose picker** — `QuestionForm.tsx`: `topicGroups.filter((group) => group?.attributes?.label !== 'Off-topic')`. Users currently can't pick `#introductions`. One line. - **Two pickers at compose, not a multi-select:** "Kind" (required, the `#` topics) and "About" (optional, product topics). Creation currently connects one topic (`connect: [topicID || 346]`), so this needs two slots. - Consequence: flip `every` to `some` in the resolvable check, or a thread tagged both `#building-with-ai` and `Session replay` gets "Mark as solution" back. - Moderators keep post-hoc topic assignment, and it should re-fire team alerts ([issue already exists here](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog.com/issues/19756)) ### 2. Forum home restructure - **Three action cards**, asking last: 1) Building with AI 2) Shipped & learned 3) **Poll the hogs** (not married to any of these names, but the thinking behind the groups is "general AI shop talk", "show and tell", and "asking the community" — where the last one deliberately covers questions, sanity checks and roast-my-setup, since "judge my thing" and "what do you all do" are the same request with and without an artifact. Trying to be clear it's not questions for PostHog, but for the community.) - **Merged feed** with filter tabs (Everything / then a tab for each group) and a "kind"/topic badge per row - **Row anatomy:** upvote count left, title, kind badge, topic pills, avatar stack of thread participants, reply count, relative time. - **Sorts:** Most voices (default- most unique people replying), Latest, Most upvoted. "Most voices" ranks by distinct participants, not reply count. Most voted depends on #19660 for votes. - **Pinned posts** at the top of the feed, this give me a way to curate stuff, especially at the start to direct people... this will require another field type on a question. ### 3. Help a hog out A section showing posts 3 most recent unanswered posts. Asker avatar, how long they've waited, and a "Jump in" button (Jump in can make sense even if its a discussion or conversation and not just a "help me out" thing) Paired incentive (belongs with #19728, but i haven't actually added that in, so if we agree with this i can update it): **points for being the first reply on a zero-reply thread**, worth more than a normal reply, plus a "First responder" badge for the first time you do this? ### 4. The sidebar is the hub We have a lot of community esque pages that are hidden but do forum style things, so these should be accessible: `/community/dashboard`, `/community/subscriptions`, `/community/notifications`, `/community/achievements`. - **"Looking for…" section at the top** routes people out before they post in the wrong place: An answer → PostHog AI/Support Ticket via there if needed · A feature → `/roadmap` · Real-time chat → Discord · What's new here → `/community`. This should help drive the feature reuqest and bug report/troubleshooting into the channels we want them to go to. - Forum nav group below it, collapsible maybe since it duplicates the feed tabs. - Signed-in block: threads with new replies, replies waiting on you, points to next tier. All of this data already comes through `useUser()` so we can just show it. - **Suggested friends** — one rotating community member with a reason line and "Say hi on Discord". Only surface profiles that have a Discord link, so it goes somewhere they can actually DM that person. That field already exists from #19403. ### 5. New post flow One entry point, headed "What's up?", with two quiet off-ramps above the compose box (again to discourage the type of posts only PostHog can address instead of community): "I need a specific answer" → PostHog AI, and "I wish I could do…" → `/roadmap`. Then kind, about, title, body. ### 6. Topics - **Kind** is one of the tabbed sections (above) - **Topics is a set of**: **Product/tools topics** (should match what we have in website dropdowns) and **Additional topics** — these could be added on to categorize things that are more around non-product discussions like self driving topics or anything else that maybe comes up over time... One thing to flag that's really a bug, and I'd rather fix separately: **29 of our 58 topics have no group, which means users can't pick them when asking.** That includes **Desktop** and **Self-driving**, our newest product and our positioning. ### 7. Rename /questions → /forum With redirects from `/questions/*`, including topic pages and permalinks. If we need to avoid this we can but i think it just encourages people to ask posthog anything, instead of asking the community. ## Explicitly out of scope - **`posthog.com/community`** — separate workstream. I have some ideas for over there, but forum is a section of community, so it wont replace that page. - **A public leaderboard** — `LevelBadge` already renders reputation inline, and a ranked table looks sad at this volume. Suggested hogs instead. Future idea: suggest people based on overlapping topics! ## Decisions needed - [ ] `/forum` as the URL. `/conversations` fights Discord, `/discussions` collides with GitHub. - [ ] Default sort — Most voices, or Latest? Most voices self-curates with no editorial effort and would show a new user actual discussions rather than a stale ghost town, and new questions with no answers appears on the help a hog section. ## Potential Issues from this? (I worked this plan through with Claude — the ordering and dependencies are mine, the table is its formatting.) | | Issue | Depends on | | :- | :- | :- | | A | Forum home restructure — cards, merged feed, tabs, Help a hog out | — | | B | Post kinds via topics — two pickers, un-filter Off-topic, `every`→`some` | — | | C | Sidebar hub — Looking for…, collapsible nav, signed-in block, Suggested hogs | A | | D | New post flow with off-ramps | B | | E | Pinned posts — new field on Question | — | | F | Topic cleanup — group the ungrouped topics so Desktop and Self-driving are pickable | — | | G | Rename `/questions` → `/forum` + redirects | — | ## Deadline Great question.

issues.title: Validate MCP tool names in docs against the tool catalog
issues.body:
## What happened

The MCP section of `/docs/ai-evals` named six tools that no longer exist in the MCP catalog. An agent that followed the page found nothing on an exact search and had to recover with a broad one. [#20439](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog.com/pull/20439) corrects that page.

Nothing stops the same drift on another page. Docs name MCP tools inline in backticks across the `contents/docs/**/surfaces/mcp.mdx` pages and elsewhere, and a tool rename in the product repo does not fail any build here.

## Suggested check

The pieces already exist:

- `src/components/McpToolsList` reads the tool catalog that the build sources from `services/mcp/schema/tool-definitions-all.json` in PostHog/posthog.
- Every inline tool reference is a backticked kebab-case token.

A build-time or CI check could collect the backticked tokens that look like tool names, compare them against the catalog, and fail on a name that is absent. To keep false positives low, it could scan only pages that already reference the MCP server, or only tokens that match a known tool prefix.

Alternative, or in addition: let `McpToolsList` take a prefix or family filter, so a product page can render its own subset from the catalog instead of a hand-written table. `/docs/ai-evals` would then have no static tool names at all.

## Why it matters

A wrong tool name does not break a page visually, so nobody sees it. The reader who pays is an agent following the documented flow, and it fails at discovery.

issues.title: Run one abort sequence on every exit and clean up every run artifact on Windows, Linux and macOS
issues.body:
cc @PostHog/team-wizard-docs

## Problem

A wizard run leaves files behind, and the agent can keep working after the user quits. Ctrl-C in the TUI skipped every cleanup until #1351. Even with #1336 and #1351 merged:

- **Project leftovers.** `.posthog-wizard-cache/`, skills installed mid-run, `.posthog-events*.json` and orphaned `.tmp` files survive a cancel. A successful orchestrator or headless run never restores `.claude/settings.json`.
- **Temp leftovers.** Every agent run creates a `posthog-wizard-claude-*` directory and never removes it.
- **The agent outlives the cleanup.** Cleanups run while the agent is still working, so it can rewrite a file right after it's removed.
- **Most exits skip cleanups.** Only `wizardAbort` and three paths in `run-wizard` call `runCleanups()`. The other 61 raw `process.exit` calls run none.
- **Windows.** SIGTERM never reaches Node there, and Ctrl+Break (SIGBREAK) has no handler. CI runs on Linux only, so none of this is tested on Windows or macOS.

## The rules

1. **Anything that needs cleanup registers for cleanup.** Whatever creates a transient artifact calls `registerCleanup` when it creates it. The removal is synchronous file work.
2. **Any kill runs the abort sequence.** Ctrl-C, SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGBREAK all run the same sequence, below.
3. **It all gets cleaned up.** Every exit runs the registered cleanups: success, an error, a crash, a screen's Exit, and an abort.
4. **Ctrl-C says so.** The abort sequence starts by showing `Aborting run, cleaning up`, in the TUI and in headless output.

One limit. SIGKILL, Windows `TerminateProcess` and power loss run no code, so no handler can clean up after them. The next run finishes the job instead: a startup sweep removes known leftovers before anything else reads the project. [`recoverOrphanedSettingsBackups`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/bin.ts#L92) already does this for settings backups.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Ends["How a run ends"]
    KEY["Ctrl-C key"]
    SIG["SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGBREAK"]
    EXIT["success, error, crash, screen Exit"]
    KILL["SIGKILL, TerminateProcess, power loss"]
  end
  subgraph Abort["wizard-abort.ts"]
    SEQ["abort sequence, wizardCancel"]
    BACK["exit backstop (proposed)"]
    CLEAN["runCleanups"]
  end
  REG["registerCleanup at creation"]
  SWEEP["startup sweep (proposed)"]
  KEY --> SEQ
  SIG --> SEQ
  SEQ -->|"message, stop agent"| CLEAN
  EXIT --> BACK --> CLEAN
  REG -.->|"registered removals"| CLEAN
  KILL -.->|"next start"| SWEEP
```

Every transient artifact registers its removal. The abort sequence and the exit backstop both drain the same list. The sweep covers the kills that run no code.

## The abort sequence

`wizardCancel` from #1351 runs it, in this order:

1. **Show `Aborting run, cleaning up`.** TUI and headless.
2. **Stop the agent.** Abort the Claude SDK query and the pi session, so nothing writes after step 3. Today the SDK only SIGTERMs its child from its own `process.on('exit')`, after the cleanups have run. On Windows it only closes the child's stdin.
3. **Run the cleanups.** Synchronous file work only, so a second Ctrl-C can't interrupt it.
4. **Run the cancel hooks, capped at 2 s.** Network work, such as settling the task stream as an error.
5. **Flush analytics as `cancelled`, capped at 2 s.**
6. **Exit 128 plus the signal number.** 130 for Ctrl-C and SIGINT, 143 for SIGTERM, 129 for SIGHUP, 149 for SIGBREAK. `os.constants.signals.SIGBREAK` only exists on Windows, so the SIGBREAK code needs a fallback elsewhere.

A second Ctrl-C skips steps 4 and 5 and exits at once. The disk is already clean by then.

Every other exit gets step 3 from one `process.on('exit', runCleanups)` backstop. On Node 22, `exit` fires on `process.exit`, a drained event loop, an uncaught exception and an unhandled rejection. It doesn't fire on a signal with no handler, which is why rule 2 installs one for every signal.

## Cleanup ledger

Every artifact a run creates that shouldn't outlive it. Links pin `main` at `4acadcc2`.

| # | Artifact | Created by | Cleaned today | Target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | `<installDir>/.posthog-audit-checks.json` | [`seedAuditLedger`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/lib/programs/audit/seed.ts#L118), agent tools via [`writeLedgerAtomic`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/tools/tools.ts#L982) | Only by the skill's `rm` step. #1336 removes it on settle, throw and `wizardAbort` | #1336, then the backstop and the sweep |
| C2 | `<file>.tmp` next to any atomic ledger | [`writeJsonAtomic`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/shared/utils/atomic-ledger.ts#L12) | Never. Orphaned only by a kill between write and rename | Sweep |
| C3 | `<installDir>/.posthog-events.json` | The agent, planning events | pi harness only, [`src/agent/runner/harness/pi/index.ts:745`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/runner/harness/pi/index.ts#L745). The Anthropic arm relies on the agent | Register at run start when the program sets `eventPlanFile` |
| C4 | `<installDir>/.posthog-events-inventory.json` and `.part-N.json` | events-audit subagents, names at [`src/shared/constants.ts:113`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/shared/constants.ts#L113) | Never, on the host side | Register for events-audit runs |
| C5 | `<installDir>/.posthog-wizard-cache/` | Orchestrator queue, [`QUEUE_DIR_NAME`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/runner/sequence/orchestrator/queue.ts#L172) | `cleanupQueue` in a `finally`, [`src/agent/runner/sequence/orchestrator/orchestrator-runner.ts:601`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/runner/sequence/orchestrator/orchestrator-runner.ts#L601) and [`src/agent/runner/sequence/orchestrator/orchestrator-runner.ts:1338`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/runner/sequence/orchestrator/orchestrator-runner.ts#L1338). Not on an abort | Register at queue creation |
| C6 | Skills task agents install mid-run in `.claude/skills/` | Task agents | `sweepRunInstalledSkills`, [`src/agent/runner/sequence/orchestrator/orchestrator-runner.ts:1271`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/runner/sequence/orchestrator/orchestrator-runner.ts#L1271) and [`src/agent/runner/sequence/orchestrator/orchestrator-runner.ts:1340`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/runner/sequence/orchestrator/orchestrator-runner.ts#L1340). Not on an abort | Register at run start |
| C7 | The run's skill in `.claude/skills/<id>/` | [`installSkillById`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/runner/sequence/linear.ts#L64), [`downloadSkill`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/tools/tools.ts#L115) | TUI Keep Skills screen, on the user's choice, [`handleRemove`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/ui/tui/screens/KeepSkillsScreen.tsx#L90). Stays in CI and headless | Register at install. Choosing Keep unregisters it |
| C8 | `.claude/settings.json` moved to `settings.json.wizard-backup` | [`backupAndFixClaudeSettings`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/shared/claude-settings.ts#L271) | Registered at [`src/shared/claude-settings.ts:292`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/shared/claude-settings.ts#L292). Restored on a throw, `wizardAbort`, a signal, the linear outro ([`src/lib/programs/run-agent-legacy.ts:215`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/lib/programs/run-agent-legacy.ts#L215)) and the next start ([`bin.ts:92`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/bin.ts#L92)). Not on orchestrator or headless success | Backstop runs the existing registration |
| C9 | `*.wizard-backup` line appended to `.claude/.gitignore` | [`ensureBackupGitignored`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/shared/claude-settings.ts#L250) | Never | Remove the line on restore when this run appended it |
| C10 | `<tmp>/posthog-wizard-claude-XXXX/` | [`createIsolatedAgentConfigDir`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/stored-login.ts#L62), called at [`src/agent/agent-interface.ts:943`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/agent-interface.ts#L943) and [`src/agent/mcp-prompt-streaming.ts:389`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/mcp-prompt-streaming.ts#L389) | Never | Register at creation |
| C11 | Claude SDK child process | The SDK's `query` | SIGTERM from the SDK's own `exit` handler, after the cleanups. Only stdin closed on Windows | Abort sequence step 2 |
| C12 | pi in-process agent session | pi harness, cancellation at [`src/agent/runner/harness/pi/cancellation.ts:4`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/runner/harness/pi/cancellation.ts#L4) | Not stopped by `wizardCancel` | Abort sequence step 2 |

The rest are kept on purpose and stay out of the cleanup list:

| # | Artifact | Why it stays |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | Reports (`posthog-*-report.md`), SDK code and edits, `.env` keys and their `.gitignore` entry | The run's deliverable |
| K2 | Kept skills, and framework docs promoted by [`promoteReferenceSkill`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/agent/runner/sequence/orchestrator/orchestrator-runner.ts#L95) | The user chose them, or they're the run's durable artifact |

## Abort path ledger

Every way a run ends. The target column is what closes it.

| # | Path | Runs cleanups today | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Ctrl-C key in the TUI | No on `main`. Yes with #1351 | Abort sequence |
| S2 | SIGINT | Only under `runWizard`, through its handler. #1351 covers every TUI command and headless | Abort sequence |
| S3 | SIGTERM, never delivered on Windows | Only under `runWizard`. #1351 covers every TUI command and headless | Abort sequence |
| S4 | SIGHUP, a closed terminal. Windows kills the process about 10 s later | No. #1351 adds it | Abort sequence, inside the 10 s |
| S5 | SIGBREAK, Ctrl+Break on Windows | No | Abort sequence |
| S6 | Second Ctrl-C while aborting | #1351 exits at once after the sync cleanups | Unchanged |
| S7 | Uncaught exception or unhandled rejection | No. Node prints the error and exits 1 | Backstop |
| S8 | Normal return, the event loop drains, `process.exitCode` set, for example [`src/commands/mcp/add.ts:85`](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard/blob/4acadcc2b440946cc6353b42959c5ad5637bf1ea/src/commands/mcp/add.ts#L85) | No | Backstop |
| S9 | SIGKILL, Windows `TerminateProcess`, power loss | Impossible | Startup sweep |

</details>

The backstop closes every E row without editing it. A test per area (TUI screen, CLI command, runner) proves it.

## Platform notes

- **Windows signals.** SIGTERM can be listened for but never arrives. `process.kill` with SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGKILL terminates the target outright. Closing the console sends SIGHUP, then Windows kills the process about 10 s later. Ctrl+Break sends SIGBREAK.
- **Windows raw mode.** With processed input off, Ctrl-C arrives as a key, the same as on macOS and Linux. So #1351's key path should hold, but it's untested on Windows.
- **Windows renames.** `renameSync` over a file a watcher is reading may throw EPERM. That's an inference, not tested, and it matters for C1 and C2.
- **CI.** Every workflow runs `ubuntu-latest`. Nothing runs on `macos` or `windows`.

## Evidence

- [Node process signal events](https://nodejs.org/api/process.html#signal-events). Raw mode means Ctrl-C "is not generated" as SIGINT. SIGTERM is "not supported on Windows". SIGKILL "cannot have a listener installed". This is why the key path and the startup sweep are both required.
- [Microsoft SetConsoleMode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/setconsolemode). With `ENABLE_PROCESSED_INPUT` off, Ctrl-C is read as input rather than handled by the system.
- [signal-exit](https://github.com/tapjs/signal-exit). One handler for every exit, the same design as the backstop. It only fires for signals "if the signal would cause the process to exit", and it doesn't re-enter.
- **Checked locally on Node 22.** `process.on('exit')` fires on an uncaught exception and an unhandled rejection with code 1. It doesn't fire on SIGTERM with no handler.
- **Checked locally, Agent SDK.** The SDK kills its child from `process.on('exit')`. That runs after the wizard's cleanups, which is the ordering problem step 2 fixes.
- **Against.** I found no source arguing against one exit routine plus a sweep. The real risks are local: a sweep deleting a file another wizard run in the same directory is using, and Windows CI flakiness with a pty.

## Plan

Each slice starts with a test that fails for the named reason, then the change, then the test passes.

| PR | Scope | Depends on | Failing test first |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1336 | C1, ledger removal | None | In review |
| #1351 | S1 to S4 and S6, one cancel path | None | In review |
| 1. Exit backstop | `process.on('exit', runCleanups)` installed once at startup. Closes S7, S8, C8 on success, and every E row | None | A registered cleanup runs after a screen's `process.exit(0)`, a thrown error and a normal return. It fails today because nothing drains the list on those exits |
| 2. Abort sequence | The message, stopping the agent first (C11, C12), SIGBREAK (S5) and its exit code. `registerCleanup` returns a remover | #1351 | The message shows and the agent is aborted before the first cleanup runs. It fails today because `wizardCancel` does neither |
| 3. Register every artifact | C3 to C7, C9 and C10 register at creation. Keep Skills unregisters C7 | 1 | Per row: after a success, a throw and an abort, the artifact is gone. It fails today for each row the "Cleaned today" column marks as not covered |
| 4. Startup sweep | Extend `recoverOrphanedSettingsBackups` into one sweep for C1 to C5 and stale C10 dirs. Skip it while another run holds the directory | 3 | Seeded leftovers are gone after startup, and a live run's files survive. It fails today because only settings backups are swept |
| 5. Cross-platform proof | A pty test on `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest` and `windows-latest`. Start a run, press Ctrl-C mid-run, check the message, the exit code, and that no C row remains | 2, 3 | Red on `main` for the message and the leftovers |

The system stays coherent after each slice. Slice 1 alone fixes the most exits. Slice 5 can land its job early as a failing, non-required check if that helps track progress.

No feature flag is proposed. The sweep only deletes wizard-named files, and a CLI release can be reverted.

## Not in scope

- **Uninstalling deliverables.** K1 to K7 stay.
- **POSIX-only shell commands on Windows.** `command -v`, `lsof` and `open || xdg-open` are a separate issue.
- **A manifest of created paths.** Deferred. Revisit if random-named leftovers show up that the sweep can't find by name.
- **A supervisor process to catch SIGKILL.** Rejected. CI kills the whole process tree, and passing the TTY through to Ink costs a lot.

## Open questions

- **Mid-run fixture.** Slice 5 needs a network-free run that reaches the agent. Options are a stub agent behind a dev flag, or the recorded fixtures in `e2e-tests/fixtures` if they can replay a run. That's unverified.
- **Sweep lock.** A pid file in the project, checked with `process.kill(pid, 0)`, would let the sweep skip a live run. It's an artifact too, so it registers and gets swept.
- **Screen Cancel choices.** A Cancel before any run starts exits 0 today. I'd keep it a quiet exit 0 with the backstop, and not show the abort message.
- **Windows CI cancel.** Whether a cancelled GitHub Actions job on Windows sends Ctrl-C or terminates outright isn't verified.

issues.title: Track multi-route AI observability coverage and blocked evaluator recheck
issues.body:
## Status

Parked for now. This tracks the multi-route AI observability reproduction and the blocked before/after evaluation. No further runs are planned until work resumes.

## Reproduction and findings

The [Workbench fixture PR](https://github.com/PostHog/wizard-workbench/pull/4154) exercises six inference route groups: OpenAI-compatible chat, Responses, Ollama chat and generate, direct assistant tool calls, and WebSocket generation. It includes JSON, SSE, NDJSON, provider failures, and cancellation.

- Before guidance changes, the Wizard run took 236.5 seconds and incorrectly captured a successful WebSocket generation as an error without output or tokens.
- After applying [Context Mill #406](https://github.com/PostHog/context-mill/pull/406) and manually supplying the Markdown from [docs #20409](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog.com/pull/20409), the Wizard run took 352.5 seconds. The WebSocket classification improved, but five successful `$ai_output_choices` entries across four route groups still lack `role`. The promised inference coverage ledger/report was not written, and the SSE completion parser remains brittle to valid JSON whitespace.
- Both runs added capture hooks for all six route groups and passed the fixture's five response-contract tests. Those checks do not establish that the emitted AI observability payloads are complete.

The earlier gateway evaluator scored both runs 5/5 despite the remaining payload/report misses. The Workbench PR adds specific rubric criteria and scoring caps; `pnpm test:evaluator` passed 57/57. The live recheck with that rubric did **not** yield a usable after score.

## Evaluation blocker

In the live recheck, the evaluator logged a completed report result (10,784 output tokens), then another success result (28 output tokens). Its loop assigns `resultText = message.result` on each success, so the later result appears to replace the full report. It then retried and failed with `No result received from agent (including retry)`. A model mismatch is possible but unconfirmed; the observed result replacement should be investigated first. This is in the Workbench evaluator (`services/pr-evaluator/evaluator.ts`), not established as the same failure as Wizard's long-running gateway connection issue #581.

## When resumed

1. Preserve the complete evaluator report when subsequent SDK result messages arrive, and rerun the updated rubric against the saved before/after diffs.
2. Verify each successful generation has the required `$ai_output_choices` shape, including `role`, across all six routes; verify SSE variants and the promised coverage ledger/report.
3. Decide whether any remaining misses need Context Mill guidance, docs, or Wizard behavior changes, using the Workbench fixture as the regression case.

issues.title: Remove the keep-skills screen and leave a handoff skill instead
issues.body:
## Problem

At the end of a run, the keep-skills screen asks whether to keep the skills in `.claude/skills`. What it offers to keep is the framework reference skill, for example `integration-javascript_node`. That skill is generic. The agent used it to do this run's work. It is the same for every project on that framework, and it says nothing about what the wizard did in this project.

Saving it is the wrong goal. A later agent in this project does not need a copy of the docs the wizard read. It needs to know where to get PostHog context when it needs it: the PostHog MCP server, and the skills it can pull from there.

This issue first reported that the screen lists and removes wizard skills from earlier runs as if this run installed them. That bug is real, but removing the screen makes it moot. #1338 scoped the list to this run. It fixed the list, not the goal, so it is closed.

## Change

1. **Remove the keep-skills screen.** Drop the `keep-skills` step from every program, and stop promoting the reference skill into `.claude/skills` at run end. The run leaves no generic skill behind.
2. **Leave a handoff skill, with no prompt.** Every run writes one small skill into `.claude/skills`. It tells the next agent in this project:
   - how to reach the PostHog MCP server (`https://mcp.posthog.com/mcp`), and to install it if it is missing
   - where to pull related PostHog skills when it needs deeper context

The handoff skill can be custom packaged by the wizard. It does not have to be a copy of a context-mill skill.

## Open questions

- What goes in the handoff skill beyond the MCP and skills pointers. For example, whether it records what this run set up.
- Whether it is packaged per run or is one fixed skill.
- Its name, and how a re-run replaces it instead of stacking a second copy.
- Whether it stays when the user declines the MCP install step.

## Where this lives

Paths are on main (140af5d1).

- `src/ui/tui/screens/KeepSkillsScreen.tsx`: the screen. `ScreenId.KeepSkills` is at `src/ui/tui/screen-sequences.ts:48`, registered at `src/ui/tui/screen-registry.tsx:149`.
- `src/lib/programs/*/steps.ts`: seven programs have a `keep-skills` step (agent-skill, error-tracking-upload-source-maps, events-audit, migration, posthog-integration, revenue-analytics, warehouse-source). Eight of the nine `test/e2e.json` traces reach a `keep-skills` frame. Self-driving is the one that does not.
- `src/agent/runner/sequence/orchestrator/orchestrator-runner.ts:95`: `promoteReferenceSkill` copies the reference docs into `.claude/skills/<id>`. It is called at line 1324.
- `src/agent/runner/sequence/orchestrator/orchestrator-runner.ts:117`: `sweepRunInstalledSkills` spares the reference skill. Once nothing promotes it, the sweep can drop that exception.
- `src/lib/programs/self-driving/index.ts`: self-driving already has no keep-skills step. Its `postRun` removes its setup skill. That is the precedent for the other programs.
- Tests that reach the screen: `src/ui/tui/__tests__/router.test.ts:51`, `store.test.ts`, `keyboard-equivalence.test.tsx:222`, `frames.test.tsx:507`, `src/lib/programs/__tests__/flow-traces.test.ts:155`, and the `keep-skills-*.txt` frame snapshots.

issues.title: Real-TUI snapshot runs hang on a failed run, mislabel frames, and never fail on a missing report or a host exit code
issues.body:
## Problem

The snapshot route, where `scripts/tui-snapshots.no-jest.ts` drives `scripts/tui-host.no-jest.ts` in a PTY, has seven gaps. A failed run sits until the outer timeout. Some frames get the wrong label, and some show a blank screen. `result.json` can leave off the end of the flow. A missing report, or a host crash, still exits 0. The profile's `skills: "delete"` deletes nothing.

- [ ] **The timeout kill does not reach the host.** node-pty starts the host in a new session. It uses `POSIX_SPAWN_SETSID` on macOS and `forkpty` on Linux. A process-group kill of the driver therefore never signals the host. `tui-snapshots` installs no signal handler and never calls `cap.kill()`. Cleanup depends on the SIGHUP from the PTY hangup, and any descendant that survives SIGHUP is left running.
- [ ] **A fast screen gets the next screen's label.** `snap()` adds the screen to `screenPath` when it is called. It then sleeps 500 ms and writes `store.currentScreen` as the frame label. If the screen changed during that sleep, the frame shows the next screen and carries its name, so the first screen has no frame. With CI-mode auth this happened to `auth` on every B2 run, and on 3 of 9 Release A runs.
- [ ] **A failed run waits on the mint-failure screen until the timeout.** `decideE2eAction` has no case for `mint-failure` ("The Wizard's a little busy"). It returns `{ wait: true }`, and the driver waits in 600 s turns until the outer timeout kills it. The action registry already has `dismiss_outro` for this screen. Choosing it is not enough on its own: `ExitScreen` does not exit while `mintHandoff` is set, because `run-wizard` normally does that exit, and the host does not use `run-wizard`.
- [ ] **`result.json` stops at `outro`.** The `outro` subscription writes the result and sets `resultWritten`, so the final write after keep-skills returns early. For every program whose outro screen id is `outro`, `screenPath` ends at `outro` and `skillsComplete` is false, even when mcp, slack-connect and keep-skills ran. #1308 fixes this on the stack, but main still has the bug.
- [ ] **No check reads the report outcome or the host's exit code.** `result.json` includes `reportFile.exists`, but no code in this repo reads it. It also does not record whether the agent published a handoff, which is the report channel the `publish_handoff` description now asks for (#1141). `TuiCapture.exited` also drops the host's exit code, and `tui-snapshots` then always exits 0.
- [ ] **The capture can run after the driver has acted.** The host keeps the screen for 300 ms after it writes the label. The capturer polls every 150 ms and then waits 200 ms before it reads, so the read can come up to 350 ms after the label. `term.write(d)` is asynchronous, and `frameAnsi()` does not wait for pending writes to finish. When the machine is loaded, the timers slip further.
- [ ] **`skills: "delete"` deletes nothing.** Every `test/e2e.json` sets it, but the keep-skills action only records `kept: false` in the store. No harness run exercises Remove, and runs leave their skills in the app directory.

## Evidence

The sweep ran all nine programs through `tui-snapshots.no-jest.ts` on the refactor stack's B2 head, d938a43b (#1307): nine runs in parallel, then a sequential rerun of source-maps and self-driving. It also ran on the Release A top, 200961f8. Apart from import paths, the harness files match main, so the line numbers below are for main (d8486dc1).

**1. Timeout kill**

- `e2e-harness/tui-capture.ts:108` starts the host with `pty.spawn`.
- `scripts/tui-snapshots.no-jest.ts:29-61` installs no signal handler and exits only after the child exits (`:55-61`). Nothing calls `cap.kill()` (`e2e-harness/tui-capture.ts:155-161`).
- I reproduced this locally in the sweep driver's shape: `Popen(start_new_session=True)`, then `killpg(SIGTERM)`. The host's session and group id did not match the driver's group. In that minimal case the PTY hangup still ended the host and a plain grandchild. A process is left behind only when a descendant outlives SIGHUP.

**2. Labels**

- `scripts/tui-host.no-jest.ts:471-472` adds `screen` to `screenPath`. Lines `:474-475` sleep 500 ms and then append `store.currentScreen` to the control file.
- On B2, all nine `screenPath`s list `auth`, but none of the nine runs has an `auth` frame. In posthog-integration, frame 02 is labelled `run` and shows the run screen with "Using provided API key (CI mode - OAuth bypassed)".
- On the Release A top, auth was slower, and 6 of the 9 runs have an auth frame.

**3. Mint failure**

- `e2e-harness/e2e-profile.ts:322-325` handles the outro screens. There is no case for `ScreenId.MintFailure`, so it falls to `:389-390` and returns `{ wait: true }`.
- `scripts/tui-host.no-jest.ts:619` waits up to 600 s per turn.
- `e2e-harness/action-registry.ts:220-231` already defines `continue_setup` and `dismiss_outro` for mint-failure.
- `src/ui/tui/screens/ExitScreen.tsx:14` exits only when `mintHandoff` is unset. Otherwise `src/lib/runners/run-wizard.ts:284-297` does the exit.
- In an earlier sweep of the C stack, replay-vision (`replay-vision/react-vite`) reached mint-failure at frame 04. It captured frames 04 to 08 and then waited until the 2400 s timeout.

**4. `result.json` tail**

- The guard is at `scripts/tui-host.no-jest.ts:631-632`, the `outro` write at `:703-705`, and the final write at `:720`. The final write returns early. The comment at `:624-629` says integration rewrites the result after keep-skills. The guard came in with #1152, and the `outro` write came in with 6f0c7317 (#1151).
- On B2, posthog-integration captured frames 28-mcp, 29-slack-connect and 30-keep-skills. Its `result.json` still has `screenPath` intro → auth → run → outro and `skillsComplete: false`. Metrics, error-tracking, ai-observability, replay-vision and warehouse-source show the same pattern: the last frame is keep-skills, but `screenPath` ends at outro. Audit and source-maps have their own outro screen ids, so the bug does not affect them.
- The workbench `wizard-ci --e2e` checks "full interactive flow reached keep-skills" and "skillsComplete" read these fields (PostHog/wizard-workbench `services/wizard-ci/e2e.ts:470-471`).
- The #1308 head, 17c02e46, adds `createE2eResultWriter` to `e2e-harness/e2e-result.ts` and calls `writeResult(true)` in the host.

**5. Missing report and exit code**

- `e2e-harness/e2e-result.ts:170-193` defines `readReportFile`, and `scripts/tui-host.no-jest.ts:696` stores its result. No code in the repo reads the field.
- On B2, metrics (`posthog-metrics-report.md`), audit (`posthog-audit-report.md`) and warehouse-source (`posthog-warehouse-report.md`) all have `reportFile.exists: false`. All three still have `runPhase: completed` and exit 0. The files are also absent from the app copies.
- The workbench's "report written" check (`services/wizard-ci/warehouse-checks.ts:806-831`) runs only for apps that have `apps/<app>/.wizard-ci/expect.json`. `revenue/stripe/stripe-saas-demo` has no such file. Where it does run, it passes only when the file exists (`:813-820`).
- A missing file is not always a failed run on main. The `publish_handoff` description says "do not write the report to a file yourself" (`src/agent/tools/handoff.ts:33`), while `skillPrompt` still asks for the file (`src/agent/agent-prompt.ts:54`). In the B2 audit and warehouse runs the agent published the handoff and wrote no file. So a check on `reportFile.exists` alone would fail runs that followed the tool description. The report-file issue covers picking one channel.
- `e2e-harness/tui-capture.ts:121-123` resolves `exited` without the exit code, and `scripts/tui-snapshots.no-jest.ts:60` exits 0. The workbench pass condition includes `run.status === 0` (`e2e.ts:399`), so it never sees a host failure.

**6. Capture race**

- `scripts/tui-host.no-jest.ts:476` keeps the screen for 300 ms after the label is written. `scripts/tui-snapshots.no-jest.ts:54` polls every 150 ms, and `:45` waits 200 ms before it calls `frameAnsi()`.
- `e2e-harness/tui-capture.ts:118` calls `term.write(d)` with no callback. `frameAnsi()` (`:136-151`) reads the buffer in whatever state it is in.
- On B2 with nine parallel runs, source-maps frame 31 (wizard-ask) shows only the header and the "↑↓ navigate  enter select" footer. In the sequential rerun, the same frame shows the full test-affordance question.
- On the Release A top, self-driving frames 55 and 61 (wizard-ask) are blank in the parallel sweep and complete in a solo rerun (frames 64 and 70).
- On B2, self-driving frames 58 and 64 are blank, and they were still blank in the sequential rerun (frames 63 and 69). Load is not the only cause.

**7. `skills: "delete"`**

- `e2e-harness/e2e-profile.ts:343-351`: the keep-skills decision returns `kept: profile.skills === 'keep'` and `skillsPolicy`. The comment at `:149` says "the orchestrator does the fs deletion", and the doc comment at `:265` says the caller "handles `skillsPolicy` itself".
- `e2e-harness/action-registry.ts:326-330`: `keep_skills` only calls `store.setSkillsComplete(...)`.
- Nothing in the repo reads `skillsPolicy`. `E2E_KEEP_SKILLS`, which PostHog/wizard-workbench `services/wizard-ci/e2e.ts:300` sets, is not read either.
- `e2e-harness/ARCHITECTURE.md:92-94` says keep-skills outcomes only commit store state. So "delete" in every `test/e2e.json` is a label that nothing acts on.
- The keep-skills screen issue shows the effect on the product side: a run's skills stay in the directory, and a later run lists them as its own.

## Suggested fix

1. In `tui-snapshots`, handle SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP. Send SIGTERM to the PTY child's process group, send SIGKILL after a grace period, then exit. Expose `pid` on `TuiCapture` so this is possible. Add a wall-clock deadline in the harness so a stuck run does not rely on the outer driver.
2. Label each frame with the screen that `snap()` recorded. If the screen changed before the capture, write a marker such as `NN-auth.missed`, so that `screenPath` and the frames agree. A better option is for the capturer to wait until the output goes quiet, instead of sleeping a fixed time.
3. In `decideE2eAction`, add `case ScreenId.MintFailure: return { action: { id: 'dismiss_outro' }, done: true }`. The host then writes the result and exits 1 when `mintHandoff === 'exit'`. #1278 made the profile change on a route that was later closed.
4. Land `createE2eResultWriter` from #1308, or cherry-pick it to main.
5. Record the handoff in `result.json` (for example `handoff: { published, chars }` from the store's `handoffText`). Declare the expected report channel in each program's `test/e2e.json`, and exit non-zero when neither the handoff nor the named file exists. Once the product keeps one channel, check only that one. Pass the host's exit code through `TuiCapture.exited` and use it as the exit code of `tui-snapshots`. The e2e-key issue adds a scope-blocked result on top of this.
6. Replace the timed handshake with an acknowledgement. The capturer writes the frame and then appends an ack, and the host waits for the ack before it acts. Use `term.write(d, cb)` and capture only after all pending writes have finished.
7. Make `skills: "delete"` do something, or remove it. Either move the removal into a shared function that `KeepSkillsScreen`'s `handleRemove` and the `keep_skills` action both call when `kept` is false, or delete `skillsPolicy`, the profile field and the `E2E_KEEP_SKILLS` env, and say the profile only records the choice.

issues.title: Success outro claims all changes even when some steps didn't complete
issues.body:
The success outro always shows the framework's full static "What the agent did" list. There is no partial state — a run where a step didn't complete still renders every claimed change under "Successfully installed PostHog!".

Seen in a Flutter run (#942): the agent couldn't install the SDK, said so in its setup report, and left its "Install SDK" task pending — the outro still claimed the SDK was added.

The outro is the wizard's last word, so overstating it undermines the "please review the changes" note right below. The run's task statuses already exist in the store; the outro could reflect them instead of static copy.

issues.title: Outro names a report file the agent was told not to write
issues.body:
## Problem

Main now has part of the "report goes through `publish_handoff`" change, and the outros point at files that do not exist.

#1141 (merged 2026-08-27) added this clause to the `publish_handoff` description: "do not write the report to a file yourself". It is at `src/agent/tools/handoff.ts:30-33` on main (d8486dc1), and the pi tool uses the same text. The rest of the code still asks for the file or says it exists:

- `skillPrompt` still says "write a brief markdown report to ./${reportFile}" (`src/agent/agent-prompt.ts:54`). Every program with a `skillId` gets this line.
- The context-mill skills still say to write it. `context/skills/data-warehouse-source/description.md:99` says "write the report file requested by the wizard". `context/skills/audit/references/6-report.md:7` and `:52` say to `Write` `posthog-audit-report.md` to disk. context-mill#306 moves these skills to `publish_handoff`. It is still a draft.
- The outros show the file name and never check the file exists. `src/agent/runner/sequence/linear.ts:294-300` passes `run.reportFile` through. `src/ui/tui/screens/OutroScreen.tsx:87-93` prints "Check ./… for details", and `src/ui/tui/exit-line.ts:91-92` adds the same line on exit. `src/ui/tui/screens/audit/AuditOutroScreen.tsx:64-76` prints "Report saved to:". The audit success message at `src/lib/programs/audit/index.ts:48`, the ledger row label at `src/lib/programs/audit/seed.ts:99-103` and the "Write report" slide at `src/ui/tui/screens/audit/slides/writeReport.tsx:25` also name the file.
- On main, `publish_handoff` writes a file only when the host sets `POSTHOG_HANDOFF_OUTPUT_PATH`. The TUI does not set it, so nothing is written to the project.
- The wizard-workbench warehouse grader also expects the file. Its "report written" check passes only when `result.reportFile.exists` is true (PostHog/wizard-workbench `services/wizard-ci/warehouse-checks.ts:813-820`), so a run that follows the tool description fails it.

## Evidence

Each run follows one instruction or the other. We saw this in a real-TUI sweep of all nine programs on the refactor stack head d938a43b (#1307), which has the same code for this path as main:

- warehouse (`revenue/stripe/stripe-saas-demo`): the agent called only `publish_handoff` and marked "Write setup report" completed. The outro says "Check ./posthog-warehouse-report.md for details". No file was written.
- audit (`audit/posthog-demo-3000`): the agent resolved `write-report` as pass: "Final markdown report delivered through the wizard handoff." The outro says "Report saved to: <installDir>/posthog-audit-report.md". No file was written. The Release A top (200961f8) did the same.
- metrics (`express-todo`, orchestrator flow): the report went only to a notebook. The orchestrator outro does not name a file, so it shows nothing false.
- ai-observability wrote its file and also called `publish_handoff`. On 200961f8, warehouse wrote its file too. The result depends on which instruction the model follows.

The stack carries the same lines at other positions (`src/agent/agent-prompt.ts:54`, `src/agent/tools/handoff.ts:33`, `src/agent/runner/sequence/linear.ts:314`, `src/ui/tui/screens/OutroScreen.tsx:107`, `src/ui/tui/screens/audit/AuditOutroScreen.tsx:67`, `src/programs/resolve-run-definition.ts:56`), so this is not a stack regression.

## Prior work

#1047 (open draft, last updated 2026-07-31, conflicting) makes `publish_handoff` the only report channel. It changes `skillPrompt`, stops programs naming a `.md` file, and shows the file in the outro only when one was written. context-mill#306 is its skill-side pair. Both are stale, and #1047 predates #1141, so it does not describe the contradiction main has now. Its base is ce8b70d3, and the files have moved since: `src/lib/agent` is now `src/agent`, and `src/lib/wizard-tools` is now `src/agent/tools`.

#811 (open draft, stale since 2026-07-06) gates the linear-runner outro on the file existing. It is on old paths and does not cover the audit success message or screen.

## Suggested fix

1. Now: pick one instruction. Either drop "do not write the report to a file yourself" from `PUBLISH_HANDOFF_DESCRIPTION` until the rest moves, or change `skillPrompt` to order a `publish_handoff` call and stop naming the file.
2. Until one channel remains, show a report path only when that file exists in `installDir`. #811 did this for the linear runner. The same check needs to cover the audit outro screen, the audit success message and the exit line.
3. Longer term: land #1047 and context-mill#306 together, or close them and do the same change on the current paths. Update the workbench "report written" check to accept the published handoff when the program no longer names a file.

issues.title: Node default integration adds a full OpenTelemetry NodeSDK for logs and leaves no posthog-node shutdown
issues.body:
## Problem

Since context-mill v1.55.0 (#390), a default integration run always queues a Logs task. On a small Express todo API, that task added five `@opentelemetry` packages and a new `posthog-logs.js`. It also added a `posthogLogs.info()` call after every `posthog.capture()`. The file starts a full `NodeSDK` from `@opentelemetry/sdk-node` just to export logs.

`NodeSDK` does more than logs. With only `logRecordProcessors` set, it also registers a global tracer provider and a meter provider. Both get OTLP exporters built from `OTEL_*` environment defaults. They do nothing today. But they pull in about 30 `@opentelemetry` packages (about 35 MB) plus `@grpc`. Any span or metric the app adds later goes to the default OTLP endpoint, not to PostHog. This is too much for a todo API that did not ask for logs.

The same run added no graceful shutdown. Nothing calls `posthog.shutdown()` on SIGINT or SIGTERM. `posthog-node` and the OTel `BatchLogRecordProcessor` both buffer, so events and log records queued at stop time are lost. The Logs task did write an exported shutdown helper. The review task then deleted it under its "Minimal" rule, because nothing called it. The posthog-node client never got a shutdown path.

An earlier run of the same program on the same app, on context-mill v1.54.1 before #390, added `server.close()` and `await posthog.shutdown()` on SIGINT and SIGTERM. This is one run per version, so it shows the guidance allows both results. It does not prove a regression.

## Evidence

Sweep: the `posthog-integration` program on `basic-integration/javascript-node/express-todo`, pi harness, orchestrator sequence. Wizard build 2.76.1, at the refactor stack's B2 head d938a43b (PostHog/wizard#1307). Skills came from context-mill `releases/latest`, which was v1.55.0. `logs-nodejs` came from `releases/download/v1.55.0/logs-nodejs.zip`.

- Plan: 10 tasks. "Configure log capture" completed. "Assess AI observability" was skipped. The seed queued the Logs task with the reason "Log capture follows AI instrumentation to preserve any tracing configuration it adds."
- `package.json` gained `@opentelemetry/api-logs`, `@opentelemetry/exporter-logs-otlp-http`, `@opentelemetry/resources`, `@opentelemetry/sdk-logs`, and `@opentelemetry/sdk-node` (all 0.222.x or 2.11.x). The other new dependencies were `posthog-node` and `dotenv`.
- `posthog-logs.js` builds `new NodeSDK({ resource, logRecordProcessors: [new BatchLogRecordProcessor(new OTLPLogExporter(...))] })` and calls `sdk.start()`. It has no shutdown.
- `index.js` has four `posthog.capture()` calls. Each one is followed by a `posthogLogs.info()` call with the same facts. `index.js` and `posthog.js` never call `posthog.shutdown()` or `posthog.flush()`, and they register no signal handlers.
- Review status line in the wizard log: "The minimality review found one unused exported shutdown helper; removing it". The edit that follows removes `async function ...` and `let sdk;` from `posthog-logs.js`.
- Installed `@opentelemetry/sdk-node` 0.222.0: `build/src/sdk.js:28-33` and `:146-149` build OTLP metric readers from env when none are passed. `build/src/utils.js:83-89` builds an OTLP trace exporter when `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` is empty. `build/src/sdk.js:214-229` registers the global tracer provider.
- Comparison run: the same program and app on the Release A top, 200961f8 (PostHog/wizard#1303), with context-mill v1.54.1. That run had no Logs task, and its `index.js` added a `shutdown()` that closes the server and awaits `posthog.shutdown()` on SIGINT and SIGTERM.

Where it lives. The wizard gets these prompts at runtime from context-mill `releases/latest`, so this happens on wizard main too. It does not depend on the refactor stack. On main, the only wizard-side control is the kill switch: `src/lib/programs/posthog-integration/index.ts:255-258` (`excludedTaskTypes`) and `src/shared/constants.ts:310` (`wizard-default-aio-logs`). An explicit `'false'` drops the task for everyone. The fix belongs in PostHog/context-mill, and the Node setup code comes from the posthog.com Node logs page. Paths are on context-mill main, dc2898b (v1.55.0):

- `context/agents/integration-v2/integrate-posthog.md:29-34` queues `logs` on every default run: "Queue it even when AIO will be skipped."
- `context/agents/integration-v2/logs.md:18-26` says to use "the documented OTLP exporter" for the platform. It gives no rule for when an app needs logs, and nothing stops a log line from repeating every capture.
- `context/skills/logs/config.yaml:26-30` builds `logs-nodejs` from `https://posthog.com/docs/logs/installation/nodejs.md`. That page uses `NodeSDK` and shows no shutdown.
- `context/agents/integration-v2/review.md:58-60`: "Delete helpers nothing calls" removed the only shutdown code in the run.
- `context/commandments.yaml:65` (`javascript_node`): "await flush() or await shutdown() before letting that process exit". A long-running server with no exit path can read this as not applying. In `context/skills/posthog-best-practices/description.md`, the long-running server rule at `:125` does not mention shutdown, and `:130` asks for `shutdown()` only in short-lived processes. The Rust rule at `context/commandments.yaml:97` (#354) already closes this gap for Rust: "An app with no shutdown path still needs this".
- `context/agents/integration-v2/init.md` has no shutdown requirement.

## Suggested fix

1. Offer logs only when the app needs them. Queue or run the Logs task when the app already has a logger (pino, winston, bunyan, or structured `console` use at request boundaries), or when the user asks. Otherwise, complete it as `not needed` and put one line in the report about how to add logs later. In `logs.md`, say that a log line must not repeat a `capture()` call.
2. For plain Node, use a `LoggerProvider` from `@opentelemetry/sdk-logs` with `BatchLogRecordProcessor` and `OTLPLogExporter`, and register it with `logs.setGlobalLoggerProvider`. Do not use `@opentelemetry/sdk-node`. Use `NodeSDK` only when the app already runs one, and then attach to it. Add this as a `logs-nodejs` commandment or override in context-mill, and fix the posthog.com Node logs page to match.
3. Always flush on shutdown for long-running Node servers. Change the `javascript_node` commandment to match the Rust wording: register SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers that close the server and await `posthog.shutdown()`, even when the app has no shutdown path. When logs are set up, the same handler also awaits the logger provider's `shutdown()`. Make `init.md` own this. In `review.md`, say that shutdown and flush wiring is never an unused helper: the fix is to wire it, not to delete it.

issues.title: Snapshot sweep passes warehouse-source, replay-vision, self-driving and audit Live Data without running them, because the e2e key lacks their scopes
issues.body:
## Problem

The real-TUI snapshot sweep runs each program with one PostHog personal API key. That key does not carry the scopes several programs need. The PostHog MCP hides or rejects the gated tools. The agent then records a blocker, skips the task, or marks a check as a suggestion. The run still exits 0 with `runPhase: completed`, so the sweep reports a pass.

The result is that these paths have no end-to-end coverage today:

- warehouse-source never creates a source. It needs `external_data_source:read` and `external_data_source:write`.
- replay-vision never enables replay or creates a scanner. It needs `product_enablement:write`, `replay_scanner:read` and `replay_scanner:write`.
- self-driving never enables Support or creates a scanner. It needs the same three scopes.
- audit never reads live health findings. It needs `health_issue:read`, which is already in the documented base set.

Nothing in the harness notices this. In CI mode the wizard sets `missingScopes` to an empty list, because a personal API key has no requested scope set to diff against. The scope-aware degrade and the error copy that name a missing permission never fire in e2e.

The docs do not help either. The README lists the base set plus the integration additions. It does not list what replay-vision or self-driving add. The harness docs name the key variables but no scopes.

This issue is about coverage and the key. Two related problems are tracked apart: the outros that still say success when a scope blocked the work (a comment on #951), and the harness never failing a run on a missing report or a host exit code (the snapshot-harness issue). Fix 3 below is the scope-specific part of the second.

## Evidence

Sweep on the refactor stack head d938a43b (PostHog/wizard#1307), with the key read through `POSTHOG_KEY_FILE` against the sweep's US test project. The sweep of the Release A top 200961f8 (#1303) shows the same results, and its notes say main behaves the same.

- warehouse-source, app `revenue/stripe/stripe-saas-demo`. Frame 12 says "MCP source creation is unavailable under the active connection's scopes." The task list ends with "Record blocker" completed. The outro frame still says "Data warehouse source connected!" The Release A run's report says it created 0 of 1 detected sources because `external_data_source:read` and `external_data_source:write` were missing. Exit 0.
- replay-vision, app `replay-vision/react-vite/court-booking`. The report says `products-enable` was rejected for lack of `product_enablement:write`. It also says the connection has no `replay_scanner:read` or `replay_scanner:write`, so the scanner list, estimate, quota and create tools were unreachable. All three scanner tasks are `skipped`. The outro reads "4/4 steps completed (3 skipped as not required)." Exit 0.
- self-driving, app `self-driving/react-router/expense-splitter`. All nine tasks read `completed`. The report says Support could not be enabled without `product_enablement:write`, and both Replay Vision monitors were skipped without `replay_scanner:read` and `replay_scanner:write`. Exit 0.
- audit, app `audit/posthog-demo-3000`. The `live-data-findings` check in `.posthog-audit-checks.json` has status `suggestion` and says: "Skipped: health-issues-list requires the health_issue:read scope." Exit 0.

The code is the same on main (d8486dc1):

- `src/shared/utils/setup-utils.ts:448` takes the CI api-key path. Lines 500-502 return `missingScopes: []`.
- `src/shared/constants.ts:283-289` defines `WIZARD_OAUTH_SCOPES`. Line 285 is `health_issue:read`.
- `src/lib/oauth/program-scopes.ts:180-196` (`SELF_DRIVING_SCOPE_ADDITIONS`), `:206-209` (`WAREHOUSE_SOURCE_SCOPE_ADDITIONS`) and `:246-251` (`REPLAY_VISION_SCOPE_ADDITIONS`) list what each program needs. `:264` maps them per program, and `:296` `getOAuthScopesForProgram` resolves the union for one program.
- `README.md:263-278` ("Required API Key Scopes") lists the base set and only the integration additions.
- `scripts/tui-host.no-jest.ts:194-198` reads the key, and `:227` builds the session with `ci: true`. `e2e-harness/ARCHITECTURE.md:46-48` and `scripts/README.md` name the key variables but no scopes.
- `src/lib/programs/replay-vision/test/e2e.json` describes the happy path as enabling replay and creating three scanners, and `warehouse-source/test/e2e.json` as creating in-cli sources over the PostHog MCP. The sweep reaches neither.

The key is not in any repo. The same kind of key is stored as the `GH_APP_POSTHOG_WIZARD_CI_BOT_POSTHOG_PERSONAL_KEY` secret, used by `.github/workflows/smoke-test.yml` here and by `.github/workflows/wizard-ci.yml` in PostHog/wizard-workbench. This sweep did not check whether that secret has the same scopes.

## Suggested fix

1. Document the scopes the e2e key needs for each program. Generate the list from `getOAuthScopesForProgram` for every program id, so it cannot drift from `PROGRAM_SCOPE_ADDITIONS`. Put the union in the README "Required API Key Scopes" section and link it from `e2e-harness/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `scripts/README.md`.
2. Issue a new CI bot key with that union. Rotate `GH_APP_POSTHOG_WIZARD_CI_BOT_POSTHOG_PERSONAL_KEY` in both repos and replace the local key file the sweep uses.
3. Make the harness flag steps blocked by a scope. Before the run, `tui-host` should compare what the key can do with `getOAuthScopesForProgram(programId)`. Read the key's scopes if PostHog exposes them. If not, check that the MCP tool list served to the key includes the tools the program needs. Put the gap in the `E2E_RESULT_JSON` payload as `missingScopes`, and make the sweep report the program as scope-blocked, not passed. The same diff can fill `credentials.missingScopes` on the CI path, so CI runs get the missing-permission error copy that OAuth runs already get.

issues.title: Audit runs can leave .posthog-audit-checks.json in the user's project
issues.body:
## Problem

The wizard writes `.posthog-audit-checks.json` into the project root before the audit agent starts. No wizard code deletes it. The audit skills end with an instruction for the agent to run `rm -f .posthog-audit-checks.json`. The file is removed only if the agent runs that last step.

When the agent skips the step, the run still completes and the user keeps an untracked JSON file in their repo root, next to their own code. The next run does not break: the watcher ignores a leftover ledger and the seed replaces it. But the file is clutter, and a user can commit it by accident.

There is a second, smaller problem in the same path. On pi, a scoped `rm` of that file is logged as `Denying bash command (not in allowlist)` and captured as a `bash denied` event. Then the scoped-rm rule from #834 lets it run. The log and the telemetry say "denied". The command ran.

## Evidence

Real-TUI sweep of the `audit` program on the wizard-workbench app `audit/posthog-demo-3000`. Harness pi (binding), sequence linear, model `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`.

- Refactor stack B2 head `d938a43b` (#1307). The agent read step 6, uploaded the notebook, resolved `write-report` and `upload-notebook`, and published the handoff. It never ran the `rm`. After exit, `.posthog-audit-checks.json` (3929 bytes) was still in the project root.
- Release A top `200961f8` (#1303). The agent ran `rm -f .posthog-audit-checks.json` and the file was removed. The wizard log shows the misleading pair:
  ```
  [pi] → bash {"command":"rm -f .posthog-audit-checks.json"}
  Denying bash command (not in allowlist): rm -f .posthog-audit-checks.json
  [pi] ← bash: {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"(no output)"}]}
  ```

The same prompt, harness and model gave both outcomes. The cleanup depends on the agent.

Code on main (`d8486dc1`):

- `src/lib/programs/audit/seed.ts:118-124`: `seedAuditLedger` writes the ledger. `src/lib/programs/audit/index.ts:26-29` and `:58` call it before the agent starts. The wizard creates the file.
- `src/lib/programs/run-agent-legacy.ts:81-95`: `runProgramAgent` starts the ledger watcher and stops it in `finally`. Nothing removes the file.
- `src/lib/programs/audit/ledger-watcher.ts:32`: "A ledger an earlier run left behind stays ignored until this run writes." The code already expects leftovers.
- `src/lib/runners/run-wizard.ts:223`: the task stream reads the checks from the session (`getAuditChecks(session)`), not from the file. Nothing reads the file after the run.
- `src/agent/runner/harness/pi/index.ts:741-749`: pi deletes `.posthog-events.json` host-side after the run. There is no matching cleanup for the audit ledger.
- `src/agent/runner/harness/pi/runtime-notes.ts:53`: pi still tells the agent that `bash` is only for install, build, typecheck, lint and format commands. #894 names this line as the reason agents skip `rm`. #1000 would update it.
- `src/agent/runner/harness/pi/security.ts:372-385`: `evaluateToolCall` calls `wizardCanUseTool` first and applies `isScopedFileRemoval` after.
- `src/agent/agent-interface.ts:523-528`: `wizardCanUseTool` logs `Denying bash command` and captures `bash denied` before it returns the deny that pi then overrides.

Skill side, context-mill main:

- `context/skills/audit/description.md:49` and `context/skills/audit/references/6-report.md:284` tell the agent to delete the ledger.
- The same step is in the six `audit-*` leaf skills, for example `context/skills/audit-events/references/4-report.md:21`, and in `context/skills/events-audit/references/6-dashboard.md:270`.
- context-mill#306 (open) moves reports to `publish_handoff` and keeps the agent-driven delete.

The refactor stack has the same behavior. On `d938a43b`, `src/programs/program-file-watchers.ts:16-58` owns the ledger for the run, but `stop()` only stops the watcher (`src/programs/run-program.ts:706-708`).

Prior work. #833 added a host-side `cleanupArtifacts` seam for `.posthog-events.json`. It was closed because it worked around pi blocking `rm`, and #834 fixed that instead. This case is different. `rm` works here, and the agent did not run it. The wizard also seeds this file, so the program is the file's owner. #898 and #901 fixed the misleading deny log and telemetry. Both were closed without merging, and main still has the old order. #612 (open) raises the same class of leak for `/tmp` scratch files that skills name themselves, and leans toward a skill-side fix because the wizard does not know those names. That concern does not apply here: the program declares the name in `auditLedgerFile`, so the wizard can delete it without learning skill filenames. #894 (open) would make the agent more likely to run the `rm`, but cleanup would still depend on the agent.

## Suggested fix

1. Delete the ledger in the wizard after the agent run settles, on every exit path. On main, remove `path.join(session.installDir, programConfig.auditLedgerFile)` with `force: true` after `ledger.stop()` in the `finally` of `runProgramAgent`, and in the `registerCleanup` callback so aborts clean up too. On the stack, do it in `startProgramFileWatchers().stop()` or next to it in the `run-program.ts` `finally`. This covers `audit`, `events-audit` and the family leaves, because they all set `auditLedgerFile`.
2. In context-mill, remove the "delete `.posthog-audit-checks.json`" step from the audit skills, or mark it optional, once the wizard deletes the file. Then the skill and the wizard do not both own the file.
3. In `evaluateToolCall`, decide the scoped-rm rule before the deny is logged and captured. Keep the `disallowedTools` check. Log an allow line for the command that runs, and do not capture `bash denied` for it. #898 has a small version of this change.

issues.title: ai-observability on an openai v4 Node app ends with an unsupported or duplicate OpenAI SDK, and the outcome differs per run
issues.body:
## Problem

`wizard ai-observability` does not handle a Node app pinned to `openai` v4. The current `@posthog/ai` (8.13.1) declares `openai ^6.48.0` as an optional peer dependency. npm still checks an optional peer when the package is present, so installing `@posthog/ai` next to `openai ^4.77.0` fails with `ERESOLVE`.

Nothing tells the agent what to do next, so it improvises. Two sweep runs on the same fixture ended in two different states:

- One run installed `@posthog/ai@^8.13.1` past the conflict. The lockfile shows `@posthog/ai` 8.13.1 next to the root `openai` 4.104.0, which npm only allows with `--legacy-peer-deps` or `--force`. The wrapper then extends an OpenAI SDK major it does not support. The report says so, but calls the setup done.
- The other run pinned `@posthog/ai@^6.4.3`. Before 8.0, `@posthog/ai` has `openai` as a hard dependency (`^5.20.1` in 6.4.3). npm nests `openai` 5.23.2 under `@posthog/ai`. The wrapped client runs OpenAI SDK v5, and the app's own fallback client runs v4. The lockfile grows from 73 packages (8.13.1 run) to 162, because 6.4.3 also brings in `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@google/genai`, `ai` and `langchain` as hard dependencies. The report says the wrapper "installs alongside the unchanged root OpenAI v4 SDK". That is true of the manifest but not of what the wrapped calls run.

Both runs pass `npm run build` and report success. The skill's "Do not upgrade the vendor SDK" rule is kept in the manifest and broken at runtime in the second run.

The instructions also disagree about installing at all. The skill says to declare packages and not run the package manager. The wizard's program prompt and the pi harness tell the agent to run the install. The agent follows the wizard, hits `ERESOLVE`, and has no rule for it.

## Evidence

Sweep program `ai-observability`, fixture `ai-observability/openai/node-weather` (wizard-workbench `04f55e0a9`, `apps/ai-observability/openai/node-weather/package.json:12`, `"openai": "^4.77.0"`, no lockfile).

- Release A top, 200961f8 (#1303): manifest ends with `@posthog/ai ^8.13.1`, `openai ^4.77.0`. Lockfile: 73 packages, `node_modules/@posthog/ai` 8.13.1 with peer `openai ^6.48.0` (optional), `node_modules/openai` 4.104.0. Frames 15 and 16 show "Resolving the wrapper's peer-dependency constraint without changing the existing OpenAI SDK version."
- B2 head, d938a43b (#1307): manifest ends with `@posthog/ai ^6.4.3`, `openai ^4.77.0`. Lockfile: 162 packages, `node_modules/@posthog/ai` 6.4.3 depending on `openai ^5.20.1`, `node_modules/@posthog/ai/node_modules/openai` 5.23.2, `node_modules/openai` 4.104.0, plus `@langchain/openai` with its own `openai` 5.12.2. `src/index.ts` builds the wrapped client from `@posthog/ai/openai` and a fallback client from `openai`. Frames 15 to 17 show "The current OpenAI dependency conflicts with the wrapper's required peer version, so configuration can proceed while compatibility remains unresolved." The agent added a "Resolve SDK compatibility" task and marked it completed.

The Release A run installed `ai-observability-openai-node` 1.54.1, and the B2 run installed 1.55.0. `references/2-install.md` did not change between v1.54.1 and v1.55.0, and it matches context-mill main. The wizard lines below are the same on the stack. So the install rule was the same in both runs, and this is not stack-only.

Skill, context-mill `dc2898b`:
- `context/skills/ai-observability/references/2-install.md:7`: "Declare the packages in the project manifest. Do not run the package manager."
- `2-install.md:22` and `:46`: do not add or upgrade the vendor SDK.
- `2-install.md:24`: the pinned-major rule covers only pre-1.0 Python `openai`. It ends with "The same holds for any provider pinned below its current client interface", which the agent did not apply to `openai` v4 on Node.
- `2-install.md:44`: "Do not run `npm install` or `pip install`."
- `4-verify.md:33`: the import check passes in both runs, so it does not catch a mismatched SDK major.
- Compare `context/agents/integration-v2/install.md:38`, which names a pre-existing `ERESOLVE` as an environment failure with a defined fallback. The ai-observability skill has no such rule.

Wizard main, `d8486dc1`:
- `src/lib/programs/ai-observability/index.ts:51-53`: "The skill itself will install packages".
- `src/agent/runner/harness/pi/tools.ts:390`: `detect_package_manager` says to run the returned install command via bash.
- `src/agent/runner/harness/pi/runtime-notes.ts:53`: "Run installs synchronously and wait (e.g. `npm install <pkg>`)".

SDK, posthog-js `f8eaea26`:
- `packages/ai/package.json:79`: peer `"openai": "^6.48.0"`, marked optional at `:107`. The optional peer arrived in 8.0.0 (#3739). Every earlier line bundles `openai` ^5 or ^6 as a hard dependency. No published `@posthog/ai` from 5.0 on supports `openai` v4.

## Suggested fix

1. context-mill, `context/skills/ai-observability/references/2-install.md`: add a Node rule next to the pinned-major rule. Read the `openai` peer range of the current `@posthog/ai`. If the manifest's `openai` major is below it, do not install `@posthog/ai` with `--legacy-peer-deps` or `--force`, and do not pin a pre-8.0 `@posthog/ai`. Pick `manual-capture` instead, and say in the report that the wrapper needs `openai` 6 and that upgrading it is the user's call.
2. context-mill, `4-verify.md`: add a check that the wrapper and the app load the same vendor SDK major (for example `npm ls openai` shows one major), and require the report to name the major the wrapped client runs.
3. Wizard: make the program prompt agree with the skill on who installs. Either drop "The skill itself will install packages" from `src/lib/programs/ai-observability/index.ts:52` and scope the pi install guidance, or change the skill to allow one install attempt with an `ERESOLVE` fallback like `integration-v2/install.md:38`.
4. wizard-workbench: have the node-weather evaluator fail a run that ends with two `openai` majors in the lockfile or a `@posthog/ai` below 8.0.

Widening the `@posthog/ai` peer range to `openai` v4 (posthog-js `packages/ai/package.json:79`) is an option only if the wrapper is tested against v4. That call belongs to the posthog-js AI SDK owners.

issues.title: Technical blog post idea: How is PostHog making its warehouse self-driving?
issues.body:
## Summary
I noticed one of Lizzie's Q3 goals included [a technical blog for the warehouse team](https://github.com/PostHog/requests-for-comments-public/issues/571) on **Self-driving warehouse**, and I know someone ([me](https://www.linkedin.com/in/olasunkanmi-fafowora/)) who has a good handle on explaining complex topics like these and turning them into simple language.

The current [PostHog Warehouse doc](https://posthog.com/docs/data-warehouse) says _"when a materialised view stops refreshing, the failure becomes a [signal](https://posthog.com/docs/self-driving/inbox/sources) for [Self-driving](https://posthog.com/docs/self-driving)..._, that is, a signal is sent when a materialised view breaks; it also paints the picture that a human will fix and re-run it at the end of the day. 

But the official [Self-driving documentation](https://posthog.com/self-driving) describes the agent in a loop action where it investigates the product data, looks for issues, opens a PR, proposes changes, and all you have to do is _merge_ for the human side.

I'm actually now curious about how they both work together to fit the warehouse team's implementation, and I have a couple of questions in order for this article to bang. But I do have some proposed headlines, an outline and who our target audience is, before writing

**Target reader**: Product engineers and developers interested in data warehouse infrastructure, data warehouse reliability, and agent-driven product workflows

**Intended reader reaction**: "I now understand what it means by a Self-driving warehouse, how the relevant workflow functions, and what the data warehouse engineering team set out to solve."

End note: Rereading [Jina's tips for new writers](https://posthog.com/handbook/content/newsletter-tips) and discovered I didn't perform an important task during my technical content writer application, which was to "_before you write anything...have 2–3 issues with some preliminary research_", I may have jumped the gun and wrote a [blog post about my experiments and failures using PostHog's platform](https://sunkanmi.hashnode.dev/preview/6aa6b9949ad9aae35e3e5eff) (particularly Session Replay). I know it's not a requirement, but I'm doing it anyway.

## Headline options
- How we're making PostHog warehouse self-driving
- What happens when your data warehouse starts investigating its failures?
- Your warehouse stopped refreshing! Here's what happens next
- How PostHog's self-driving solves your data warehouse failures for you

## What (if any) keywords are we targeting?
`self-driving data warehouse`, `AI-powered data warehouse`, `data pipeline monitoring`, `PostHog Self-driving data warehouse`, `materialized view refresh failures`

## Outline (optional)
If all goes well, my initial outline would look like this:
1. What the warehouse engineering team set out to solve initially
2. Signals available when something goes wrong
3. How does PostHog's self-driving workflow investigate the problem
4. What happens after workflow diagnosis: suggested fixes or human intervention
5. How PostHog verifies the problem is solved
6. What we learned while building the system

## More questions
1. What does the term "self-driving warehouse" mean in the context of your work?
2. Is the blog post about using warehouse data to drive your product's improvement or is it about the warehouse's own reliability or is it about both?
3. What actions are actually _automated_? Is it when the agent investigates warehouse failures and gives feedback or is it when the agent proposes changes/fixes or is it both?
4. Is there a _really good_ example, PR, implementation, or incident that one can use to anchor the article?
5. Where exactly does the agent run? Only when a failure occurs? And why doesn't the agent fix the errors automatically?
6. What was the hardest technical problem or even a tradeoff the warehouse team encountered while building this workflow?
7. Lastly, has the article been assigned to somebody else? (fingers crossed)

issues.body:
## Problem

MCP servers that accept alternative argument names (for example `experimentId` for `id`) want to measure which spelling agents use. Without SDK support, each server adds its own `$mcp_*` property with its own format, so analytics cannot rely on one contract.

## Proposal

- Let `getToolInputProperties` (and automatic tool-call capture) accept a server-owned alias map, for example `{ experimentId: 'id' }`.
- Emit `$mcp_input_aliases_used`, for example `["experimentId:id"]`, only for aliases the map declares, so unknown names stay hidden behind `[redacted]`.
- Agree the public API change here before the PR.

Follow-up from review on #5048.
