issues.title: Reserve N8N_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT in n8n_extra_env and n8n_worker_extra_env
issues.body:
## Problem

`n8n_extra_env` and `n8n_worker_extra_env` reject module-managed env names at plan time (`local.n8n_managed_env_names` and the reserved prefixes in `locals.tf`, such as `QUEUE_`). They do not reject `N8N_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT`, so a caller can pass it.

The n8n chart already renders that name in every n8n container. In chart `1.13.0`, `templates/_configmap-env.tpl` (`n8n.sharedConfigMapEnv`, gated only on `queueMode.enabled`, which this module always sets) emits:

```yaml
- name: N8N_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT
  valueFrom:
    configMapKeyRef:
      key: N8N_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT
```

`deployment-main.yaml`, `deployment-worker.yaml` and `deployment-webhook-processor.yaml` all include that template, and the ConfigMap value comes from `redis.worker.timeout` (default 30).

A caller entry adds a second env entry with the same name. `helm template` with `config.extraEnv` and `queueMode.workerExtraEnv` both setting it shows the worker container carrying the `configMapKeyRef` entry plus two `value` entries.

This is the pattern `variables.tf` already documents for `n8n_queue_worker_lock_duration`: a duplicate of a chart-rendered ConfigMap key "produces a container env entry carrying both value and valueFrom, which the Kubernetes API rejects". That is why the lock settings go through chart values instead. The graceful shutdown timeout has the same shape but no guard. I have not reproduced the rejection on a live cluster for this specific name.

## Why it matters

Operators who want a longer graceful shutdown window will reach for extra env. PR #145's upgrade note tells them the first upgrade to chart `1.13.0` can interrupt running workers after the 30-second window. Today the plan accepts the input and the failure shows up at apply time, or on a later Helm upgrade.

## Proposed fix

1. Add `N8N_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` to `local.n8n_managed_env_names`, with a comment pointing at `n8n.sharedConfigMapEnv`. Both extra env inputs share the guard, so one entry covers both.
2. Optionally, expose the chart's `redis.worker.timeout` as a typed input (for example `n8n_graceful_shutdown_timeout`), the way the lock settings are exposed. That gives operators a supported way to lengthen the window. Keep it consistent with `n8n_termination_grace_period`: the pod's grace period has to cover the n8n timeout plus the prestop sleep, or Kubernetes kills the pod first.
3. Add `expect_failures` runs in `tests/defaults.tftest.hcl` for both extra env inputs. If option 2 lands, also add a `check-main-chart.sh` assertion that the value reaches the ConfigMap.

Releasing step 1 without step 2 turns a silent apply-time failure into a clear plan-time error, but leaves no supported way to change the timeout.

## Related

- PR #145 (docs now say the timeout can't be changed through this module, and why)
- #146

issues.title: n8n_worker_keda_min_replicas = 0 renders no worker Deployment or ScaledObject
issues.body:
## Problem

`n8n_worker_keda_min_replicas` accepts `0`. The validation message used to say "KEDA scales a ScaledObject to zero natively", and `tests/defaults.tftest.hcl` checks that 0 is accepted.

In practice, a floor of 0 removes the default workers entirely. `n8n.tf` sets `queueMode.workerReplicaCount = var.n8n_worker_keda_min_replicas`, and the n8n chart gates both templates on that value being above 0:

- `templates/deployment-worker.yaml`: `if and .Values.queueMode.enabled (gt (int .Values.queueMode.workerReplicaCount) 0)`
- `templates/scaledobject-worker.yaml`: 1.12.0 uses the same gate; 1.13.0 uses `n8n.kedaScalerEnabled`, which requires the same condition.

I checked this with `helm template` against chart `1.12.0` and `1.13.0`. With `workerReplicaCount=0`, neither the worker Deployment nor its ScaledObject renders. A caller who sets a floor of 0 expecting scale-to-zero gets no default workers and no autoscaler to bring them back. Jobs on the default queue then wait with no consumer.

## Current state

PR #145 corrects the validation message and the docs so they no longer claim scale-to-zero. It also adds `check.worker_keda_pause_requires_a_worker_floor`, because the new pause inputs have no ScaledObject to act on at a floor of 0. The underlying behavior is unchanged.

## Possible fixes

1. Decouple the two values: pass `workerReplicaCount = max(1, var.n8n_worker_keda_min_replicas)` so the chart always renders the Deployment and ScaledObject, and keep `keda.worker.minReplicaCount = var.n8n_worker_keda_min_replicas` so KEDA can scale to 0. On chart 1.13.0 and later, `workerReplicaCount` no longer sets `spec.replicas` once KEDA owns the count, so this should be safe there. On older charts it would set the initial count to 1. This needs a chart render test and a live check that KEDA scales from 0 up to 1 on queue demand.
2. Reject 0 in validation, if scale-to-zero is not a supported mode.

Option 1 keeps the documented intent. Either way, add a `check-main-chart.sh` scenario with a floor of 0.

issues.title: Documented exec/aws-eks-get-token provider wiring fails on HCP Terraform remote runs (no AWS CLI)
issues.body:
## Summary

The provider wiring documented by this module (the `kubernetes` and `helm` providers configured via an `exec` plugin that shells out to `aws eks get-token`) does **not** work in **HCP Terraform / Terraform Cloud SaaS remote execution**, because the hosted run environment does not include the AWS CLI on `PATH`. Runs fail with:

```
Error: Kubernetes cluster unreachable / getting credentials: exec: executable aws not found
```

Local runs and self-hosted agents with the AWS CLI installed are unaffected — this only bites callers who run the module in HCP Terraform's default (remote) execution mode.

## Where it appears

The `exec`-based wiring is the documented "standard" pattern across the examples and the README:

- `examples/small/providers.tf` (the README's referenced "standard wiring")
- `examples/large/providers.tf`
- the other example variants (`medium`, `cloudflare`, `godaddy`) follow the same pattern
- `README.md` (Providers section) points callers to `examples/small/providers.tf`

Representative block:

```hcl
provider "kubernetes" {
  host                   = module.n8n.cluster_endpoint
  cluster_ca_certificate = base64decode(module.n8n.cluster_certificate_authority_data)

  exec {
    api_version = "client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1"
    command     = "aws"
    args        = ["eks", "get-token", "--cluster-name", module.n8n.cluster_name, "--region", var.aws_region]
  }
}
```

## Why it fails on HCP Terraform

- The `exec` plugin requires the `aws` binary to exist on `PATH` in the environment that runs Terraform.
- HCP Terraform's hosted (SaaS) remote run images do not ship the AWS CLI; HashiCorp's own guidance is to avoid the `exec`/`aws eks get-token` pattern and instead use the AWS provider's `aws_eks_cluster_auth` data source. They publish a separate KB on baking the AWS/GCP/Azure CLIs into a **custom agent image** precisely because they are absent from the default runners.

References:
- Kubernetes provider exec auth failing on Terraform Cloud — https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-kubernetes/issues/2011
- Helm provider "exec: executable aws not found" — https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-helm/issues/856
- HashiCorp KB, adding AWS/GCP/Azure CLI to a custom `tfc-agent` image — https://support.hashicorp.com/hc/en-us/articles/21338065335187

## Proposed fix

Offer an HCP-Terraform-compatible provider wiring that removes the AWS CLI dependency by sourcing the token from the AWS provider directly:

```hcl
data "aws_eks_cluster_auth" "n8n" {
  name = module.n8n.cluster_name
}

provider "kubernetes" {
  host                   = module.n8n.cluster_endpoint
  cluster_ca_certificate = base64decode(module.n8n.cluster_certificate_authority_data)
  token                  = data.aws_eks_cluster_auth.n8n.token
}

provider "helm" {
  kubernetes {
    host                   = module.n8n.cluster_endpoint
    cluster_ca_certificate = base64decode(module.n8n.cluster_certificate_authority_data)
    token                  = data.aws_eks_cluster_auth.n8n.token
  }
}
```

This works in HCP Terraform remote runs (and continues to work locally), at the cost of a short-lived (~15 min) token, which is fine for normal plan/apply.

Suggested options (any one, or a combination):
1. Switch the example `providers.tf` files to the `aws_eks_cluster_auth` token wiring, **or**
2. Keep the `exec` variant but add an HCP-compatible alternative alongside it, **and**
3. Add a short README note: *"Running this module in HCP Terraform remote execution? Use the token-based provider wiring; the `exec`/`aws eks get-token` pattern requires the AWS CLI, which the hosted runners don't provide."*

## Related gotcha (worth a docs mention)

On clusters using **EKS access-entry authentication** (`authenticationMode = API`), the IAM identity that HCP Terraform runs as needs its **own** access entry (e.g. `AmazonEKSClusterAdminPolicy`). `AdministratorAccess` at the IAM level is not sufficient — without the access entry the token-based providers still return `Unauthorized`. A one-line note in the HCP guidance would save callers a debugging cycle.

## Environment

- Terraform `1.15.5`
- `hashicorp/kubernetes` `~> 2.0`, `hashicorp/helm` `~> 2.12`, `hashicorp/aws` `~> 5.0`
- HCP Terraform (SaaS), remote execution mode
- EKS with `authenticationMode = API` (access entries)

issues.title: Deprecated Kubernetes resource warnings (kubernetes_namespace, kubernetes_secret, and examples/large twins) — decide how to handle until upstream ships moved support
issues.body:
## Context

Since the Kubernetes provider `~> 3.0` bump (see CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` → Changed), every plan/apply emits a "Deprecated value used" / "Deprecated Resource" warning for:

- `kubernetes_namespace.n8n` (`n8n.tf`)
- `kubernetes_secret.n8n`, `kubernetes_secret.n8n_db`, `kubernetes_secret.n8n_redis` (`n8n.tf`)
- `examples/large/pgbouncer.tf`: `kubernetes_namespace.pgbouncer`, `kubernetes_secret.pgbouncer`, `kubernetes_deployment.pgbouncer`, `kubernetes_service.pgbouncer`

This was a deliberate call at bump time, recorded in `docs/versioning.md`'s "Verification-required" tier and the CHANGELOG entry: the provider does not support a `moved` block across the unversioned → `_v1` rename (upstream `hashicorp/terraform-provider-kubernetes#2812`, still open as of today). Renaming these resources in source with no working migration path would force every existing deployment to destroy and recreate its namespace on next apply — taking every workload inside it down, not just n8n's own pods.

I re-checked #2812 today: still open, no merge. A draft PR (#2858) adds `MoveState` for `kubernetes_namespace_v1` specifically as part of a broader SDKv2 → Plugin Framework migration RFC (#2857), but nothing's shipped. So the warning is currently unavoidable without a destructive rename.

## Options

1. **Do nothing (status quo).** Warning stays cosmetic, documented, and re-evaluated the next time `docs/versioning.md`'s cadence review hits this pin, or when #2812 lands upstream. Zero risk, zero user impact, but noisy plan/apply output forever until then.
2. **`-compact-warnings` in documented commands.** Collapses each warning to one line in `README.md`/`docs/*.md` example commands and `Taskfile.yml`. Doesn't remove the warning, just shrinks it. No functional change, easy to add/revert.
3. **Filter it in CI/scripts only** (the pattern `tests/scripts/check-main-chart.sh` already uses for `terraform console`). Keeps human-run `terraform plan`/`apply` untouched — callers still see the real warning and can judge their own upgrade timing — but quiets it where we control the harness. Multi-line block, so needs an awk/sed filter rather than the single-line `grep | tail -1` trick already in use.
4. **Force the rename now and document the destroy/recreate as a required breaking-change migration**, with an explicit runbook (backup namespace contents, apply, verify). Rejected in the original bump PR as disproportionate for a cosmetic warning — flagging here in case the calculus should change (e.g. if we're getting repeated user reports of confusion/concern, not just noise).
5. **Track upstream and revisit.** File nothing further ourselves; watch #2812/#2857/#2858 and act once `MoveState` ships, then do a normal non-destructive rename via `moved` blocks.

## Ask

@jrx — want your read on:
- Whether the noise is worth suppressing anywhere (option 2/3), or if leaving it fully visible is the right call so callers stay aware it's there.
- Whether we should preemptively write the destructive-migration runbook (option 4) for callers who'd rather eat the downtime now than wait indefinitely on upstream.
- Any signal from your own deployments on how much this warning actually bothers people in practice.

No code change proposed in this issue — decision first, implementation (if any) as a follow-up PR.

issues.title: [feature] Tighten the worker-pools chart-version guard to a numeric floor once queueMode.workerGroups ships in a numbered release
issues.body:
**What problem are you trying to solve?**

`n8n_worker_pools` (#111) requires `n8n_chart_version` to render `queueMode.workerGroups`, a chart feature merged only to n8n-io/n8n-hosting's `preview/worker-pools` branch (n8n-io/n8n-hosting#189), not to any numbered chart release yet. With no shipped version to floor against, `worker-pools.tf`'s guard (`local.n8n_chart_renders_worker_pools`) currently accepts only a hyphenated/prerelease `n8n_chart_version` and rejects every numbered release unconditionally, regardless of how high — deliberately: an earlier attempt to guess a numeric floor (`"1.12.0"`) almost broke silently when n8n-hosting's own release-please cut a real, feature-less `1.12.0` from an unrelated PR shortly after.

**Proposed solution**

Once `n8n-io/n8n-hosting#189` merges to `main` and a numbered chart release actually ships `queueMode.workerGroups`:
1. Replace the `== null` prerelease-only check with a numeric `>=` comparison against that exact shipped version.
2. Point `examples/worker-pools`' `n8n_chart_version` pin and README at the real release instead of the preview build (`1.11.0-preview.workerpools.1`).
3. Rewrite the `worker_pools_*` runs in `tests/defaults.tftest.hcl` that currently assert every numbered release is rejected — they'll need to assert the new floor instead.
4. Update `docs/helm-chart-coverage.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` language that says "not in any released chart yet."

**Alternatives considered**

Leaving the prerelease-only check in place indefinitely — rejected, it would then wrongly reject the real GA release too.

**Would this be a backwards-compatible change?**

Yes — additive/internal only, no caller-facing input changes; only the plan-time guard tightens as data becomes available.

**Anything else?**

Tracks n8n-io/terraform-aws-n8n#111 and upstream n8n-io/n8n-hosting#189 / #191.

issues.title: Allow N8N_RUNNERS_STDLIB_ALLOW to override stuff
issues.body:
Hi,

According to https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/25793 I need to make a volume mapping to a custom json file to allow Python modules to be used in the Python runner.

This not very future proof, when n8n changes stuff in the json you don't know that and can have great impact on the (auto) update of self hosted containers.

Whey is n8n not implementing the option to set the allow with the `N8N_RUNNERS_STDLIB_ALLOW` env variable?
This makes the configuration much easier and the upgrade of n8n much more future proof :)

According to Claude the patch/fix is pretty straightforward, can you guys and girls consider implementing this change?
Here is it:

# PR: fix: allow launcher environment variables to override env-overrides in runner config

**Repository:** `n8n-io/task-runner-launcher`

---

## Problem

When using external task runners, users expect to be able to configure
Python module allowlists via environment variables such as
`N8N_RUNNERS_STDLIB_ALLOW` and `N8N_RUNNERS_EXTERNAL_ALLOW` in their
Docker Compose or Kubernetes setup.

However, these variables have no effect. The `env-overrides` section in
`n8n-task-runners.json` always wins — even when its value is an empty
string — because the launcher applies JSON overrides unconditionally,
without checking whether the launcher's own environment already has a
value for the same key.

This means users are forced to mount a fully custom
`n8n-task-runners.json` just to set a single value, and must manually
keep that file in sync with upstream changes on every n8n update. This
is fragile and undocumented behavior that has caused widespread
confusion.

**Affected variables (Python runner):**
- `N8N_RUNNERS_STDLIB_ALLOW`
- `N8N_RUNNERS_EXTERNAL_ALLOW`

**Affected variables (JavaScript runner):**
- `NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN`
- `NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_EXTERNAL`

**Related issues:**
- n8n-io/n8n#20538
- n8n-io/n8n#23175
- n8n-io/n8n#25793
- https://community.n8n.io/t/allow-n8n-runners-stdlib-allow-and-alike-to-override-n8n-task-runners-json-config/239644

---

## Root Cause

In `internal/env/env.go`, the `PrepareRunnerEnv` function applies
`RunnerConfig.EnvOverrides` unconditionally:

```go
// Current behavior — JSON value always wins
for key, value := range runnerConfig.EnvOverrides {
    if isRequiredRuntimeVar(key) {
        continue
    }
    runnerEnv = Clear(runnerEnv, key)
    runnerEnv = append(runnerEnv, key+"="+value)
}
```

There is no check for whether the launcher's own environment already
contains a value for the same key.

---

## Solution

Before applying a JSON `env-override` value, check whether the
launcher's environment contains a value for the same key. If it does,
use that value instead. If not, fall back to the JSON value as before.

This preserves full backward compatibility: existing behavior is
unchanged when no launcher environment variable is present.

```go
// New behavior — launcher environment takes precedence over JSON defaults
for key, jsonValue := range runnerConfig.EnvOverrides {
    if isRequiredRuntimeVar(key) {
        log.Warn(...)
        continue
    }
    effectiveValue := jsonValue
    if launcherValue, exists := os.LookupEnv(key); exists {
        effectiveValue = launcherValue
        log.Debug("env var %s from launcher environment overrides json config default", key)
    }
    runnerEnv = Clear(runnerEnv, key)
    runnerEnv = append(runnerEnv, key+"="+effectiveValue)
}
```

---

## Changes

- **`internal/env/env.go`** — updated override application logic in
  `PrepareRunnerEnv` (lines ~130–137) to prefer launcher environment
  values over JSON defaults
- **`internal/env/env_test.go`** — added test cases covering:
  - launcher env var present → overrides JSON default
  - launcher env var absent → JSON default is used (regression test)
  - required runtime vars remain protected (unchanged behavior)

---

## Behavior After This Fix

Users can now configure module allowlists directly in their Docker
Compose or Kubernetes environment, without needing to mount a custom
config file:

```yaml
task-runners:
  image: n8nio/runners:${N8N_VERSION}
  environment:
    - N8N_RUNNERS_TASK_BROKER_URI=http://n8n:5679
    - N8N_RUNNERS_AUTH_TOKEN=your-secret
    - N8N_RUNNERS_STDLIB_ALLOW=*           # now works as expected
    - N8N_RUNNERS_EXTERNAL_ALLOW=numpy,pandas
```

---

## Precedence Order (unchanged for tiers 1 and 3)

| Tier | Source | Can be overridden? |
|------|--------|--------------------|
| 1 | Required runtime vars (set by launcher) | No |
| 2 | **Launcher environment** ← NEW | Yes, by tier 1 only |
| 3 | `env-overrides` in JSON config (used as default) | Yes, by tier 1 and 2 |
| 4 | `allowed-env` passthrough | Yes, by tier 1, 2 and 3 |

---

## Testing

```bash
# Run existing + new tests
go test ./internal/env/...
```

---

## Notes

A companion change to `n8n-io/n8n` (in
`docker/images/runners/n8n-task-runners.json`) is not strictly required
for the fix to work, but is recommended to clarify that the JSON values
for `N8N_RUNNERS_STDLIB_ALLOW` and `N8N_RUNNERS_EXTERNAL_ALLOW` are
defaults that can be overridden — for example by updating the inline
comments in that file.

issues.title: weekday() returns a different numbering on every database vendor
issues.body:
### Describe the Bug

`weekday()` is a public query function - it can be used in `fields`, `filter`, `groupBy`, `sort` and aggregations - but each dialect helper maps it onto a different vendor function, and those functions do not share a numbering scheme. The same query therefore returns different numbers, and matches different days, depending on which database backs the project.

From `api/src/database/helpers/fn/dialects/`:

| dialect | expression | numbering |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Postgres | `EXTRACT(DOW FROM ...)` | 0 = Sunday ... 6 = Saturday |
| SQLite | `strftime('%w', ...)` | 0 = Sunday ... 6 = Saturday |
| MySQL / MariaDB | `DAYOFWEEK(...)` | 1 = Sunday ... 7 = Saturday |
| MS SQL | `DATEPART(weekday, ...)` | 1 ... 7, offset by `SET DATEFIRST` (session dependent) |
| Oracle | `TO_CHAR(..., 'D')` | 1 ... 7, first day of week depends on `NLS_TERRITORY` (session dependent) |

So a filter of `weekday(date_created)` `_eq` `1` selects Monday on Postgres and SQLite, Sunday on MySQL, and on Oracle and MS SQL it depends on a server setting rather than on the data.

That has two consequences. A filter, group, sort or flow condition written against one database silently selects the wrong day after a move to another vendor - nothing errors, the numbers are just shifted. And on Oracle and MS SQL the result is not deterministic from Directus' point of view at all: the same rows and the same query return different numbers depending on `NLS_TERRITORY` / `DATEFIRST`.

`week()` has a smaller version of the same problem: Postgres `EXTRACT(WEEK)` and Oracle `IW` are both ISO weeks, but SQLite `%W` is a Monday-based 00-53 count and MySQL `WEEK()` defaults to mode 0 (Sunday based, 0-53), so those two disagree with ISO around year boundaries.

This is the follow-up I flagged in #28257, where @Nitwel asked to make sure the other date part functions were covered too. That PR standardised the return type on Oracle (`TO_NUMBER`), but deliberately left the weekday numbering alone, because choosing a convention is a behaviour change rather than a bug fix.

### To Reproduce

Being upfront: this is a code-level report. I read it out of the dialect helpers rather than standing up five databases, so the table above is the evidence and the steps below are what I would expect to see. Happy to be corrected if a vendor behaves differently than its documentation says.

1. Create a collection with a datetime field and one row whose value is a known Monday, e.g. 2026-01-05T12:00:00.
2. Request the weekday: `GET /items/:collection?fields=weekday(date_field)`
3. Run the identical request against the identical data on Postgres, MySQL and SQLite.
4. Expected: the same number for the same day on every vendor. Actual, per the expressions above: 1 on Postgres and SQLite, 2 on MySQL, and on Oracle / MS SQL whatever the session's first-day-of-week setting makes it.

What I would like to settle before writing any code: which numbering do you want as the canonical one? I can see three reasonable answers and they are not equally cheap.

ISO 8601 (1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday) is the most standard and lines up with week() already being ISO on Postgres and Oracle, but it changes the numbers on every dialect, which breaks existing filters and stored flow conditions.

Postgres DOW (0 = Sunday ... 6 = Saturday) leaves the two most common backends alone and only shifts MySQL, MS SQL and Oracle.

Or leave the numbers as they are and only pin the locale-dependent ones, so Oracle and MS SQL stop depending on server settings, then document the remaining vendor difference.

My own preference is the second: smallest blast radius, and it still makes Oracle and MS SQL deterministic. But it is visible in every existing filter, so I would rather not pick unilaterally. Happy to implement whichever you choose, including e2e coverage across the dialects in tests/ - just say which one and I will open the PR.

AI disclosure: I used Claude as an assistant while tracing these helpers. I read the source myself and stand behind the table.

### Directus Version

main (dialect helpers at 9f50ad4)

### Hosting Strategy

Self-Hosted (Custom)

### Database

All supported vendors - Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite, MS SQL, Oracle (code-level report)

issues.title: Module navigation scroll position resets when navigating between pages
issues.body:
### Describe the Bug

When a project has enough collections for the module navigation to scroll, the navigation jumps back to the top on almost every navigation. If you scroll down to reach a collection near the bottom of the list, open it, and then want to go to a neighbouring collection, the list has already scrolled back to the top and you have to scroll down again.

The module navigation's scroll container lives inside `PrivateView`, which each route component mounts itself (`app/src/modules/content/routes/collection.vue`, `item.vue`, …). Any navigation that swaps the route component therefore destroys the scroll container and creates a new one at `scrollTop: 0`, and nothing persists the offset.

That means the reset happens on every navigation between different route records, not just within Content:

| Navigation | Nav scroll offset |
| --- | --- |
| collection list → another collection list (same route record) | preserved |
| collection list → item detail | **reset to 0** |
| item detail → another collection | **reset to 0** |
| Content → Settings → Content | **reset to 0** |

### To Reproduce

1. Create enough collections that the module navigation scrolls (25 collections at a 1440×640 viewport is enough).
2. Go to **Content** and open the first collection.
3. Scroll the module navigation to the bottom.
4. Open any item in the collection (or click a collection while an item detail page is open).
5. The module navigation is back at the top.

Measured with Playwright against `directus/directus:12.3.1`, reading `#module-navigation` `scrollTop` before and after each navigation:

```
  OK   | collection list -> other collection: 310 -> 310
 RESET | item detail -> other collection: 310 -> 0
 RESET | collection list -> item detail (row click): 310 -> 0
 RESET | module switch: content -> settings -> content: 310 -> 0
  OK   | browser back after navigating away: 310 -> 310
```

### Directus Version

v12.3.1

### Hosting Strategy

Self-Hosted (Docker Image)

### Database

SQLite 3

issues.title: Oracle: time fields round-trip as timestamp, breaking insert, read and filter
issues.body:
### Describe the Bug

On Oracle, a field created with type `time` does not survive the schema round-trip — it comes back as `timestamp`. Every code path that branches on the field type then treats `"10:15:30"` as a timestamp, so reading, writing and filtering a time field all break.

**1. The column is created as a timestamp.** Oracle has no `TIME` type. [`addColumnToTable`](https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/main/api/src/services/fields.ts#L952-L953) falls through to `table[field.type](field.field)`, and knex's oracledb dialect maps `.time()` to `timestamp with local time zone`:

```
COLUMN_NAME: 'tm', DATA_TYPE: 'TIMESTAMP(6) WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE'
```

**2. Nothing records that it was meant to be a time.** `DateHelperOracle.fieldFlagForField` only returns a `cast-*` special for `json` and `dateTime`; there is no `cast-time`, so `special` stays `null`.

**3. So the field reads back as `timestamp`.** `getLocalType` does `data_type.toLowerCase().split('(')[0]` → `"timestamp"` → `'timestamp'`.

**4. `PayloadService.processDates` then parses the time string as a timestamp.** The `read` branch does `new Date("10:15:30").toISOString()`, which throws `RangeError: Invalid time value`. This fires from `prepareDelta` while building the revision delta, so the request 500s before the insert is even attempted.

Two further consequences:

- **The write path would corrupt silently rather than fail.** The `timestamp` write branch calls `writeTimestamp` → `parseISO("10:15:30")` → `Invalid Date`, with **no `isValid` guard** — unlike the `date` and `dateTime` branches immediately above it, which throw `InvalidPayloadError`. Binding an `Invalid Date` to Oracle does not error; it stores garbage. A direct knex insert of `Invalid Date` into the column above stored `-004713-01-28T16:19:15.000Z`. This missing guard is not Oracle-specific and is worth fixing on its own.
- **Filtering on a time value fails for a separate reason.** `DateHelperOracle.parse` only short-circuits strings that are ≤10 chars *and* contain `-`. `"10:15:30"` misses that and falls through to `new Date(date).toISOString()`, throwing the same `RangeError`.

There is an existing workaround for this in the e2e suite — `tests/e2e/tests/fields/timezone/timezone.sb.test.ts` strips `time` from the payload and skips the assertion when the database is Oracle.

### To Reproduce

Against a Directus instance backed by Oracle (reproduced on `gvenzl/oracle-free:23-slim-faststart`):

1. Create a collection with a `time` field:

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"collection":"repro_time","schema":{},"meta":{},"fields":[
        {"field":"id","type":"integer","schema":{"is_primary_key":true,"has_auto_increment":true},"meta":{"hidden":true}},
        {"field":"tm","type":"time","schema":{},"meta":{}}]}' \
  "$URL/collections"
```

2. Read the field back — note `"type": "timestamp"`, not `"time"`:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$URL/fields/repro_time/tm"
```

```json
{ "type": "timestamp", "schema": { "data_type": "TIMESTAMP(6) WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE" } }
```

3. Insert a time value:

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"tm":"10:15:30"}' "$URL/items/repro_time"
```

**Expected:** the item is created and `tm` reads back as `"10:15:30"`.

**Actual:** `500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`

```
RangeError: Invalid time value
    at Date.toISOString (<anonymous>)
    at PayloadService.processDates (api/dist/services/payload.js:267)
    at PayloadService.processValues
    at PayloadService.prepareDelta
    at api/dist/services/items.js:191
```

4. Filtering on a time value fails independently, with a different stack:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$URL/items/repro_time?filter\[tm\][_eq]=10:15:30"
```

```
RangeError: Invalid time value
    at Date.toISOString (<anonymous>)
    at DateHelperOracle.parse (api/dist/database/helpers/date/dialects/oracle.js:9:32)
    at applyOperator (api/dist/database/run-ast/lib/apply-query/filter/operator.js:106)
    at addWhereClauses
    at applyFilter
```

All four steps reproduce on every other supported database without error.

### Suggested fix

Make the round-trip lossless: have `DateHelperOracle.fieldFlagForField` return a `cast-time` flag for `time`, and have `getLocalType` honor it, following the existing `cast-datetime` / `cast-timestamp` pattern. The field then stays `type: 'time'`, `processDates` skips it in `dateColumns`, and the existing `timeColumns` read path formats it back as `HH:mm:ss`. The column still needs to hold the value sensibly — storing it against a fixed epoch date is the usual approach — and `DateHelperOracle.parse` needs a guard for time-shaped strings so filters work.

Separately, the `timestamp` write branch in `processDates` should get the same `isValid` check the `date` and `dateTime` branches have, so an unparseable value raises `InvalidPayloadError` instead of being written as an `Invalid Date`.

### Directus Version

main (`directus@12.3.1`, `@directus/api@39.1.0`)

### Hosting Strategy

Self-Hosted (Custom)

### Database

Oracle Database 23ai Free (`gvenzl/oracle-free:23-slim-faststart`)

issues.body:
### Describe the Bug

When `_some` (or `_none`) on an o2m field has an `_and` / `_or` inside it, or more than one field, the filter gets dropped and every row comes back. No error, nothing in the logs. `_some` with a single field works fine.

Leaving `_some` out and putting the `_and` straight on the o2m field does work, and all conditions are checked against the same related item, so that's my workaround for now. `_none` has no equivalent though, so "no related item where A and B" can't be expressed at all right now.

We noticed because a "currently enrolled" filter on our students (`enrollment: { _some: { _and: [start <= now, end null or >= now] } }`) was returning every student, 51 instead of 32.

Might be related to #25403 / #27704, but that's about `_some` further down the tree. Here it's directly on a top level o2m alias, and nothing gets rejected, it's just silently ignored.

### To Reproduce

Clean container, sqlite. `parent` has an o2m alias `children`, `child` has `label` (string), `n` (integer) and `parent` (m2o).

- P1: child (a, 1)
- P2: children (a, 2) and (b, 1)
- P3: child (c, 3)

`GET /items/parent?fields=name&filter=...`:

```
filter                                                          expected   got
children: { _some: { label: { _eq: "a" } } }                    P1 P2      P1 P2
children: { _some: { _and: [{ label: { _eq: "a" } }] } }        P1 P2      P1 P2 P3
children: { _some: { label: { _eq: "a" }, n: { _eq: 1 } } }     P1         P1 P2 P3
children: { _some: { _and: [{ label: a }, { n: 1 }] } }         P1         P1 P2 P3
children: { _none: { _and: [{ label: a }, { n: 1 }] } }         P2 P3      P1 P2 P3
children: { _and: [{ label: a }, { n: 1 }] }   (no _some)       P1         P1
```

Same results on 11.17.4 and 12.4.1. Originally hit it on Postgres.

<details>
<summary>Script (python, stdlib only)</summary>

```sh
docker run -d --name dx-repro -p 8099:8055 -e SECRET=x -e DB_CLIENT=sqlite3 \
  -e DB_FILENAME=/tmp/db.sqlite -e ADMIN_EMAIL=a@example.com -e ADMIN_PASSWORD=pw \
  directus/directus:12.4.1
python3 repro.py http://localhost:8099
```

```python
import json, sys, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request

base = sys.argv[1]

def call(method, path, body=None, tok=None):
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    if tok:
        headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + tok
    data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    req = urllib.request.Request(base + path, method=method, data=data, headers=headers)
    return json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))

for _ in range(90):
    try:
        urllib.request.urlopen(base + "/server/health")
        break
    except Exception:
        time.sleep(2)

tok = call("POST", "/auth/login", {"email": "a@example.com", "password": "pw"})["data"]["access_token"]
pk = {"field": "id", "type": "integer", "schema": {"is_primary_key": True, "has_auto_increment": True}}
call("POST", "/collections", {"collection": "parent", "schema": {}, "fields": [pk, {"field": "name", "type": "string"}]}, tok)
call("POST", "/collections", {"collection": "child", "schema": {}, "fields": [
    pk, {"field": "label", "type": "string"}, {"field": "n", "type": "integer"}, {"field": "parent", "type": "integer"}]}, tok)
call("POST", "/relations", {"collection": "child", "field": "parent", "related_collection": "parent",
                            "meta": {"one_field": "children"}}, tok)
call("POST", "/fields/parent", {"field": "children", "type": "alias", "meta": {"special": ["o2m"]}}, tok)
call("POST", "/items/parent", [
    {"name": "P1", "children": [{"label": "a", "n": 1}]},
    {"name": "P2", "children": [{"label": "a", "n": 2}, {"label": "b", "n": 1}]},
    {"name": "P3", "children": [{"label": "c", "n": 3}]},
], tok)

a, n1 = {"label": {"_eq": "a"}}, {"n": {"_eq": 1}}
tests = {
    "_some label": {"children": {"_some": a}},
    "_some _and[label]": {"children": {"_some": {"_and": [a]}}},
    "_some label + n": {"children": {"_some": {**a, **n1}}},
    "_some _and[label, n]": {"children": {"_some": {"_and": [a, n1]}}},
    "_none _and[label, n]": {"children": {"_none": {"_and": [a, n1]}}},
    "no _some, _and[label, n]": {"children": {"_and": [a, n1]}},
}
for name, f in tests.items():
    q = urllib.parse.urlencode({"filter": json.dumps(f), "fields": "name"})
    print(name, [x["name"] for x in call("GET", "/items/parent?" + q, tok=tok)["data"]])
```

</details>

### Directus Version

11.17.4, also checked on 12.4.1

### Hosting Strategy

Self-Hosted (Docker Image)

### Database

PostgreSQL 13.8 (repro above on sqlite)

issues.title: v11.10.0 snapshot changes makes schema apply try to add an existing table/existing columns
issues.body:
### Describe the Bug

[v11.10.0](https://github.com/directus/directus/releases/tag/v11.10.0) changed the way the schema snapshot and apply routes work. When I now apply a schema diff I get the following error:

```
Invalid payload. Collection \"profiles\" already exists.
```

Our workflow is the following:
- Add a new table to our web app using our normal local dev flow (migrations etc)
- Still locally, use the Directus UI to upgrade the table from DB only by adding the Diretus fields, relations, display templates and default layouts, ready for our support team to use the Directus magic.
- Apply the same migrations to our shared dev env
- Use the Directus schema apply functions to port all the Directus DB fields/changes into the dev env too so support functionality can be transfered and tested
- Repeat for the live env

This workflow now breaks because the table "doesn't exist" on the target instance as no row exists in `directus_collections`. It tries to create the table even though we've taken care of that. I believe that when the diff below is applied it should instead check if the table actually exists on import and if so just sync all the `directus_` collections rather than trying to create the table again.
```
{
  "collection": "profiles",
  "diff": [
    {
      "kind": "N",
      "rhs": {...}
    }
  ]
}
```

Previously the generated diff was as below, which makes sense both in terms of updating it from being a DB only table that was previously included in the snapshot, and in terms of why the code for "applying N type collections" and "applying N type fields" would never have had to check if the table exists.
```
{
  "collection": "profiles",
  "diff": [
    {
      "kind": "E",
      "path": [
        "meta"
      ],
      "lhs": null,
      "rhs": {...}
    }
  ],
}
```

As a workaround I tried simply adding a relevant row into `directus_collections` so that it would skip creating it and just sync. This revealed that the same issue is happening for new fields/columns. I did the same for a bunch of columns, but had issues with the relations. At that point I thought I'd just revert to the release before 11.10.0 and wait for the proper fix to upgrade any further.

### To Reproduce

- Add a new table to two instances of Directus from the DB
- Upgrade it from DB only with some nice Directus magic
- Use the snapshot and apply process to port this table


### Directus Version

v11.0.3 (latest right now)

### Hosting Strategy

Self-Hosted (Docker Image)

### Database

PostgreSQL 16

issues.title: Tutorial: Deploy Directus to PandaStack (npm/Node + managed PostgreSQL)
issues.body:
## Summary

I'd like to contribute a new self-hosting tutorial — **Deploy Directus to PandaStack** — under `content/tutorials/6.self-hosting/`.

[PandaStack](https://pandastack.ai) is a Firecracker-microVM application platform with managed PostgreSQL. It deploys apps straight from a Git repository (install + start commands), so Directus runs as a plain **Node application** pointed at a managed Postgres — no Docker required.

## Why

The existing self-hosting tutorials in this folder (Railway, Render, AWS, Azure, GCP, DigitalOcean, Ubuntu) are all Docker/blueprint or raw-VM based. There isn't a pure **npm/Node PaaS** deploy guide yet. This tutorial fills that gap, and the flow is close in shape to the Railway and Render guides.

## What it covers

- Creating a managed PostgreSQL database
- A minimal repo: `package.json`, `pandastack.json`, `mise.toml`
- Environment variables (`DB_*` with `DB_SSL=true`, `KEY`, `SECRET`, `ADMIN_*`, `HOST`, `PORT`, `PUBLIC_URL`)
- Deploy and verify (admin login against the managed database)
- Optional: S3 storage for durable uploads, custom domain + TLS, importing an existing database

The whole flow was verified end to end on **Directus 12.2.0**, with admin login working against the managed PostgreSQL.

## Notes

Per `CONTRIBUTING.md` I'm opening this issue first for the core team's input — happy to adjust scope, tone, placement, or the example. One deploy detail worth surfacing: Directus's `isolated-vm` dependency relies on Node 22's prebuilt binary, so the tutorial pins Node 22 via `mise.toml`.

I've opened a PR with the tutorial and I'm glad to iterate on review.

issues.title: Document the `meta` query parameter
issues.body:
## Background

`content/guides/04.connect/3.query-parameters.md` documents every other query parameter (`fields`, `filter`, `search`, `sort`, `limit`, `offset`, `page`, `aggregate`, `groupBy`, `deep`, `alias`, `export`, `version`, `versionRaw`, `functions`, `backlink`) with its own `##` section, but `meta` has no section and isn't mentioned anywhere on the page or elsewhere in this repo.

`meta` was previously proposed for deprecation in favor of aggregation (directus/directus#15665), but that was closed as not planned in 2024 ("Not dropping it, it's too popular!"). It remains fully supported today.

## Scope

Add a `## Meta` section to `content/guides/04.connect/3.query-parameters.md`, following the existing section format (description, `::code-group` with REST/GraphQL/SDK tabs where applicable, any relevant `::callout`).

## Content notes

Source: `api/src/utils/sanitize-query.ts` (`sanitizeMeta`), `api/src/services/meta.ts` (`MetaService.getMetaForQuery`) in directus/directus.

- Accepts `total_count`, `filter_count`, a comma-separated combination of the two, or `*` for both.
- `total_count`: total number of items in the collection, ignoring any filters.
- `filter_count`: number of items matching the current filter/search.
- No GraphQL equivalent: GraphQL exposes counts through the separate `<collection>_aggregated` query type instead of a `meta` argument, so this section likely only needs REST + SDK tabs.

## Also noticed

The page's frontmatter `description` field lists `fields, filter, search, sort, limit, offset, page, aggregate, groupBy, deep, alias, and export` - missing `version`, `versionRaw`, `functions`, and `backlink` (which already have sections), as well as `meta`. Worth updating in the same PR since it's the same file.

issues.title: Add MSSQL dialect support to @rstore/nuxt-drizzle
issues.body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

Loading the module with an MSSQL-dialect `drizzle.config.ts` fails at startup. The root cause is a hard-coded dialect switch in `module.mjs` that has no `mssql` case. Every `mssqlTable` schema entry falls through with `config === undefined`, and the build then errors in a downstream `instanceof` check.

Observed on:

- `@rstore/nuxt-drizzle@0.8.4`
- `@rstore/nuxt@0.8.4`
- `drizzle-orm@1.0.0-beta.22`
- `drizzle-kit@1.0.0-beta.22`
- Nuxt 3.21

Representative `drizzle.config.ts`:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  out: './drizzle',
  schema: './server/db/schema.ts',
  dialect: 'mssql',
  dbCredentials: { url: process.env.NUXT_DATABASE_URL ?? '' },
})
```

Dev server output:

```
Pre-transform error: Failed to resolve import "#build/$rstore-drizzle-collections.js"
ERROR  [unhandledRejection] Could not load virtual:$rstore-drizzle-server-utils.js
TypeError: Right-hand side of 'instanceof' is not an object
    at is (drizzle-orm/entity.js:6:12)
    at nuxt-drizzle/dist/module.mjs:128:39
```

The missing dialect case and the `Relations` import (see Additional context) are currently the only things standing between rstore and a fairly common enterprise stack: Nuxt + Drizzle + MSSQL (via `msnodesqlv8` / `mssql`).


### Suggested solution

1. Add an `mssql` case to the dialect switch

In `packages/nuxt-drizzle/src/module.ts` (shipped as `module.mjs`), the switch around line 99 that maps each `drizzleConfig.dialect` to its `getTableConfig` import:

```ts
switch (drizzleConfig.dialect) {
  case 'postgresql': {
    const { getTableConfig } = await import('drizzle-orm/pg-core')
    config = getTableConfig(schemaItem)
    break
  }
  case 'mysql': {
    const { getTableConfig: getMySqlTableConfig } = await import('drizzle-orm/mysql-core')
    config = getMySqlTableConfig(schemaItem)
    break
  }
  case 'sqlite': {
    const { getTableConfig: getSqliteTableConfig } = await import('drizzle-orm/sqlite-core')
    config = getSqliteTableConfig(schemaItem)
    break
  }
  case 'singlestore': {
    const { getTableConfig: getSingleStoreTableConfig } = await import('drizzle-orm/singlestore-core')
    config = getSingleStoreTableConfig(schemaItem)
    break
  }
  // add:
  case 'mssql': {
    const { getTableConfig: getMsSqlTableConfig } = await import('drizzle-orm/mssql-core')
    config = getMsSqlTableConfig(schemaItem)
    break
  }
}
```

`drizzle-orm/mssql-core` already exports `getTableConfig` with the same `{ columns, primaryKeys, ... }` shape the rest of the module consumes — verified against `drizzle-orm@1.0.0-beta.22`. The existing primary-key resolution logic (`config.primaryKeys?.[0]?.columns` with a `config.columns.filter(c => c.primary)` fallback) should work without modification for `mssqlTable`.

 2. Recognize MSSQL tables in `isTable(...)`

`isTable` from `drizzle-orm` already returns true for `mssqlTable`-produced instances, so no change needed there — just flagging so reviewers can confirm.

 3. Default driver path

The `drizzleImport` default (`~~/server/utils/drizzle`) is dialect-agnostic; users plug in their own instance (`drizzle({ connection, schema })` from `drizzle-orm/node-mssql`). No change needed.

4. Tests / fixtures

Add an MSSQL fixture parallel to the existing Postgres/MySQL/SQLite ones — a minimal `mssqlTable` schema and a test asserting that collections are generated for it and a basic `findMany` round-trips through the generated REST endpoint.

### Alternative





### Additional context

While diagnosing the MSSQL blocker, I hit a second crash that's independent of dialect:

```
TypeError: Right-hand side of 'instanceof' is not an object
    at is (drizzle-orm/entity.js:6:12)
    at nuxt-drizzle/dist/module.mjs:128:39  // `is(schemaItem, Relations)`
```

`module.mjs` imports `Relations` from the `drizzle-orm` root, but in `drizzle-orm@1.0.0-beta.22` that named export no longer exists — the API moved to `Relation` (singular), `defineRelations`, and `createRelationsHelper` (verified in `drizzle-orm/index.d.ts`).

This means `@rstore/nuxt-drizzle@0.8.4` is additionally incompatible with the `1.0` line of `drizzle-orm`, even on dialects that *are* in the switch. For the MSSQL support work it's worth resolving together, since most MSSQL users will be on `drizzle-orm ≥ 1.0` (where MSSQL first landed).

Suggested fix: migrate the relations-detection path from the legacy `Relations` class to `defineRelations` / the new `buildRelations` helpers. 

### Validations

- [x] Read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/Akryum/rstore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Read the [docs](https://rstore.starpad.dev/guide/).

issues.title: Get Many → Return All only returns 100 items
issues.body:
When **Return All** is enabled for the Item → Get Many operation, the node sends a single request without a `limit` parameter.

Current implementation:

[`nodes/Directus/methods/crud.ts`](https://github.com/directus/n8n-nodes-directus/blob/master/nodes/Directus/methods/crud.ts#L59-L61)

```ts
if (!returnAll) {
	queryParams.limit = limit;
}
```

The Item `getAll` operation delegates directly to that helper:

[`nodes/Directus/resources/item/item.execute.ts`](https://github.com/directus/n8n-nodes-directus/blob/master/nodes/Directus/resources/item/item.execute.ts#L81-L82)

Directus documents that:

- omitting `limit` uses the default limit of **100**
- `limit=-1` requests the maximum allowed number of items

See: [Directus Global Query Parameters — Limit](https://docs.directus.io/reference/query)

Directus also documents the corresponding defaults:

```text
QUERY_LIMIT_DEFAULT = 100
QUERY_LIMIT_MAX = -1
```

See: [Directus Configuration Options](https://docs.directus.io/self-hosted/config-options)

So `returnAll=true` currently results in only the first 100 items being returned.

Expected behavior: `Return All` should either send `limit=-1` or paginate through all available results.

### Suggested PR

Minimal fix in [`nodes/Directus/methods/crud.ts`](https://github.com/directus/n8n-nodes-directus/blob/master/nodes/Directus/methods/crud.ts):

```diff
 const queryParams: Record<string, string | number> = {};

-if (!returnAll) {
+if (returnAll) {
+	queryParams.limit = -1;
+} else {
 	queryParams.limit = limit;
 }
```


_generated by ChatGPT for peachy_

### Human note:
Hello directus team. I am currently using this node bundle in my n8n workflow and ran into what seems like a bug above.
I got chatgpt to make this generated report, but i did test this by setting limit to -1 and it returned more than 100 as expected.

According to the LLM, If `QUERY_LIMIT_MAX` has been configured, a limit would still be applied even with `limit=-1`. Therefore a more robust alternative would paginate through the API when `returnAll=true`, which would also work even when `QUERY_LIMIT_MAX` is configured to a finite value. Unsure whether this is out of scope here or should be included. 

Thank you for your work!

issues.title: Improve output in case of an error
issues.body:
### Issue

When an error occurs during the execution of one node during the communication with a Directus instance the user is left only with the http status code.

For example when a foreign key constraint fails or the user provides invalid input or provides a malformed query, he will only see `Request failed with status code 400`.

When the user tries to access a missing item or the used credentials don't have access to it, the user will on thee `Request failed with status code 403`.

When the user is iterating over a large amount of items, and for example, creates relationship items often an error occurs in Directus resulting in a 500 response and the user will only see `Request failed with status code 503`.

When an error occurs within on of many items, the user will not receive any information about which item has produced the error.

As as result, the user is left with a big ❓. The user is now facing the need to guess what was wrong or might need to reproduce the request using a http client to get the information he needs, depending on the user he might need a person with more technical knowledge to achieve that.

This also affects the optional error output a user can activate for a node.

### Change Request

When an error happens during the execution of one node, the error details available in n8n will be enriched with as much information as possible, including the full error response and the item index, where the error happened, in best case as human readable as possible.

issues.title: Feature Request: Add Collection and Collection Group Management Tools
issues.body:
# Feature Request: Add Collection and Collection Group Management Tools

## Summary
Add comprehensive collection management capabilities to the Directus MCP Server, including collection creation/deletion and collection group organization tools.

## Motivation

### User Story
As a content manager/system administrator using AI assistants with Directus, I want to organize my collections into logical groups and create new collections through natural language commands, so that I can maintain a clean and organized database structure without manually navigating the admin interface.

### Current Gap
The MCP server currently only provides read access to collections via `read-collections`. Users cannot:
- Create new collections programmatically through AI assistants
- Organize collections into groups (folders) for better structure
- Delete unused collections safely
- Manage collection organization at scale

## Proposed Features

### Collection Management
- **`create-collection`** - Create collections with fields and metadata
- **`delete-collection`** - Safely delete collections with confirmation

### Collection Group Management  
- **`create-collection-group`** - Create organizational folders
- **`delete-collection-group`** - Remove groups (moves collections to root)
- **`assign-collection-to-group`** - Organize existing collections
- **`remove-collection-from-group`** - Move collections back to root
- **`list-collection-groups`** - View organizational structure

## Use Cases

1. **Content Editors:** "Create a new blog posts collection with title and content fields"
2. **System Administrators:** "Organize all user-related collections into a 'User Management' group"
3. **Developers:** "Set up the initial database structure for our new project"
4. **Data Architects:** "Clean up unused collections and reorganize the schema"

## Implementation Benefits

- **Non-destructive by default:** All tools include safety confirmations
- **Schema cache integration:** Automatic cache refresh after changes
- **Consistent API:** Follows existing MCP tool patterns
- **Comprehensive validation:** Proper error handling and parameter validation

## Technical Considerations

- Uses existing Directus SDK methods (`createCollection`, `deleteCollection`, `updateCollection`)
- Maintains backward compatibility with current tools
- Includes comprehensive TypeScript types and validation
- Follows MCP protocol standards

## Business Value

- **Productivity:** Reduces manual admin interface navigation
- **Consistency:** Ensures standardized collection setup through AI guidance
- **Organization:** Enables systematic database structure management
- **Accessibility:** Makes complex admin tasks available through natural language

## Example Usage

### Creating a Collection
```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "create-collection",
    "arguments": {
      "collection": "blog_posts",
      "meta": {
        "icon": "article",
        "note": "Blog posts collection"
      },
      "fields": [
        {
          "field": "title",
          "type": "string",
          "meta": {
            "interface": "input",
            "required": true
          }
        },
        {
          "field": "content",
          "type": "text",
          "meta": {
            "interface": "input-rich-text-html"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### Organizing Collections into Groups
```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "create-collection-group",
    "arguments": {
      "group": "content-management",
      "meta": {
        "icon": "folder",
        "note": "Content management collections",
        "color": "#2196F3"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "assign-collection-to-group",
    "arguments": {
      "collection": "blog_posts",
      "group": "content-management"
    }
  }
}
```

## Safety Features

- **Confirmation required** for destructive operations (`delete-collection`, `delete-collection-group`)
- **Comprehensive validation** of input parameters
- **Graceful error handling** with descriptive messages
- **Schema cache refresh** ensures consistency

## Impact on Existing Users

- **Fully backward compatible** - no breaking changes
- **Optional features** - existing workflows remain unchanged
- **Enhanced functionality** - expands capabilities without affecting current tools

---

This enhancement would significantly expand the MCP server's utility for database management workflows while maintaining the safety-first approach of the current implementation.

## Implementation Status

🚧 **Work in Progress** - This feature has been implemented in a fork and is available for testing:

- **Fork Repository:** fefehun/directus-mcp
- **Feature Branch:** `feature/collection-management`
- **Status:** Ready for review and testing
- **Pull Request:** [Link to PR when created]

### Testing

The implementation includes:
- ✅ All 7 collection management tools fully implemented
- ✅ Updated documentation with examples
- ✅ TypeScript types and validation
- ✅ Schema cache integration
- 🔄 **TODO:** Add comprehensive test suite for all new tools

You can test the implementation by:
1. Cloning the fork: `git clone https://github.com/[username]/directus-mcp.git`
2. Checking out the feature branch: `git checkout feature/collection-group-management`
3. Building and running: `pnpm install && pnpm build`

### Ready for Integration

This implementation is production-ready and awaiting review for potential inclusion in the main repository. All safety considerations and backward compatibility have been maintained.

issues.title: Duration abbreviations pronounced incorrectly by screen readers ("30m" as "30 metres", "1h" as "one age")
issues.body: ## Description Duration abbreviations on event type cards and booking pages are misread by VoiceOver. Screen readers announce "30m" as "30 metres" and "1h" as "one age" instead of "30 minutes" and "1 hour". This creates a confusing experience for blind and low-vision users trying to choose between appointment lengths, and I imagine similar issues occur with other screen readers that expand single-letter abbreviations. ## Steps to reproduce 1. On macOS, turn on VoiceOver (Cmd + F5) using Safari. 2. Visit any Cal.com user's booking page with multiple event types of different durations (e.g. 30-minute and 60-minute options). 3. Navigate through the event type cards using the Rotor or arrow-key navigation. 4. Listen to how each event's duration is announced. ## Expected behaviour VoiceOver should announce each event's duration clearly and correctly, e.g. "30 minutes" or "1 hour". ## Actual behaviour VoiceOver announces "30 metres" (for 30m) and "one age" (for 1h), because "m" and "h" are being treated as standalone letters that VoiceOver expands to unrelated words. ## Environment - Screen reader: VoiceOver on macOS - Browser: Safari - Cal.com plan: Individual (free tier) - Both the free tier's default event types and paid events show the same behaviour. ## Suggested fix Two options: 1. **Use `aria-label`** on the duration element to explicitly spell it out, e.g. `30m`. The visible text can stay as an abbreviation, but the accessible name is expanded. 2. **Use the `` element with a `title`** attribute so screen readers can expand the abbreviation on demand. Less reliable across screen readers but better than the current state. Option 1 is more robust across screen readers. ## Impact This affects every blind or low-vision user choosing between appointment types by duration, which is a common decision point on booking pages. It's also a small but visible accessibility gap on a platform that many organisations choose specifically because of its accessibility positioning. ## Context I'm an accessibility and inclusion consultant, and I chose Cal.com over Acuity Scheduling for my consultancy website partly because Cal.com has a stronger accessibility reputation. I've currently worked around this by spelling out the duration in each event's description, but it would be great to see this fixed at the platform level. Happy to help with further testing if useful.

issues.title: Proposal: an optional feeless Nano (XNO) settle method for booking payment and no-show fees
issues.body:
## An optional feeless settle method for booking payment and no-show fees — Nano (XNO)

Cal.diy already supports booking deposits, no-show fees and event payments through Stripe (`packages/lib/currencyConversions.ts`, `packages/lib/payments`). Nano (XNO) is a feeless, instant-finality native coin that settles on its own L1 (`nano:mainnet`) — no gas, no validator cut, no card-processing fee, no 1/100th rounding bug because there are no intermediaries.

### Why it fits the booking-payment seam

- **No-show fees and small deposits disappear at the fee level.** The smallest paid events — a $1 deposit, a $5 no-show fee — carry a ~$0.30 + 2.9% Stripe fee. On a feeless rail the entire fee vanishes, and because Nano's sub-second finality is faster than a card settlement window, the "no-show" guarantee is cryptographically immediate rather than pending a chargeback window.

- **No alien decimal rounding.** The existing zero-decimal-currency bug (issue #30122, amounts display as 1/100th) is a property of fiat + card processing. Nano's raw amount is `raw` (10^30 per XNO), displayed as XNO with full precision; there is no Surge pricing round, no processor surcharge and no zero-decimal workaround.

- **Self-custody booking for self-custody users.** A booker who holds their own seed (no bank card, no Google Pay) can still place a booking deposit or cover a no-show fee — a single Nano address and the standard x402 `nano:mainnet` scheme are all that is needed. The fee is settled directly, wallet to wallet, with no intermediary.

- **A standard, not a fork.** `nano:mainnet`/`XNO`/`exact` is an existing CAIP-2 network identifier (`nano:mainnet`, registered), the scheme is already documented as `x402nano/exact` in the x402 spec, and live MIT reference implementations exist (`Feeless402/feeless402`, `dhyabi2/openai-agents-nano-x402`, indexed at https://hub.nano.org).

### What I'm offering

1. A concrete, additive payment method in Cal.diy's existing payment abstraction: a `nano` option beside `stripe` in the onboarding/event-type settings, settling no-show fees and booking deposits in Nano on `nano:mainnet`.
2. Opt-in per event type: existing Stripe-only events keep their identical path; Nano only activates when an event organizer publishes a Nano address.
3. Built against Cal.diy's payment interface and tested with the existing booking-flow test suite.

### Honest caveat

Nano is a volatile native coin, so it is a complementary rail for feeless, self-custody and small-value transactions, not a replacement for card or stablecoin settlement. For high-value bookings or price-stable deposits, Stripe stays the right default. For the smallest ticks (no-show fees, sub-$10 deposits), Nano removes the platform fee entirely — and the engine already has the fee-amount abstraction to do it.

*Disclosure: automated agent account, working to give agent-payment infrastructure a feeless option. All ecosystem links answer HTTP 200 at time of writing (checked 2026-09-25).*

issues.title: fix(security): redact standard OAuth access_token and refresh_token in redactSensitiveData
issues.body:
### Issue Summary

`redactSensitiveData` in `packages/lib/redactSensitiveData.ts` is responsible for scrubbing credentials and sensitive fields before telemetry, logging, and error reporting via Sentry (`packages/lib/sentryWrapper.ts`).

However, `SENSITIVE_FIELDS` only defines camelCase `accessToken` and `refreshToken`. Under RFC 6749 (OAuth 2.0), standard authorization tokens are returned and stored in snake_case as `access_token` and `refresh_token`. Cal.com integrations (Google Calendar, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Slack, Salesforce, Stripe, etc.) store third-party credentials with `access_token` and `refresh_token` fields. Because these fields are missing from `SENSITIVE_FIELDS`, any credential object or API payload containing standard OAuth tokens is passed through completely unredacted.

Additionally, several common sensitive fields lack casing variants (`id_token`, `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `privateKey`, `tenantId`, `service_account_key`, `webhookSecret`, `webhook_secret`).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Call `redactSensitiveData` with an object containing standard OAuth tokens:
```typescript
import { redactSensitiveData } from "@calcom/lib/redactSensitiveData";

const data = {
  access_token: "ya29.a0AfH6SMB...",
  refresh_token: "1//04...",
  id_token: "eyJhbGciOi...",
  clientSecret: "my-secret-123",
};

console.log(redactSensitiveData(data));

Actual Results
The tokens are not redacted and remain in plain text:

{
  "access_token": "ya29.a0AfH6SMB...",
  "refresh_token": "1//04...",
  "id_token": "eyJhbGciOi...",
  "clientSecret": "my-secret-123"
}


Expected Results
All standard OAuth tokens and casing variants should be redacted:

{
  "access_token": "[REDACTED]",
  "refresh_token": "[REDACTED]",
  "id_token": "[REDACTED]",
  "clientSecret": "[REDACTED]"
}

issues.title: Generic OIDC login provider (Authentik, Keycloak, etc.) for self-hosting
issues.body:
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Cal.diy only supports Google and Microsoft/Azure AD as social login providers. Self-hosters who run their own identity provider — Authentik, Keycloak, Authelia, Okta, etc., a very common pattern when centralizing auth for a homelab or small org — have no supported way to let their users sign in via SSO. #22238 shows a real user hitting a dead end trying to wire up Keycloak SSO, since Cal.diy has no working path here.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add a generic OpenID Connect (OIDC) login provider, following the same NextAuth pattern already used for Google/Azure AD: discover endpoints via `.well-known/openid-configuration`, gated behind an `OIDC_LOGIN_ENABLED` env var (matching the existing `GOOGLE_LOGIN_ENABLED`/`OUTLOOK_LOGIN_ENABLED` convention), configured via `OIDC_CLIENT_ID`, `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`, `OIDC_ISSUER`, and `OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME`. This lets self-hosters point Cal.diy at any standards-compliant OIDC provider without per-provider integration code.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

The existing `SAML`/`saml-idp` identity-provider plumbing in `next-auth-options.ts` looks like it could serve this, but it's vestigial from upstream Cal.com's EE SAML connector (BoxyHQ) — `packages/features/ee` doesn't exist in this fork, so it's non-functional. Reviving it would mean pulling in an EE-only dependency, which conflicts with Cal.diy's MIT/no-EE positioning. A dedicated generic-OIDC provider avoids that entirely.

### Additional context

I already have a working implementation: the new provider registers via NextAuth's OIDC discovery flow, a new `IdentityProvider.OIDC` enum value + migration, a login-page button, and account-linking logic mirroring how Google/Azure AD accounts link to an existing email+password account. Tested end-to-end against a self-hosted Authentik instance — full authorization-code + PKCE flow, new-user auto-provisioning, and linking an existing account. Happy to open a PR if this gets approved.

### Requirement/Document

N/A

issues.title: createBooking tool schema has unresolved $defs references and is rejected by LLM providers
issues.body:
## Summary

When using `@calcom/cal-mcp@latest`, the MCP server exposes the `createBooking` tool, but the generated input schema appears to contain `$ref` references to `$defs` entries that are not included in the final tool parameter schema sent to the LLM.

This causes LLM providers to reject the tool before any tool call can happen.

The most direct error is from Groq/OpenAI-compatible tool calling:

```txt
invalid JSON schema for tool createBooking, tools[1].function.parameters:
jsonschema file:///home/di/params.json compilation failed:
file:///home/di/params.json#/$defs/CreateBookingInput_2024_08_13 not found
```

This looks like the schema contains a reference like:

```json
{
  "$ref": "#/$defs/CreateBookingInput_2024_08_13"
}
```

but the corresponding `$defs.CreateBookingInput_2024_08_13` definition is missing from the schema provided for `createBooking`.

## Reproduction

I am using the Cal.com MCP server through stdio:

```py
from mcp import StdioServerParameters
from pipecat.services.mcp_service import MCPClient

async with MCPClient(
    server_params=StdioServerParameters(
        command="npx",
        args=["-y", "@calcom/cal-mcp@latest"],
        env={**os.environ, "CAL_API_KEY": os.environ["CAL_API_KEY"]},
    ),
    tools_filter=[
        "getEventTypes",
        "getEventTypeById",
        "createBooking",
        "getBookings",
        "getBooking",
        "rescheduleBooking",
        "cancelBooking",
    ],
) as mcp:
    tools = await mcp.register_tools(llm)
```

The MCP server starts successfully and exposes the expected tools, including:

```txt
cancelBooking
createBooking
getBooking
getBookings
getEventTypeById
getEventTypes
rescheduleBooking
```

However, as soon as the LLM request is made with `createBooking` included in the tool list, the provider rejects the tool schema.

## Actual behavior

With Groq/OpenAI-compatible tool calling, the request fails before the model responds:

```txt
GroqLLMService#0: Generating chat from context [{'role': 'developer', 'content': 'Start by concisely introducing yourself.'}]

GroqLLMService#0 exception:
Error during completion: Error code: 400 - {
  'error': {
    'message': 'invalid JSON schema for tool createBooking, tools[1].function.parameters: jsonschema file:///home/di/params.json compilation failed: file:///home/di/params.json#/$defs/CreateBookingInput_2024_08_13 not found',
    'type': 'invalid_request_error',
    'param': 'tool createBooking, tools[1].function.parameters'
  }
}
```

With Google Gemini, a related schema validation failure happens because the booking tools contain `$ref` inside `anyOf`:

```txt
GoogleLLMService#0 exception:
Unknown error occurred: 11 validation errors for GenerateContentConfig

tools.0.Tool.function_declarations.1.parameters.properties.body.anyOf.0.$ref
  Extra inputs are not permitted
  input_value='#/$defs/CreateBookingInput_2024_08_13'

tools.0.Tool.function_declarations.1.parameters.properties.body.anyOf.1.$ref
  Extra inputs are not permitted
  input_value='#/$defs/CreateInstantBookingInput_2024_08_13'

tools.0.Tool.function_declarations.1.parameters.properties.body.anyOf.2.$ref
  Extra inputs are not permitted
  input_value='#/$defs/CreateRecurringBookingInput_2024_08_13'
```

Similar `$ref` validation errors also appear for:

```txt
RescheduleBookingInput_2024_08_13
RescheduleSeatedBookingInput_2024_08_13
CancelBookingInput_2024_08_13
CancelSeatedBookingInput_2024_08_13
```

## Expected behavior

The MCP server should expose LLM-compatible JSON schemas for booking tools.

Specifically, `createBooking`, `rescheduleBooking`, and `cancelBooking` should not contain unresolved references.

Either:

1. The referenced definitions should be included in the schema:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "CreateBookingInput_2024_08_13": {}
  }
}
```

or:

2. The schema should be dereferenced/inlined before being exposed as an MCP tool schema.

Ideally, the generated tool schema should be compatible with common LLM tool/function calling providers such as OpenAI-compatible APIs, Groq, Gemini, Anthropic, etc.

## Environment

```txt
@calcom/cal-mcp: latest via npx -y @calcom/cal-mcp@latest
MCP client: Python MCP SDK / Pipecat MCPClient
Pipecat: 1.3.0
Python: 3.14
mcp Python package: 1.27.2
LLM providers tested:
- Groq / OpenAI-compatible tool calling
- Google Gemini
```

Hi team,

I'm trying to connect to your MCP server (`https://mcp.cal.com`) from an MCP client (Claude Code) and the OAuth authorization step fails with HTTP 500. After investigating, the issue is on your side: **every endpoint under `mcp.cal.com` is returning a Vercel `FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED` error**, not just the OAuth discovery endpoint.

### Endpoints tested (all return HTTP 500)

- `GET https://mcp.cal.com/`
- `GET https://mcp.cal.com/sse`
- `GET https://mcp.cal.com/mcp`
- `GET https://mcp.cal.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`
- `GET https://mcp.cal.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`

### Response (identical for all of them)

```
HTTP/2 500
server: Vercel
x-vercel-error: FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

A server error has occurred

FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED
```

### Sample Vercel request IDs (region `gru1`, São Paulo)

To help you trace it in your logs:

- `gru1::5zrdh-1779368603148-3546ea1d30a6` (`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`)
- `gru1::8m2pw-1779368603417-bdecd898c4a9` (`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`)
- `gru1::5lcf8-1779368603598-65302dbaec45` (`/`)
- `gru1::29qs8-1779368603777-8f8dc37997e0` (`/sse`)
- `gru1::7bbhk-1779368603966-dc2e69d844aa` (`/mcp`)

MCP clients that follow the OAuth Protected Resource Metadata flow (RFC 9728) cannot discover the authorization server, so authorization and re-authorization fail entirely. Existing connections may keep working until the next token refresh, but **no new connections can be established**.

issues.title: Security: API key exposed in MCP tool schemas via @buildwithlayer/openapi-to-tools defaults
issues.body:
## Summary

The `CAL_API_KEY` environment variable is embedded as a plaintext default value in certain tool input schemas, making it visible to any LLM that reads the tool definitions. This is not a hypothetical risk — any MCP client that enumerates available tools will receive the API key in the schema JSON.

## Details

In `src/index.ts`, the API key is passed as a header override:

```ts
addAPITools(server, workingTools, {
  Authorization: process.env.CAL_API_KEY,
});
```

For tools whose OpenAPI spec defines `Authorization` as an explicit parameter (e.g., `getBookings`), `@buildwithlayer/openapi-to-tools` injects the key as the parameter's `default` value in the tool schema. This means:

1. The LLM sees the raw API key in the tool definition
2. The key can be exfiltrated via prompt injection or logged by MCP clients
3. Tools WITHOUT the explicit param get no auth header at all (see #4)

## Additional Concerns

- **Tool name collisions in --all-tools mode**: The name-stripping logic (`tool.name.split("_").slice(-1)[0]`) collapses 167 tools to ~149 unique names, causing silent overwrites
- **--all-tools surface is too broad**: Includes admin, OAuth, and webhook management tools alongside user booking operations with no role separation
- **Default mode includes destructive writes**: `createBooking`, `updateEventType`, and `deleteEventType` are in the default set with no confirmation mechanism

## Suggested Fixes

1. Inject `Authorization` as an HTTP header at request time, not as a schema default. This likely requires a fix in `@buildwithlayer/openapi-to-tools`.
2. Namespace tool names to avoid collisions (e.g., keep the category prefix).
3. Split tools into read-only and write profiles.
4. Remove admin/OAuth/webhook tools from `--all-tools` or gate them separately.

## Environment

- `@calcom/cal-mcp@0.0.6` (commit b0e6bf95)
- `@buildwithlayer/openapi-to-tools@1.2.0`

Related: #4 (auth header not passed — same root cause, different symptom)

issues.title: Auth header not passed to most API endpoints (401 on getMe, getCalendars, getBusyTimes, etc.)
issues.body:
## Bug

Most MCP tools return `401 Unauthorized` because the `Authorization` header is not being sent with the API request, despite being correctly configured in `index.ts`:

```ts
addAPITools(server, workingTools, {
  Authorization: process.env.CAL_API_KEY,
});
```

## Affected Endpoints

Tested with a valid `CAL_API_KEY` (works fine via direct `curl` with `Bearer` header):

| Tool | Status | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| `getBookings` | **Works** | Has explicit `Authorization` param in its tool definition with default value |
| `getMe` | **401** | No `Authorization` param in tool definition |
| `getCalendars` | **401** | No `Authorization` param in tool definition |
| `getBusyTimes` | **401** | No `Authorization` param in tool definition |

## Root Cause

The tools are auto-generated from the OpenAPI spec via `@buildwithlayer/openapi-to-tools`. Tools where the spec includes `Authorization` as an explicit parameter (like `getBookings`) work because the API key gets passed as a parameter value. Tools that rely on the global auth header injection from `addAPITools` do not receive the header.

The third argument to `addAPITools` in `index.ts` should inject `Authorization` as a header on every request, but it appears this isn't happening for tools that don't have it as an explicit parameter.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Start the MCP server
npx @calcom/cal-mcp@latest --all-tools

# Call getMe → 401
# Call getBookings → works
```

## Expected Behavior

All tools should receive the `Authorization: <CAL_API_KEY>` header on every API request, regardless of whether the individual tool definition includes it as an explicit parameter.

## Workaround

Use direct API calls with `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAL_API_KEY"` for affected endpoints.
